532531|2026-09.headline: Strides Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹14,297 million (+17% YoY), with Ex-US overtaking US, but FY28 US $375m aspiration slips beyond FY28.
532531|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record revenue of ₹14,297 million (+17% YoY, +13% QoQ) and record EBITDA of ₹2,509 million, though EBITDA margin fell to 17.6% from 19.0% a year earlier on higher material, freight and logistics costs. Ex-US revenue reached ₹6,963 million (+31% YoY) and exceeded US revenue for the first time, reaching 102% of US revenue in the quarter. US revenue of ₹6,855 million (+9% YoY) recovered sequentially, but management pushed the ~$375 million US revenue aspiration beyond FY28 while keeping the overall FY28 growth ambition intact. Working capital rose ₹307 million in H1 as inventory was built, lifting net debt to EBITDA to 1.72x.

financial_highlights.change: vs 57.8% in Q2 FY26 and 60.9% in Q1 FY27
+8% YoY; margin vs 19.0% in Q2 FY26 and 18.2% in Q1 FY27
+26.4% YoY, includes Pivot Path divestment gain recognised in Q1
net debt up ₹211 crore in H1 on working capital

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹6,855 million ($73 million), +9% YoY and +9% QoQ; H1 ₹13,137 million, +7% YoY. Commercialised portfolio at 75 products after three launches in the quarter; top-three positions in 38 products contributing about 70% of US revenue.

segments.name: Ex-US
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹6,963 million, +31% YoY; H1 ₹12,838 million, +24% YoY. Ex-US was 76% of US in FY25, 90% in FY26 and 102% in Q2 FY27. Growth broad-based across UK, Europe (partnered and German private-label OTC), Nordics, Australia, Francophone Africa and South Africa.

segments.name: Controlled Substances (within US)
segments.commentary: Five commercialised oral solid CS products contribute about 6% of US revenue, addressing a ~$750 million market. Pipeline of more than 10 CS products (nasal sprays, patches, films) targets a ~$4.5 billion addressable market.

guidance_outlook: FY28 overall revenue growth ambition 'firmly in place', but the ~$375 million US revenue aspiration now expected 'a little beyond FY28'.
Management said Ex-US could reach upwards of $375 million in FY28 and expects Ex-US to keep growing faster than the company average.
H2 expected stronger than H1, with 4 to 6 US launches planned and Q3 relaunch of a controlled-substance patch.
Gross margin expected in the 58% to 60% range, with H1's 58.3% described as sustainable.
Net finance cost expected in the ₹40 to ₹45 crore range for H2 FY27.
Capex around ₹300 crore by end FY27; FY28 capex 'slightly lower'.
Net debt to EBITDA expected to stabilise and improve by year end; cash-to-cash cycle expected to improve starting next quarter.
Bottom line expected to grow ahead of top line; trailing ROCE of 14.4%, expected to improve.
Latin America not expected to contribute meaningfully until about FY29-30.
capex_capacity: Capex and intangibles of ₹208 crore deployed in H1 FY27; cash-flow capex about ₹265 crore including ₹60 crore of payments for prior-year investments.
Investments include IP purchases, nasal spray and transdermal patch programmes.
First nasal spray (controlled substance) has a GDUFA goal date in H2 FY27, with approval expected in Q4; third nasal spray filed in September 2026.
Controlled-substance patch relaunch expected in Q3, acquired from Endo ANDAs.
Chestnut Ridge (US) facility has capacity for US-manufactured controlled-substance products.
demand_pricing: US B2B partner business had a strong order book with new wins from a partnered product, recent launches and other molecules; wins expected to show up over coming quarters.
US pricing pressure: US revenue flat in dollar terms YoY, attributed to product mix, price adjustments tied to currency and volume given up; management cited cost improvement plans as an offset.
Drug-shortage opportunities in oral solids have largely normalised; remaining shortages seen mainly in injectables and patches.
Controlled Substances growth constrained by quota allocations, which are set twice a year and have improved progressively; CS share moved from 0% to 6% of US revenue over a couple of years.
Ex-US: shipment delays from Q1 resolved with no spillover into Q2; management said the Q2 level is a new run rate excluding Sandoz.
Sandoz Francophone Africa deal awaiting antitrust approval in a few countries, expected to close in Q3. Multiple new out-licensing deals signed in H1.
Input cost, freight and logistics costs elevated due to the geopolitical situation; management expects alternate sourcing and procurement initiatives to help.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving non-US momentum, and what growth is possible over 2-3 years including Sandoz?
qa_highlights.answer: Badree said growth is broad-based across B2B and B2C markets, with some sub-$30m markets growing fast and $50m+ markets in mid-teens. He expects Ex-US to reach upwards of the $375 million aspiration in FY28, with Sandoz adding scale over 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new US differentiated products contribute meaningfully?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikesh said meaningful contribution is expected in FY28-FY29, a slip of about 3-4 quarters, with the milestone reached by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve sequentially in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikesh said Q4 purchases made at the height of disruption were consumed in Q2 and cost initiatives are now playing out, so 58% margins are sustainable. He said the focus is EBITDA and PAT, with quarter-on-quarter growth over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 aspiration tied to specific products, and why was it deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikesh said it was an aspiration, not guidance, and is broad-based rather than dependent on one product. Reasons: lower shortages in the US and a decision not to launch products below profitability thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Ex-US mix affect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Badree said company gross margin will stay in the 58% to 60% range, and that each Ex-US market should be healthy within that range.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital remain elevated, and what is the finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Badree said cash conversion should improve from the next quarter as inventory normalises. Finance cost is expected at ₹40 to ₹45 crore for H2, versus ₹43 crore in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is Ex-US Q2 a new run rate, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Badree confirmed the Q2 Ex-US level is a new run rate excluding Sandoz. Vikesh said capex is around ₹300 crore by year end and slightly lower in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was US dollar revenue flat YoY, and is the controlled-substance quota gain from market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikesh cited product mix, price adjustments to currency and volumes given up. He said the CS quota gains reflect market share gains rather than market expansion.

risks_watch: US growth slow: $73 million in Q2 and a $375 million aspiration pushed beyond FY28; watch for the H2 recovery and the 4 to 6 launches.
Gross margin at 56.0% in Q2 versus 58.3% in H1; a sustained 58% to 60% range depends on cost initiatives and input prices.
Net debt to EBITDA at 1.72x with working capital up ₹307 million; the debt-free aspiration timing is not explicitly reaffirmed.
Controlled-substance growth depends on twice-yearly quota allocations; the first nasal spray approval is expected in Q4.
Sandoz Francophone Africa deal closing expected in Q3, subject to antitrust approvals.
Obsolescence provisions of about ₹70 crore charged to P&L (presentation change in cash flow statement, per management).
532531|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the Ex-US business and overall growth, but measured and somewhat defensive on the US, where the FY28 aspiration has moved out. Management was specific on margin and working capital recovery timing but offered limited product-level detail on H2 launches.
key_quotes: Our goal was for Ex-US revenue to match the US by FY28, and we have achieved that in Q2 FY27 itself.
The timing has moved; the ambition has not.
We will not compromise on profitability or the quality of our business to chase revenue.
Cash conversion cycle definitely will improve in the coming quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided to 58% to 60% (Q2 at 56.0%, H1 at 58.3%) as Q4 FY26 high-cost purchases were consumed and cost initiatives play out, though EBITDA margin was 17.6% vs 19.0% a year ago.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line is discussed; capex is around ₹300 crore by end FY27 and slightly lower in FY28, with H1 capex and intangibles at ₹208 crore on IP and programme spend, not capacity build-out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ex-US grew 31% YoY to ₹6,963 million and is seen growing faster than the company average, with the Sandoz Francophone Africa close expected in Q3, while US revenue grew only 9% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and management frames capex as steady at about ₹300 crore with FY28 slightly lower, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 stronger than H1 with 4 to 6 US launches and Ex-US at a new run rate of ₹6,963 million (+31% YoY), but no quantified revenue upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The US $375m aspiration has slipped to 'a little beyond FY28' and US revenue was flat in dollar terms YoY at $73m in Q2, though management did not cut revenue guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects 4 to 6 US launches in H2, a Q3 relaunch of the controlled-substance patch from Endo ANDAs, and first nasal spray approval in Q4 after its GDUFA date in H2.

rows.label: Sandoz Francophone Africa deal close
rows.why: Deal awaits antitrust approval in a few countries and is expected to close in Q3, with Sandoz adding Ex-US scale over 1-2 years.

rows.label: US B2B partner order book wins
rows.why: A strong order book with new wins from a partnered product, recent launches and other molecules is expected to show up over coming quarters.

rows.label: Cash conversion and net debt improvement
rows.why: Cash-to-cash cycle expected to improve from next quarter as inventory normalises, after ₹307 million working capital build in H1 that lifted net debt/EBITDA to 1.72x.

tone.note: Management was confident on Ex-US growth, the 58% to 60% gross margin range and cash-conversion recovery, but defensive on the US, where the $375m aspiration slipped past FY28; analysts pushed on the US timing, margin recovery and product-level detail for H2 launches.

532538|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA/ton of INR1,253 (ex-West Asia ~INR1,240), 200 MTPA capacity crossed, dividend INR240/share proposed.
532538|2026-03.overview: UltraTech crossed 200 million tonnes of Indian cement capacity a year ahead of target and completed 100% brand migration for India Cements and Kesoram at end-March 2026. Q4 consolidated volumes were above 44 million tonnes (brand volume up 19% YoY), grey cement prices rose about 2.5% across most geographies, and consolidated EBITDA per tonne was INR1,253 versus INR1,225 in Q4 FY25 (ex-acquired assets INR1,296). West Asia conflict is a headwind on fuel, packing bags (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March), freight and forex mark-to-market (about INR120-130 crore). Management guided 7-8% sustainable volume growth, double-digit volume growth for FY27, and a Board-proposed dividend of INR240 per share for FY26.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,225/t in Q4 FY25 (ex-acquired assets INR1,296/t, vs INR1,225/t)

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per tonne ex-West Asia impact

financial_highlights.change: vs INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3; INR670/t including tolling-booked margin per Q&A
first profit after a long time

financial_highlights.metric: Forex mark-to-market hit on USD 950 million borrowings

financial_highlights.change: bag cost rose from INR9 to INR15 per bag, now about INR13-14

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA INR497/t vs INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3; 2.73 Mt of 3.12 Mt Q4 volume was on UltraTech brand. Management says true economics are about INR670/t after tolling margin booked in UltraTech books, and targets over INR1,000/t by FY28.

segments.name: Kesoram (acquired)
segments.commentary: Already operating at over INR1,000/t EBITDA in Jan-Mar 2026 quarter, in line with southern peers, per CFO.

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: About 5 Mt capacity; EBITDA INR278 crore in Q4 vs INR267 crore in Q3; utilisation recovered from about 80% after drop during the war; all bulk, no bag cost.

segments.name: Cable and wire business
segments.commentary: About INR800 crore of INR1,800 crore capex spent; management indicated launch could come in the first month of Q3 FY27 versus earlier commitment of Q3.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27. Industry growth estimated at 6-7% for Q4 and about 6.5% for FY27.
Capacity: 200 Mtpa crossed; committed further 37 Mt taking capacity above 242.5 Mtpa in phases by FY28; plans beyond 240 Mtpa being developed.
Capex of about INR8,000-10,000 crore every year for the foreseeable future, funded from balance sheet; leverage to stay below 1x net debt/EBITDA after growth capex.
Efficiency programme: INR185/t achieved on nominal basis; target of over INR300/t now expected to be exceeded by FY28.
Clinker factor (cement-to-clinker ratio) target of about 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x; 85% green power target by FY30 (43% today).
capex_capacity: Capacity 200 Mtpa in India (about 196 Mt India capacity mentioned); the acquired India Cements and Kesoram assets make up about 13% of consolidated capacity.
India Cements: INR1,592 crore committed for efficiency improvement plus INR400 crore for capacity expansion; Kesoram: INR400-500 crore cost-improvement capex.
Green energy: 1.8 GW platform; 43% of power from green sources; no thermal capacity to be added, per management, with more WHRS and renewable tie-ups.
Lead distance reduced to 367 km; bulk terminal network expanding including new Lucknow facility.
Capacity utilisation: about 90% across network in Q4 with average above 80%.
demand_pricing: Grey cement prices up about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4 on improved trade mix and premiumisation; cement price hike taken in April 2026 and management expects it to stay.
Trade mix about 65-67%, not diluted; infrastructure share was weaker in Q4 due to end of high-speed rail work in Gujarat.
Bag costs rose from INR9 to about INR15 per bag in March, now about INR13-14; management says price increases already offset about INR6/bag increase.
Fuel: average fuel cost about INR1.77/kcal, may rise to about INR1.8 in June quarter; long-term fuel contracts seen as favourable going forward.
Management sees no supply shortage of bags or pet coke; dispatches unaffected. Demand seen steady; slowdown noted in last 15 days of March around West Bengal and Tamil Nadu elections.
Management attributed cement's relatively muted price hikes versus steel, PVC and agri inputs to industry fragmentation.

qa_highlights.question: Will payout ratio stay high given internal accrual funding of capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is possible if the company and cement market perform well; the Board decides. Capex plan is INR8,000-10,000 crore a year funded from balance sheet with rising operating cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: How much of realisation gain is from brand transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand transition helped significantly since only 0.39 Mt of India Cements' 3.12 Mt Q4 volume was non-UltraTech brand; other operational levers also contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Cost impact of West Asia conflict and June-quarter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental bag cost of about INR90 crore in March, not to be annualised; fuel expected only slightly higher in June quarter; forex mark-to-market about INR120-130 crore charged within EBITDA; diesel impact not yet factored in.

qa_highlights.question: How much more can India Cements EBITDA rise and what share is from cost versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA sits in UltraTech books; INR800/t in India Cements books; further efficiency of about INR200/t still to come, with price increases and operating leverage taking it beyond INR1,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cement lagged other building materials in price hikes, and can costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry fragmentation; said price increases typically come in Q1 of the fiscal and that prices will be raised as costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for merging India Cements and status of legal cases, and RCB ring-fencing?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal cases inherited are old with no movement; merger to follow once risks are resolved. Management said UltraTech's balance sheet has been ring-fenced and no funds have moved for other purposes.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: fuel (pet coke at about USD160/t in the questions), diesel costs not yet factored in, and July-September ripple effects on fuel and bags.
Forex: USD 950 million borrowings fully hedged but marked to market at INR94.85/USD; a sharp rupee move can hit EBITDA (about INR30/t per management).
Whether cement price hikes taken in April 2026 stick given industry-wide cost pressure and monsoon seasonality.
Pace of India Cements EBITDA gains toward INR1,000/t and pending legal cases before further integration/merger of India Cements.
Cable and wire business launch timing (targeted early Q3 FY27) and dividend sustainability beyond FY26.
532538|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and celebratory on FY26 delivery and capacity milestones, but guarded on near-term West Asia cost outlook, repeatedly saying it is too early to quantify diesel and fuel impacts. Evasive on specific dividend payout targets and on India Cements merger timing.
key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.
We are not keeping cash on balance sheet out of uncertainty. We are sharing it because we can and because we have planned carefully enough to do so without any constraint.
Not a penny has moved from UltraTech balance sheet for any other purposes.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA rose from INR305/t in Q3 to INR497/t in Q4 (about INR670/t true economics), efficiency programme at INR185/t vs target over INR300/t now exceeded by FY28, and April 2026 price hike expected to stick; offset by West Asia fuel and bag costs (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March) and INR120-130 crore forex MTM.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 37 Mt committed to take capacity above 242.5 Mtpa in phases by FY28 and under construction, with 200 Mtpa crossed already, but no specific commissioning quarter is given for most of it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27 and 7-8% sustainable, against industry growth of about 6.5% for FY27, with Q4 consolidated volume above 44 Mt and brand volume up 19% YoY, though timing of the push is not tied to commissioning dates.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore a year is already stated as a firm plan, and utilisation is about 90% across the network (average above 80%), so further capacity announcements (plans beyond 240 Mtpa being developed) are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Efficiency target of over INR300/t is now expected to be exceeded by FY28 and price hikes taken in April 2026 are expected to stick, but West Asia diesel and fuel impacts are not yet factored in.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel may rise to about INR1.8/kcal in the June quarter, diesel impact is not yet factored, July-September ripple effects on fuel and bags are flagged, and a sharp rupee move hits about INR30/t on USD 950 million borrowings.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (first month of Q3 FY27 per call wording)
rows.why: Cable and wire business has about INR800 crore of INR1,800 crore capex spent, with launch guided for the first month of Q3 FY27 versus an earlier Q3 commitment.

rows.label: April 2026 cement price hike sticks
rows.why: Grey cement prices rose about 2.5% in Q4 and the April hike is expected to hold, but management flags industry cost pressure and monsoon seasonality as risks.

rows.label: India Cements EBITDA to above INR1,000/t by FY28
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA is INR497/t in Q4 (INR670/t with tolling margin) from INR333/t in Q2, with about INR200/t of further efficiency still to come, and management has committed to this target.

rows.label: India Cements merger
rows.why: Merger to follow only once inherited legal cases are resolved, and management gave no timeline and was evasive on it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 200 Mtpa milestone, brand migration, capex plan and FY27 double-digit volume target, but guarded on West Asia fuel and diesel costs, dividend payout and India Cements merger timing; analysts pushed on India Cements margin gap, pricing pass-through and cost pressure.

532538|2026-06.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27 domestic grey volumes rose 13.1% with EBITDA of INR5,146 crore and PAT up 17.2% to INR2,604 crore despite a fuel and packing cost shock.
532538|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever first quarter across volumes, revenue, EBITDA and profit, with capacity utilisation rising to 81% from 76%. Revenue grew 16%, EBITDA rose 12% and EBITDA per ton held above INR1,200 despite a sharp imported fuel cost increase and packing bag inflation. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton reaching INR603 from INR509 in the prior quarter, and cables and wires remains on schedule for Q3 FY27 launch. Management guided to a INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27 and reaffirmed double-digit volume growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR509 in prior quarter; INR400 earlier; ~INR386 in Q2FY26

financial_highlights.metric: India Cements revenue (ex-factory, net of freight)
financial_highlights.change: +21% vs INR821 crore like-for-like; reported INR1,013 crore vs INR1,021 crore

segments.name: Grey cement (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 13.1%; East slowest in April-June, South and North just under 15%, West and Central above 15%. Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth; industry Q2 growth estimated at 7-8%.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Brand migration to UltraTech 100% complete; EBITDA per ton INR603 and conversion ratio 1.5x. Cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crore; green power to rise from ~3% to ~86% by end FY28. Target INR1,000/ton, with full capex benefit from Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Cables and wires
segments.commentary: Investment program INR1,800 crore, with INR888 crore spent or committed. Commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026). Management sees no further investment needed for now.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: RMC is about 3.5% of UltraTech sales; 477 RMC plants. Institutional customers about 35% and retail 65-66% of sales.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 cost increase of INR130-140 per ton, covering fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage; packing bags and fuel named as Q1 inflation drivers (fuel +INR25-40/t, bags ~INR9 to ~INR12 per bag).
Management expects Q2 prices to hold broadly steady through monsoon; aims for higher prices but says it will see where it lands.
Targets double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27; capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by end FY27 and about 235 million tons by March 2028.
Capex of about INR17,000 crore over the next 2-2.5 years; FY26 capex about INR9,500 crore; all growth capex funded by internal accruals; net debt to EBITDA to stay below 1x this year.
India Cements EBITDA per ton target of INR1,000 with full capex benefit from Q4 FY28; INR1,400/ton timeline referenced for Jan-Mar 2028 without war.
India Cements standalone merger path: capex completion and disposal of non-core land, expected Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity 200.1 million tons after commissioning 8.7 million tons (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu); total capacity 205.5 million tons.
Green power about 1,897 MW (~47% of power needs at quarter end); 71 MW renewables and 19 MW WHRS commissioned in the quarter; target 2.5-3 GW soon.
Cement lead distance down to 360 km from 367 km; AFR substitution ramping up.
Management is drawing up plans beyond 240 million tons; inorganic opportunities to be examined.
Limestone secured for every ton of committed expansion.
demand_pricing: Management cites strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate; urbanisation at about 35%, targeted 39% by 2030.
All-India exit prices improved through June; East and South led, Central and West steady, North consistent.
Cost escalations of past two quarters not fully passed through, supporting price outlook into busy season.
Blended cement and premiumisation supporting realisations; converted B/C category customers to UltraTech at higher price points.
Regional: East slowest in Q1 (elections, labour); East expected to see multi-year demand upcycle, not a next-quarter story.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising operating cash flow be deployed across dividends, cement capex and cables and wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Daga said all operating cash flows are fully booked for growth capex plus dividends; no further cables and wires investment foreseen for now, as that business matures first.

qa_highlights.question: What remains before India Cements can be merged into UltraTech standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex programme to be completed and non-core land to be disposed; completion expected Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier, with some operating parameters still to align.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Jul-Sep quarter, covering fuel, maintenance and operating deleverage; management said it cannot separate war impact from normal seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did limestone mining cost rise 13-14% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial diesel rose from about INR78-80 pre-war to INR150s during the war, and is a major component of limestone mining cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended coal cost trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended coal cost was USD134/ton in the quarter (INR1.9/kcal); current level about INR2/kcal, with inventory loaded so no further rise assumed. Coal now preferred over pet coke on energy-cost basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook and industry growth for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth; industry growth in the June quarter estimated at 7-8% based on internal intelligence.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption keeping fuel, freight and insurance costs high; Q2 FY27 cost increase of INR130-140/t.
Monsoon dry spells (Rajasthan) could weigh on rural demand and water availability; August-September rains to be watched.
Industry capacity additions may be revisited by some players; industry capacity recalibration pending.
India Cements EBITDA per ton of INR603 still well short of INR1,000 target; benefit from capex only from Q4 FY28.
Cables and wires: higher working capital for the next six months; ramp-up after Q3 FY27 launch.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: India Cements EBITDA/t to INR1,000
rows.why: EBITDA/t rose from INR509 to INR603 QoQ and INR400 earlier, against a target of INR1,000 with ~INR2,000 crore cost-improvement capex and full benefit only from Q4 FY28.

532538|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; trade prices exited September ~3% above Q1 average and are about 5% above Q2 average.
532538|2026-09.overview: Management described a quarter where a weak monsoon kept construction active, while a West Asia conflict pushed fuel costs higher. Q2 trade prices averaged roughly 1-1.5% below Q1 on a soft August, but rose sharply in late September and October. Volume growth of 13.8% ran ahead of an industry estimate of about 10%, and net profit rose 21% YoY. Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45, and the company expects the price increases to flow mainly into Q3 earnings.

financial_highlights.change: absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume +13.8%

segments.name: Cement - regions
segments.commentary: North grew over 20% and South 15-20%; East ~5%, West ~10%, Central ~10%. Utilisation was above 70% in North and South, about 70% in West, and about 60% in Central and East.

segments.name: Wires and Cables (Ultravolt)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,800 crores planned capex, of which INR 1,100 crores is spent or committed. Production of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has started; power and control cable lines are due in H2. Management says it is too early to judge revenue or margins; it is a division, not a subsidiary.

guidance_outlook: Trade prices exited September at least ~3% above Q1 average; October prices are about 5% above Q2 average, with management expecting more increases in the next couple of months.
Full benefit of price increases expected in Q3 earnings rather than immediately, given festive-season slowdown.
FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crores (plus or minus), with a fuller view after Q3.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by end-March 2027.
Fuel cost guidance: INR 2.1/kcal may rise to about INR 2.2/kcal, assumed to hold for H2 if pet coke stays near $180/tonne; management expects only a marginal Q4 impact from current inventory.
Business-as-usual delivery of the INR 1,400/tonne EBITDA exit-March-2028 target, with cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Expects industry volume growth of about 8% in H1 FY27 and very strong momentum to March 2029.
Ultravolt: a mature business expected in FY28; April-June 2027 quarter is flagged as one worth discussing.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mtpa in September, taking domestic cement capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield plant at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt of debottlenecking at 3 units.
On track for 240 Mtpa as planned; next phase of organic growth to be announced, with North capacity expansion plans to come before end-FY27.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
Thermal substitution rate about 7.2% after AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants.
Ultravolt plant at Jhagadia (Gujarat); 1 main warehouse, 5 regional distribution centres and about 16 branch warehouses.
India Cement kiln shutdowns planned for upgrades (WHRS, preheater height) with benefits expected from Jan-Mar 2028 quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices were 1-1.5% below Q1 owing to a soft August; prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in the second half of September, with non-trade prices higher.
Mumbai prices rose 3-4% per bag; South showed the strongest momentum in prices, volumes and utilisation.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67%; industry sales were 463 Mt in FY26 against UltraTech's 145 Mt.
Management says the industry is now sold out, so pricing is leading volume.
Domestic coal is constrained because Coal India prioritises the power sector; pet coke was about $180/tonne, and pet coke share was cut to about 25%.
Rural demand may soften in some areas; the company cites weak monsoon, drought in pockets and farm-income risk.
UBS network above 25% of trade sales, with about 6,500 stores targeting 10,000 by FY28-29.
Ultravolt pricing is at market parity; the company says differentiation comes from premium Class 5 HR/FR products.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected in H2 from current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast peaking. The fuel kcal cost may go from INR 2.1 to INR 2.2, which is assumed to hold if nothing else changes; marginal Q4 impact expected from inventory.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the price increase versus the Q2 average?
qa_highlights.answer: Spot realisation is about 5% above the Q2 average, with September and October combined.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose QoQ; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by capex and the dividend payment. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026, and management expects it below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest costs rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crores of NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about 2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ultravolt's capex go beyond INR 1,800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: No sanction beyond INR 1,800 crores. Management says the ramp-up is the focus and that the revenue target could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crores on copper prices, against the earlier INR 10,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will the industry return to pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says pricing is leading, the industry is sold out, and the price increases will cover cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA per tonne target of INR 1,400 hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Business as usual, with cost pressures covered by price increases; management confirmed delivery of the INR 1,400 commitment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: pet coke, imported coal and industrial diesel costs are elevated, and any escalation adds to H2 cost pressure.
Whether October price increases hold through the festive slowdown and are absorbed in Q3.
Rural demand softening after a weak monsoon and drought pockets; household inflation.
Ultravolt: early-stage, with ramp-up, dealer stabilisation and margins unproven; revenue and utilisation not yet disclosed.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; the company targets below 1x by March 2027.
Eastern markets (Bihar, West Bengal) still underperforming with utilisation near 60%.
532538|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the South region, but evasive on forward cost curves, fuel contract terms and Ultravolt numbers, which were deferred to later quarters. Management said H2 will not be free of cost pressure.
key_quotes: We exited September in trade at least about 3% above the Q1 average.
Our capacity utilization was 71%, better than 66% last year on a higher base.
Business as usual is what my expectation is to deliver that INR1,400.
I won't pretend that second half will be free of cost pressures.

rows.why: Price increases are expected to flow mainly into Q3, and management has reaffirmed the INR 1,400/tonne EBITDA target for exit-March 2028, but fuel costs are up sharply (INR 51.5/bag from INR 45) and the company says H2 will not be free of cost pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: next phase to 240 Mtpa; North capacity plans before end-FY27
rows.why: Capacity now 204.7 Mtpa after 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in Sept 2026 and utilisation is 71% (vs 66% LY), with management reaffirming the 240 Mtpa target and North expansion plans before end-FY27; timing of the next phase is not yet dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes grew 13.8% YoY against an industry of about 10%, the 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in September lifts capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, and the industry is sold out with management expecting about 8% industry growth in H1 FY27 and strong momentum to March 2029.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 71% is below the 80% threshold, but the industry is sold out and management has said North expansion plans will come before end-FY27 on the way to 240 Mtpa; FY27 capex is held at about INR 10,000 crore, with a fuller view after Q3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Trade prices exited September about 3% above the Q1 average and October is about 5% above the Q2 average, with more increases expected in the next couple of months, and the full benefit is expected in Q3 earnings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45 (~13% QoQ), the kcal cost may rise from INR 2.1 to INR 2.2, and management said H2 will not be free of cost pressure, though price increases of about 5% above the Q2 average are expected to cover it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: H2 FY27 (power and control cable lines)
rows.why: Ultravolt launched on 3 September 2026 with house wire, panel wire and multicore cable production started, and power and control cable lines are due in H2 FY27 on INR 1,800 crore planned capex (INR 1,100 crore spent or committed).

rows.label: Ultravolt ramp-up and revenue target
rows.why: Ultravolt is a mature business expected in FY28, with revenue target possibly INR 16,000-18,000 crore against the earlier INR 10,000 crore, but revenue and margins are not yet disclosed and pricing is at market parity.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026 after capex and dividend, and management has committed to below 1x by March 2027.

rows.label: Price increases of 7-10 per bag in late September
rows.why: Prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in the second half of September, and spot realisation is about 5% above the Q2 average, with management expecting more increases over the next couple of months.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the South region and reaffirmed the INR 1,400/tonne and sub-1x leverage targets, but was evasive on forward cost curves, fuel contract terms and Ultravolt numbers, which were deferred; analysts pushed on H2 cost inflation and fuel costs.

532539|2026-03.headline: Uno Minda Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 5,336 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.3%, but commodity and labour cost pressure is expected to weigh on coming quarters.
532539|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 5,336 crore (+18% YoY) and EBITDA was INR 603 crore (+14%) at an 11.3% margin, both company records. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 22% to INR 326 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR 19,589 crore (+17%), normalised EBITDA INR 2,182 crore (+16%) at 11.1%, and normalised PAT INR 1,166 crore (+24%). Management flagged that aluminium and labour cost spikes (Haryana labour rates up about 35%) are expected to hit coming quarters sizably, and is negotiating faster price pass-through with customers.

financial_highlights.change: Planned increase on capex and working capital borrowings

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates and JV (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 55 crore in prior year

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (FY26, excl. Q1 prior period income)
Normalised PAT (FY26, excl. prior period income and exceptional items)

financial_highlights.change: ROCE includes land bank and CWIP
Includes INR 861 crore expansion and INR 149 crore CSN land

financial_highlights.value: INR 2.65 per share (about INR 153 crore), incl. final INR 1.75

segments.name: Switch systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,343 crore (+17%, 25% of consol), a record quarter; 2-wheeler switches grew over 26% and 2-wheeler switch exports were INR 86 crore. FY26 revenue INR 4,871 crore (+16%).

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,154 crore (+13%, about 22% of consol); FY26 INR 4,402 crore (+14%). Management says 4-wheeler lighting is now in consolidation after a threefold expansion over five years.

segments.name: Casting (alloy wheels and die casting)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 982 crore (+14%, about 18% of consol): 4-wheeler alloy wheels INR 535 crore, 2-wheeler alloy wheels INR 259 crore, die casting INR 188 crore. FY26 INR 3,694 crore (+15%). Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of growth.

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 381 crore (about 7% of consol); FY26 INR 1,416 crore (+23%). Q4 exports INR 54 crore.

segments.name: Green mobility (new reporting segment)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 423 crore (+25%, 8% of consol): alternate fuels INR 186 crore, 2W/3W EV systems INR 147 crore, 4W EV INR 46 crore, EV controllers INR 44 crore. FY26 INR 1,405 crore (+7% on restated INR 1,313 crore).

segments.name: Others (incl. acoustics, sensors/ADAS, blow moulding, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,053 crore (+25%, about 20% of consol): sensors and ADAS INR 205 crore, acoustics INR 225 crore, blow moulding INR 118 crore, non-EV controllers INR 86 crore. FY26 INR 3,801 crore (+26%). Acoustics was moved into this category.

segments.name: Aftermarket and international
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket revenue INR 340 crore (about 7% of consol) plus INR 232 crore to OEM spare parts division. International business was about 10% of Q4 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated capex planned at about INR 1,750 crore: about INR 650 crore sustaining and about INR 1,100 crore growth, plus land; more land may be needed at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat.
Annual EBITDA margin guided at about 11% plus or minus 50 bps, including known start-up costs of new plants.
Automotive industry expected to sustain growth momentum in FY27; 7 of 11 ongoing projects to commence production or ramp up in FY27.
Sunroof manufacturing commissioning expected by end FY27; EV powertrain Khed Phase 1 expected in H2 FY27.
Physical exports from India (ex overseas plants) of about INR 600 crore in FY26 expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.
Labour cost impact of about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages; mitigation via customer pass-through being negotiated.
Expected sizeable commodity-driven margin impact in coming quarters; management seeks shorter pass-through cycles (monthly or quarterly instead of half-yearly).
capex_capacity: Khed City (Pune) EV powertrain facility to begin operations in H2 FY27; Phase 1 of the Kharkhoda/Farrukhnagar-linked programmes also in progress.

New greenfield EV powertrain plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar under UMAIPL: total investment about INR 550 crore, EDU with Inovance Automotive technology partner, DHT through a customer partnership, commissioning by Q2 FY28.
CSN casting plant of about INR 300 crore to serve EDU and DST; combined EV powertrain capex about INR 1,200 crore, revenue potential more than 2x (INR 2,500 crore+, peak up to about INR 3,000 crore).
4-wheeler switch shifting from Manesar to Farrukhnagar expected to complete over the next 6 months; 2-wheeler lighting's three plants being merged into one at Kharkhoda.
Capacity post expansion: about 9.5 million 2-wheeler alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4-wheeler alloy wheels, based on announced projects.
Commissioned in Q4: 4-wheeler lighting plants at Khed City and Indonesia, 2-wheeler alloy wheel expansion at Supa, 4-wheeler alloy wheel Phase 1 at Kharkhoda, and Bawal expansion.
Sunroof order book potential exceeds INR 350 crore after a new INR 85 crore annual peak order; facility commissioning by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 PV production a record 5.5 million units (+9%); 2W production a record 26.6 million (+12%); CV production 1.17 million (+13%); 3W Q4 production +32%. Management cited EV penetration of 4.2% in PV and 6.5% in e-2W.

Q4 alloy wheel penetration moderated: 4-wheeler customers shifted mix to entry-level models with lower alloy adoption; in 2W, some programmes switched to steel wheels. Current penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W (as stated).

Pass-through: 3- or 6-month cycles set by customer policy, not by commodity; 1-2 customers operate annually. Management says commodity spikes of 30-40% are not normal and is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments.

Gross margin compressed by about 1% YoY in Q4, attributed to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impacts; the trading business (EV-related, about INR 40-45 crore) is too small to be significant.

New wins: 2W lighting order with annual peak value about INR 450 crore (SOP H2 FY28, about 25% of current 2W lighting revenue); 2W silver-box display order about INR 200 crore (production from Q4 FY27); CV seating export orders about INR 390 crore from 3 customers in Europe and North America (supplies from FY28); IVI order about INR 600 crore (SOP Q3 FY29, via Denso JV, outside consolidated revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Why set up a second 4W EV powertrain plant (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) while Khed is still under construction, and how will the multiple plants (about 9 starting FY27, ~INR 1,800 crore capex) be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited firm customer partnerships for DST and EDU and a customer push to be closer to them; Khed capacity was earmarked for existing businesses. It said one plant commissions this year and the second after about a year. Execution is handled by separate business teams, so no team overlaps across plants. Revenue guidance for the new plant was not given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 debit/credit note quantum affecting margin, and how much aluminium pass-through and commodity impact was there?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantum of the Q4 debit/credit note adjustments was not shared because it differs by business. Some customer price settlement income was booked in Q4. Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of casting growth. Commodity impact is expected to be sizable in coming quarters; Haryana labour rates are up about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the new 4W EV plant revenue potential and how much of the 1.85 lakh capacity is booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Booked share was not disclosed; the 1.85 lakh figure is eventual capacity and will be built as business is won. Khed (INR 400 crore+) and the new plant (INR 550 crore) plus about INR 300 crore CSN casting total about INR 1,200 crore capex, with revenue above 2x, at least INR 2,500 crore and up to about INR 3,000 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin impact from the labour and commodity pressures, and how does pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour impact is about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages. Pass-through cycles are set by each customer (3 or 6 months, with 1-2 customers annual), not by commodity. Management is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments. The 11% plus/minus 50 bps guidance includes known start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the alloy wheel penetration levels and the 2W alloy wheel and 4W alloy wheel capacity post expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alloy wheel penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W. Capacity post expansion is about 9.5 million 2W alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4W alloy wheels, based on announced projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down about 1%, and how large is the trading drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell about 1% YoY. Management attributed this to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impact. The EV-related trading business is about INR 40-45 crore and too small to matter. Exports from India were about INR 600 crore in FY26 and are expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the Denso JV infotainment (IVI) order and how does it reflect in consolidated numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The IVI order has annual peak value of about INR 600 crore, with SOP in Q3 FY29 and about 70% of current JV revenue of INR 846 crore. It sits in the Denso JV and is excluded from consolidated revenue, appearing only as share of JV profit. No further new business timing was committed.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium) and labour cost spikes (Haryana up about 35%; labour impact about INR 200 crore for Haryana and Gujarat) hit coming quarters, and pass-through cycles of 3-6 months (1-2 customers annual) lag the cost increase.

Start-up costs and execution load as about 7 of 11 projects commence or ramp in FY27, including Khed EV powertrain (H2 FY27), sunroof (end FY27) and CSN/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plants; the 11% plus/minus 50 bps EBITDA guidance must absorb these.
Alloy wheel penetration softening (4W mix shift to entry models, 2W programmes switching to steel wheels) could weigh on casting growth.
Capex of about INR 1,750 crore in FY27 and possible additional land at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat; net debt rose to INR 2,179 crore, partly from the INR 200-odd crore FRIWO-linked acquisition.
Q4 debit/credit note adjustments were not quantified, so the underlying Q4 margin base is harder to assess; monitor Q1 FY27 margin and the pass-through reset to monthly or quarterly.
Revenue visibility on the new 4W EV plant is not disclosed; booked share of the 1.85 lakh capacity and revenue timing remain open.
key_quotes: So some of the customers have been positive with some of the customer discussions have been happening, and we still have like 1, 1.5 month for this quarter.
Normally, you expect labor price to be 5%, 7%, 8%, 10% kind of a thing. But 35%, obviously, is not something which can be absorbed easily.
And we expect to complete the transition of Manesar plant to Farrukhnagar over the next 6 months.
But we do expect to absorb all this in our current profitability.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: 2W lighting order (INR 450 crore annual peak)
rows.why: Order worth about 25% of current 2W lighting revenue with SOP in H2 FY28.

rows.label: Physical exports to cross INR 1,500 crore

532539|2026-06.headline: Uno Minda Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores; EBITDA margin 10.3%, with FY27 guidance of 11% ±50 bps held.
532539|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations hit a record INR 5,557 crores, up 26% YoY against INR 4,420 crores excluding prior-period income. EBITDA excluding prior-year exceptional income grew 21% to INR 572 crores, but margin was 10.3% as commodity and gas inflation, a ~40 bps mathematical pass-through dilution and minimum wage hikes weighed on it. Management kept the annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, biased to the upper end. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 24% to INR 296 crores, and the company added seating, sunroof and lighting orders while the Inovance JV awaits China approval.

segments.name: Switching systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,335 crores, +20% YoY, 24% of consolidated turnover. 4-wheeler switches under Uno Mindarika grew 24% to INR 525 crores; Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift on track for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,153 crores, +14% YoY, ~21% of revenue. New domestic 4-wheeler lighting nomination from a global OEM; INR 450 crores annual peak value order in 2W lighting; Indonesia 4W lighting plant secured a second customer with SOP in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Casting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,090 crores, +32% YoY, ~20% of revenue and the fastest-growing vertical. 2W alloy wheel INR 284 crores, 4W alloy wheel INR 56 crores, aluminium die casting INR 248 crores (+66%).

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 408 crores, +28% YoY, ~7% of revenue. Exports INR 72 crores; INR 390 crores annual peak export orders from 3 new customers; INR 320 crores greenfield 4W seating plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, operations by Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 542 crores, +78% YoY, ~10% of revenue. Alternate fuels INR 184 crores, Uno Minda EV Systems INR 186 crores, Uno Minda Automation INR 123 crores, EV controller business INR 37 crores. Like-for-like EV EV Systems plus controller revenue INR 218 crores, +24%.

segments.name: Other (reconfigured)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,029 crores, +21% YoY, ~19% of revenue. Sensors and ADAS INR 250 crores, acoustics INR 225 crores, blow moulding INR 125 crores, non-EV controllers INR 80 crores; sunroof order book crossed INR 500 crores.

segments.name: Aftermarket and SPD
segments.commentary: Aftermarket revenue INR 336 crores (~6%); OEM spare parts division INR 254 crores; combined INR 590 crores, ~11% of consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, with a bias towards the higher end, reaffirmed despite Q1 headwinds.

FY27 capex stays at about INR 1,750 crores. Total announced project capex is about INR 3,800 crores, of which about INR 1,400 crores is spent; the remaining ~INR 2,000 crores to be spent over 18-24 months.
Gross margin may stay under pressure from commodity pass-through dilution (~40 bps) and lower-margin electronics business, but EBITDA margin should offset this.
Management expects healthy automotive growth through the rest of FY27 and aims to keep outperforming industry volumes.
Export targets: double and triple export value in absolute terms, with export growth needing to outpace domestic growth to raise its share.
Inovance JV: no holdup on plant construction or supplies as of now; more clarity expected in about one quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic AI in business process services is gaining traction and AI deals run as 12-16 week rapid builds with AI annualised revenue above $2.3B, but no specific named product launch or date was given.

532540|2026-06.headline: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to ₹72,275 crore, but operating margin fell 130 bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes.
532540|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹72,275 crore, up 2.2% QoQ and 13.9% YoY in rupee terms, and the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. In dollar terms revenue was $7,624 million, flat QoQ and up 2.7% YoY; constant currency growth was 0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY. TCV was $9.5 billion, including an $800 million mega deal with SKF. Operating margin fell to 24% (down 130 bps QoQ), with a 170 bps hit from annual salary increments partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and efficiencies. Management said clients deferred some projects amid geopolitical uncertainty and expects demand to improve sometime in Q2.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Delivered good growth across geographies; management remains optimistic on sustained BFSI growth.

segments.name: Technology, Software and Services
segments.commentary: Continued growth momentum with several large and mid-sized wins, including a multi-million-dollar ServiceNow deal.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Softness in auto; management expects a turnaround in Q2 based on net new wins including SKF, ABB and a Fortune 50 European firm.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: Declined this quarter; management expects recovery, with some verticals showing an uptick.

segments.name: Consumer Business Group
segments.commentary: Pressured by inflation and geopolitics affecting discretionary spend; airlines in North America and non-essential retail under stress.

segments.name: CMI and ERU
segments.commentary: CMI saw modest growth amid industry headwinds; ERU declined slightly, with management positive on AI infrastructure, electrification and renewables.

segments.name: Regional Markets
segments.commentary: Growth driven by India, public services, and products and platforms.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management expects demand to resume sometime in Q2 FY27 due to pent-up technology backlog.
Management aims to progressively move margins closer to at least FY26 levels, with an exit at 25% plus in the quarter and a target to achieve it sooner rather than later.
Management expects Manufacturing and Life Sciences to turn around in Q2, tech services to keep growing, and Consumer to recover once geopolitical sentiment improves.
Capital allocation policy unchanged; continued commitment to returning substantial free cash flows to shareholders.
Productivity pass-through to clients is about 10% to 15% on average, front-loaded in contracts, with the aim of offsetting it through new opportunities.

Anthropic partnership includes 50,000 licenses; TCS is first GSI partner for Mistral AI with a dedicated COE for industry solutions.
demand_pricing: Clients deferred some projects in Q1 as geopolitical uncertainty rose from March and continued through June; management is optimistic on a Q2 demand recovery.
TCV of $9.5 billion including SKF ($800 million, net new) and the sixth mega deal in five quarters; three mega deals announced in the last quarter per management.
AI revenue growth was lumpy: incremental AI revenue added was $75 million in Q1 versus $125 million in Q4, with management saying AI projects are often one- to two-quarter engagements.
Engagement models are shifting; agentic GBS deals saw more outcome-based commitments in F&A, HR and customer experience.
Productivity gains passed to clients are about 10% to 15% on average, typically offset by additional client work according to management.
Management said it sees no broad white-collar contraction and that total headcount rose in the quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said uncertainty rose from March and clients deferred projects; it is optimistic demand will resume sometime in Q2 on pent-up technology backlog, with no rate of change quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 16% YoY dollar increase in SG&A?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost categories were refined and the COR/SG&A split was removed; investments are in talent, partnerships and targeted areas, including some M&A-related charges.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-driven productivity deflating revenue, and how much has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to quantify; in most places productivity passed on is about 10% to 15%, and customers often give additional work in return.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental AI revenue lower QoQ, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI work is non-recurring and project-based, so quarterly revenue will be lumpy, though the trend is rising and client conversations are yielding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall sharply across segments, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 170 bps wage impact is the main driver across segments, with some vertical-level investment; TCS typically takes the Q1 headwind and aims to exit at 25%+ margin.

qa_highlights.question: How many freshers were hired and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14,000 campus graduates were onboarded last quarter, and hiring is ongoing with a focus on AI-native skills.

risks_watch: Whether the Q2 demand recovery materialises given ongoing geopolitical conflicts and project deferrals.
Margin recovery: the 170 bps wage impact and continued investment versus the stated goal of exiting at 25%+ and approaching FY26 levels.
Consumer and Life Sciences softness; management did not give a timeline beyond Q2 for consumer recovery.
AI revenue lumpiness (incremental $75 million in Q1 vs $125 million in Q4) and whether net-new AI deals convert to revenue quickly.
Productivity pass-through to clients (10% to 15%) could compress revenue per deal over time.

532540|2026-09.headline: TCS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 0.5% QoQ in constant currency to ₹73,188 crore; operating margin held at 24% amid higher subcontracting and investments.
532540|2026-09.overview: Constant-currency revenue grew 0.5% QoQ and 2.8% YoY, with international up 1.2% QoQ and India up 6% QoQ, though Regional Markets fell on an India project deferral. Growth broadened across BFSI, Manufacturing and Technology & Services, while Consumer and ERU declined. Operating margin was stable at 24% and net margin 19%, with management prioritising investment (higher bench, subcontractors, partnerships, M&A) over near-term margin expansion. Annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, over 10% of revenue, and TCV was $9.6 billion excluding Porsche and Best Buy deals.

financial_highlights.value: US$9.6 billion (excludes Porsche and Best Buy deals)

financial_highlights.change: AI revenue grew ~19% per analyst question, not disputed

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Largest large vertical and biggest growth contributor: +2.5% QoQ and +3.9% YoY in constant currency, broad-based across banking, capital markets and insurance.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.2% YoY; demand improving in factory automation, engineering productivity, and industrial AI.

segments.name: Technology and Services
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.8% YoY, driven by enterprise software, cloud modernisation and digital transformation; traditional app and infra portfolios seeing agentic AI adoption.

segments.name: Consumer Business
segments.commentary: -0.7% QoQ and -1% YoY; retail and consumer products hit by inflation, energy costs and insourcing, though QoQ decline improved versus prior quarter.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: +0.3% QoQ, stable demand from compliance, clinical/research platforms and AI-enabled drug discovery.

segments.name: Communications and Media
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ; media and digital platforms offset by continued telecom pressure.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities
segments.commentary: -0.5% QoQ; management sees medium-term structural recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Will the international growth momentum continue in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not comment on the next quarter but is confident of medium-term growth based on TCV, pipeline and client conversations.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the India revenue decline and client-count drop?
qa_highlights.answer: A project deferral in India caused the decline, expected to return in later quarters; the client drop below the $100 million band was a single account pushed below the threshold by currency movement.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin levers toward 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir Seksaria cited subcontracting cost reduction, investments starting to deliver, productivity, utilisation and non-employee expense control; long-term aspiration stays at 26%-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline QoQ, and what is the margin path to exit FY27 at 25%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin decline reflects higher subcontractor and third-party expenses; H2 headwinds include ~50 bps MHP dilution, so management will only aim to inch margins up.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI revenues margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: The $3.1 billion annualised AI revenue comes in at a much higher margin than the company average.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40% YoY growth in delivery-related costs an upfront investment that will pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir said it is a combination of investment in capacity ahead of growth and partnership costs; subcontracting is an optimisation lever, and fees to external consultants carry incremental delivery cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America lagging, and how will Consumer and ERU play out in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects North America to recover soon based on TCV and client conversations; Consumer expected to improve medium term, ERU to recover structurally over medium term.

Regional Markets volatility from lumpy deliveries; India deferral revenue expected back but no date given.

532541|2026-06.headline: Coforge Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue $592.2M (up 21.1% QoQ in USD, Encore consolidated for two months) with 16% consolidated EBIT margin, ahead of 15.5% FY27 guidance.
532541|2026-06.overview: Coforge reported Q1 FY27 with Encore (Encore/In Cora) consolidated from 24 April (revenue from 1 May), lifting headcount by 10,451 to 46,228. Consolidated EBIT margin was 16% and standalone Coforge EBIT was 16.7%, and management says it now expects to exceed the 15.5% consolidated FY27 EBIT guidance. Organic revenue grew 1.2% QoQ in CC, or 5.2% excluding the India government and data center exits; Encore G&A was cut by 40% to a combined 6.6% of revenue. Next-12-month executable order book rose 44.2% YoY to $2.23B, though the $691M quarterly order intake excludes Encore's order flow.

+5.2% QoQ CC excluding India government and data center exits
Standalone Coforge EBIT margin 16.7%; Encore EBIT margin 20.3% (from call: 20.3% and 19.1% cited)
Encore G&A down 40% from 10% to combined level; Coforge standalone was 6.7%
FCF to PAT conversion 95.3% vs -56.5% in Q1 FY26
vs INR 13.80 in previous quarter; equity base up ~25%

financial_highlights.change: Expected +US$10M earnings benefit from Q4 onwards

Organic only; excludes Encore order intake

segments.commentary: BFS 24.7% of revenue, +2.9% QoQ; Insurance 13.6%, +4.6% QoQ; Travel, transport, hospitality 21.3%, +1.7% QoQ; Healthcare and high tech 17.3%, +11.6% QoQ; Government outside India 6%; Others 17.1%, -8% QoQ after planned exits.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe +8.4% QoQ CC and Americas +3.5% QoQ CC; Rest of World -22% QoQ reflecting India government and data center exits. Management says Rest of World margins should expand from here.

segments.name: Service lines
segments.commentary: AI-led engineering 50% of revenue, data services 21%, cloud 15%; AI-led engineering, data and cloud together 86% of revenue, above the 80% indicated at the Encore announcement.

segments.commentary: One client above US$100M, three at US$50-100M, 14 at US$20-50M, 29 at US$10-20M; top 5 clients 18% and top 10 clients 26.1% of revenue.

FCF to PAT guided at more than 100% for FY27; Q1 achieved 95.3%.

Acquisition accounting: ~US$480M customer relationship intangibles amortised over 12 years (~US$40M per year); goodwill lower by US$600M after share price at closing was US$20 vs US$18.15 at signing. Management said reported goodwill is INR 120,890M in the filing.
demand_pricing: Order intake US$691M in Q1 from four large deals, organic only; Encore order intake and UK framework agreements are not included and will sit on top.

Outcome-based contracts are 6-7% of global revenue on a run-rate basis; models include risk-based legacy modernisation, subscription pricing for mod squads, and technology- or business-outcome-linked pricing.
Management said it will not discount price to chase growth, targeting 16% EBIT while aiming to be among the highest-growth and highest-margin mid caps.
Competition: management said Coforge's performance has been materially superior to the industry for nine years, citing domain focus, execution intensity and go-to-market.
Encore: one top-10 client came from the Encore portfolio with a path to US$50M+ over 18 months; two more in the 11-20 client bucket.

qa_highlights.question: How much of order intake is organic versus Encore, and are UK framework agreements included?
qa_highlights.answer: US$691M is organic only and excludes Encore order flow. The UK framework agreements are still outside the reported order intake and will be added on top.

qa_highlights.question: How is the AI monetisation (Neuron, mod squads) reported and what share is TNM vs fixed price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Neuron is an operating layer rather than a platform and cannot give a standalone AI revenue figure; the 86% AI-led engineering, data and cloud share is its proxy. Outcome-based contracts are 6-7% of revenue on a run-rate basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will Encore's G&A rise and what is the cost-out progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined G&A is 6.6% vs Coforge standalone 6.7% and Encore 10%, a 40% cut in Encore G&A. Absolute G&A rose because Encore's headcount was added; the percentage fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cloud revenue share fall and is there a reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Encore had almost no cloud revenue and was mostly engineering, so engineering share rose about 5% and cloud fell about 2.7-2.8 percentage points. Cloud grew about 4% QoQ in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Rest of World margin not expand after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: The exited India government and data center businesses carried higher margins, and Encore consolidation offset the gain, so margin was flat; management expects Rest of World margin to expand from here.

qa_highlights.question: Ramp-up of the US$158M and US$230M deals and wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The first deal ramp-up is complete with 300+ FTEs across 15-20 teams, transitioned in under four months. The second deal (US$230M+) has started ramping up with 20-30 teams. Broad wage hikes are not expected before January next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 organic CC growth of 5% QoQ repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no hard QoQ guidance; it said Q2 should be robust and that large deals signed in April are already in place.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Large-deal ramp-up from Q3 (US$230M program)

rows.label: Encore G&A and integration cost roll-off
rows.why: Encore G&A cut 40% from 10% to a combined 6.6% of revenue, with further Q2 improvement and integration cost of US$6.5M in Q1 (vs US$15M budget) fading to nil from Q3.

532541|2026-09.headline: Coforge raised FY27 consolidated EBIT margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and signed a record eight large deals, with order intake above $1 billion.
532541|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was $652.2 million, up 10.9% sequentially in constant currency, with organic sequential growth of 3.8% CC. Consolidated EBIT margin came in at 16%, ahead of the 15.5% guidance, and management raised the FY27 target to 16% and guided to a 17% reported Q4 EBIT. Order intake exceeded $1 billion (up 51% QoQ) and the next-12-month executable order book hit a record $2.4 billion, up 45% YoY. The first full quarter of the Encore (In Core) integration showed flat revenue of roughly $147-148 million on an organic basis, with management saying Encore growth will mirror Coforge from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: 10.1% QoQ in USD, 10.9% QoQ in CC, 11.6% QoQ in INR
Ahead of 15.5% FY27 guidance; H1 EBIT margin 20.5%
Acquisition-related guidance of $15-16 million overrun to about $17 million
Expected $7.1 million MTM loss in Q3 and $1.2 million in Q4
vs $12.3 million in Q1; management expects Q4 EPS around Rs 19-20 per analyst

segments.name: BFS
segments.commentary: Grew 8.3% QoQ organic CC; all eight large deals signed in the quarter came from BFSI.

segments.name: Government outside India
segments.commentary: Grew 20.8% QoQ organic CC, including a $230 million UK public sector deal signed in July 2026.

segments.name: Insurance / Travel-Transport-Hospitality / Emerging verticals
segments.commentary: Insurance grew 3.6%, TTH grew 1.8%, emerging verticals grew 2.3% QoQ organic CC.

segments.name: Healthcare and High Tech
segments.commentary: Declined 6.4% QoQ organic CC.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas grew 4.1% and Rest of World grew 16.3% QoQ organically. Order intake: $455m North America, $485m Europe, $101m RoW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBIT margin raised to 16% from 15.5%; H1 at 20.5% and management reiterated the 20.5-21% range for the full year.
Reported Q4 FY27 EBIT margin targeted at 17%, with margins expected to stay above 17% thereafter and a further significant expansion in FY28 (exit margin to carry into next year).
FY27 FCF to PAT guidance of 100% maintained; management expects to exceed 100% by year end.
Steady-state tax rate of 23-24%; no exceptional items expected in Q3 onward; hedge losses to fall to $7.1m in Q3 and $1.2m in Q4.
Encore revenue growth to mirror Coforge growth from Q3 FY27; management expressed equal confidence for FY28.
Management aims to be among the top three highest-EBIT-margin tech services firms in the short to medium term and expects to be the industry growth leader for a third consecutive year.
capex_capacity: Utilization at 82.4% versus peers at 86%+, cited as a significant margin lever.
Forward-deployed engineer (Momentum Blue) factory being built on site; heavy ongoing investment expected to cause a material gross margin spike from Q4 at consolidated level.
Near-shore capability built across Eastern Europe and Latin America via Encore acquisition.
AI in production: 520+ AI engagements for 225+ clients with 260+ agents deployed in live operations.
demand_pricing: Eight large deals signed in Q2, the highest in company history; management targets eight or more in Q3 (the shortest quarter).
Top 5 clients were 18.1% of Q2 revenue, top 10 were 26.4%; top 10 and top 20 accounts are both growing 20%+ YoY.
Second client has crossed a $100 million annualized run-rate; management says this client is among the highest-margin accounts.
Management says most deals are proactive, sole-sourced deals rather than procurement-driven RFPs, to avoid price competition; management also cited growing deal flow via advisory channels.
AI-led services (AI, engineering, data, integration, cloud) contributed 86% of consolidated revenue in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are the margin gains from AI sustainable, and are new AI deals coming at better pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current margin uptake is coming from existing fixed-price projects where AI is being infused, not from newly priced deals. Benefits are expected to show in Q4. Some efficiencies are passed to clients, but management says net margin is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Can Coforge sustain growth by relying only on sole-sourced deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to accelerate growth, attributing the industry slowdown to fewer procurement-driven RFPs, and expects advisory-channel deals to add to the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin gains from GNA optimization be reinvested in SG&A and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A has not been cut; revenue grew 53% YoY while GNA grew 15.6%. It said growth remains the first priority and that it will invest to sustain it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow conversion fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to legal entity rationalization and tax restructuring, which delayed contract transfers from US to India and caused invoicing and collection delays, raising unbilled revenue. It expects this to correct.

qa_highlights.question: How is Encore's revenue trending and how is the order book split?
qa_highlights.answer: Encore revenue was flat QoQ at about $147-148 million on an organic basis. The largest pipeline deal and largest healthcare client both come from Encore. Deal intake and order book now include Encore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPS and hedge-loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exceptional items go to zero and hedge losses fall sharply, which together with margin expansion should lift Q4 EPS; an analyst estimated Rs 19-20. Minority interest stays flat because it relates to a JV in which the client holds 20%.

risks_watch: Acute pricing pressure in the industry and AI-led deflation; management acknowledges some efficiency is passed to clients.
Q4 margin of 17% depends on fixed-price AI efficiencies and GNA levers; the gross margin investment in Momentum Blue could weigh before benefits show.
Encore revenue was flat QoQ in Q2; management says growth will match Coforge from Q3, so Q3 Encore organic growth is a key test.
Healthcare and High Tech declined 6.4% QoQ; watch recovery in these verticals.
Working capital and FCF to PAT conversion (89% in Q2) needs to reach 100% by year end; the rise in unbilled revenue is a monitoring item.
Acquisition exceptional costs overran to about $17 million against the $15-16 million guidance.
532541|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat throughout, with management repeatedly stating a "critical tipping point" for AI adoption and an intent to lead the industry on growth and margin. Answers on Encore integration and deal momentum were firm, while answers on the source of margin gains were more general and emphasised future outcomes rather than current data.
key_quotes: We are pleased to raise our consolidated EBIT margin guidance for fiscal year 27 to 16 percent from the 15.5 percent we had shared at the beginning of the year.
In quarter two, we signed eight large deals. This is the highest number of large deals we have signed in any quarter in our history.
Growth is the first, second and the third imperative as far as we are concerned we will not let anything come in the way of it.
We remain confident of delivering FCEF to PAD guidance of 100% for F527.

rows.why: Next-12-month executable order book at a record $2.4B (+45% YoY) and order intake above $1B (+51% QoQ) with eight large deals signed and eight or more targeted in Q3; Q2 organic CC growth was 3.8% sequentially.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 82.4%, which is high, but the brief shows no board-level capex plan; the Momentum Blue factory is already under way and the stated margin lever is utilisation, not new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: Q4 margin depends on AI efficiencies and GNA levers; Momentum Blue gross margin investment could weigh before benefits show, Encore was flat QoQ at about $147-148M, and FCF to PAT (89% in Q2) must reach 100%.

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed; AI agent deployments (260+ agents live) are already in production.

rows.label: Encore revenue to mirror Coforge growth from Q3 FY27
