rows.label: Exceptional items roll off from Q3
rows.why: Q2 exceptional items were $5.9M and the acquisition cost overran to about $17M; management says no exceptionals from Q3, and hedge losses fall to $7.1M in Q3 and $1.2M in Q4.

rows.label: FCF to PAT reaches 100% by year end
rows.why: FCF to PAT was 89% in Q2 and 92% in H1, with unbilled revenue rising from contract transfer delays; management holds 100% guidance and expects to exceed it by year end.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin trajectory, record order book and Encore integration, but answers on the source of margin gains and sustaining growth without procurement-driven RFPs stayed general; analysts' Q&A focus was on AI pricing, GNA reinvestment and cash conversion.

532548|2026-03.headline: Century Plyboards posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,492 crores (+24.5% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex at 13.6%.
532548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores, up 10.5% QoQ and 24.5% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA margin excluding forex losses at 13.6% versus 12.6% in Q3 and 12.1% a year ago. For FY26, revenue grew 19.2% and EBITDA ex-forex rose to INR 702 crores (13.0% margin) from INR 502 crores (11.1%), with PAT up 44% to INR 268 crores. Management has taken a 7% plywood price increase in April and an industry-wide 15% increase in MDF/particle board amid chemical and resin cost inflation, but gave no FY27 segment guidance, citing fluid geopolitical conditions. Capex is focused on plywood (Hoshiarpur, UP, Orissa land), with no frozen capex for MDF or particle board.

financial_highlights.change: +10.5% QoQ, +24.5% YoY; highest ever quarterly revenue
vs 12.6% in Q3 FY26 and 12.1% in Q4 FY25
from INR 502 crores in FY25; margin 13.0% vs 11.1%

financial_highlights.value: Growth 11.4% QoQ, 17.9% YoY; EBITDA margin ex-forex 16.1%

financial_highlights.change: Revenue +8.9% QoQ, +31% YoY; margin down ~1 pt QoQ

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% QoQ and +17.9% YoY with 16.1% EBITDA margin ex-forex; FY26 revenue +15.6%, EBITDA margin 15.2%. Capacity utilisation near 99% in Q4 per Nikita Bansal; current capacity 4,06,000 CBM as of March 2026.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.3% QoQ and +16.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.3%; FY26 revenue +13.9% with margin 8.5% vs 5.2% in FY25. Badvel thick-laminate plant utilisation 47%; overall utilisation 84% on 87.7 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.9% QoQ and +31% YoY, EBITDA margin ex-forex 11.3% after ~1 pt QoQ erosion from chemical-related disruptions and one-off ATL spend; FY26 revenue +25.5%, margin 12.7% vs 10.1%. Utilisation ~80-85%; Badvel shut down in Q4 to add 20% capacity; South plant brownfield adds 60,000-70,000 CBM in Q1 FY27 (total to ~6 lakh CBM).

segments.name: Particle Board
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +3.9% QoQ and +108.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 7.2%; FY26 revenue +38.2% but FY26 EBITDA margin only 1.2%. Old multi-daylight plant shut and to be scrapped; new continuous line capacity 2,40,000 CBM, Chennai plant cost cited at ~INR 550 crores.

segments.name: Century Ports
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary commenced commercial operations at KPD-1 West, Kolkata, in Q4 FY26; management expects it to be cash positive from Q1 FY27. Management said no cost saving accrues to Century Ply; it remains a separate profit centre.

guidance_outlook: No segment-wise FY27 guidance given; management said the situation is too fluid, with a stated intent to provide guidance at the next call.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve further as it sweats assets built over the last 3 years.
MDF steady-state EBITDA margin targeted in the high teens, timeline not specified.
Plywood planning assumes muted 10-12% volume growth and 80% utilisation for expansion planning.
Long-term debt not expected to exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA; working capital debt expected to rise with growth.
Laminates expected to outgrow the industry by 3-4 percentage points.
capex_capacity: Plywood: Hoshiarpur plant (48,000 CBM) due in October 2026 (second half FY27); brownfield expansion at Kandla, Chennai and Guwahati adds ~20% (Chennai ~25,000-30,000 CBM by July 2026).

Plywood: UP plant capex expected to start late FY27 (Feb-March 2027 or Q1 FY28), commissioning in about 15-16 months after land is ready, targeted around Q1 FY29; Orissa land procurement underway (MoU covers plywood or MDF/particle board, nothing finalised).
MDF: South plant brownfield expansion adds 60,000-70,000 CBM per year, completion targeted by end of Q1 FY27; no further MDF capacity firmed up.
Particle board: new 2,40,000 CBM continuous line running; old plant to be scrapped with no plan to revive.

Capex for FY27-28 is predominantly plywood-directed; no frozen capex for MDF or particle board. Management cited ~INR 2,000 crores of total capex over the next 4-5 years as an analyst estimate, not confirmed by management.
Century Ports absorbed roughly INR 260-270 crores of spend over three years, per analyst.
demand_pricing: Plywood: 7% price increase taken in April 2026, with further hikes contingent on the chemical and timber trend; management described it as wait-and-watch.
MDF and particle board: industry-wide price increase of about 15% in Q4 FY26, which management said barely covers the chemical-driven cost rise; some peers have made selective rollbacks.
Vishu Goel said MDF and plywood price increases of 10-12% were largely in Q1 and predominantly cover chemical cost increases.
Timber prices reported as broadly stable; management described a marginal correction, not 10%.
Plywood secondary demand stable post price increase, per management; MDF demand described as stable with normal April-May correction from Q4 exuberance.
March 2026 channel stocking was cited as a partial driver of MDF Q4 volume growth; management said April was not slow.
Plywood Sainik MR (around 8% of revenue last quarter) is being moved in-house after Hoshiarpur comes online, to reach 100% in-house production.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of MDF's ~39% YoY growth, utilisation and price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas cited year-end stocking, network expansion in the South and secondary-channel demand; utilisation 80-85% of rated capacity, with a practical max of 85-90%. Industry price increase of 15% barely covers chemical cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 segment guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said the situation is too fluid to guide now; management expects to be in a better position at the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity plans for plywood FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikita Bansal said utilisation is near 99% in Q4 and capacity rises ~30% in FY27 (about 20% brownfield plus Hoshiarpur in October); a new plant is needed in FY28-29, with UP and Orissa land being procured.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the new particle board plant cost lower than earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said the old multi-daylight plant (~INR 70 crores) was archaic and is being scrapped. The new continuous line cost about INR 550 crores, not INR 700 crores as the analyst cited.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for MDF after Q4 erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said Q4 margin fell ~1 pt QoQ from chemical disruptions and one-off ATL spend; steady state is a high-teens EBITDA margin, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels, forex exposure and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Julasaria said long-term debt will not exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA, working capital debt will rise with growth, and forex exposure is within INR 600 crores, mostly mark-to-market on long-term debt for imported machinery. Management is not increasing forex exposure.

risks_watch: Chemical (phenol, melamine, resin) and imported timber cost inflation tied to geopolitical disruption; management said the 15% price hike barely covers costs and its stickiness is unknown.
Possible price rollbacks by peers in MDF and particle board, which could affect pass-through and margins from Q1 FY27.
MDF margin recovery to high-teens EBITDA depends on chemical stabilisation; no timeline given.
Forex mark-to-market losses on long-term import debt, capped at about INR 600 crores by management.
Execution risk on Hoshiarpur (October 2026), South MDF brownfield (Q1 FY27), and UP and Orissa land timing.
Particle board FY26 EBITDA margin of only 1.2%; ramp-up of the new line is needed.
Plywood Sainik MR in-sourcing could constrain volume growth relative to the capacity addition.
532548|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and capacity growth, but deliberately cautious on forward numbers: management declined FY27 segment guidance, price-pass-through detail and chemical cost percentages, citing fluid geopolitics. Answers were sometimes inconsistent on capex and capacity figures, which the analyst challenged.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to share that the company reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores during Q4 FY '26.
Excluding forex losses, ROE improved from 10.6% to 15.2%, while ROCE increased from 12.5% to 14.6%, reflecting stronger operational performance and improved capital efficiency.
So currently, there's no frozen capex for MDF or Particle Board, which are large substantial capexes.
But long-term debt, I don't think we'll exceed 1:1 EBITDA going forward.

Sanjay Agarwal: Actually, the present situation is so, I think, fluid, it will not be right on our part to give you anything right now, but maybe by next time, we will be in a better position to -- till now whatever we have projected, we have been able to mostly achieve.

532548|2026-06.headline: Century Plyboards Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue hit record INR1,561 crore (+33.5% YoY) and PAT rose 57% to INR83.3 crore, helped by a 7% plywood price hike.
532548|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly consolidated revenue of INR1,561 crore, up 33.5% YoY, with EBITDA margin excluding forest losses at 13.0% and PAT up 57% YoY to INR83.3 crore. Plywood led, with revenue up 32.4% YoY and EBITDA margin of 16.9%, aided by a ~7% price increase taken in April on chemical input cost pressure. MDF was hit by a planned shutdown for the Andhra Pradesh capacity expansion (700 to 950 CBM/day), causing a sequential revenue decline, though revenue still grew ~29% YoY. Management has stopped giving formal guidance citing volatility, and said capex will be restrained with focus on utilisation and debt reduction.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue +32.4% YoY and +8.9% QoQ with 16.9% EBITDA margin after ~7% April price hike. Management attributes growth to price-led dealer stocking plus strong June and July sales.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue +14.7% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.2% on mix and utilisation. New home press commissioned, export-grade manufacturing planned from end-July 2026. Volume de-grew QoQ on size adjustment, per analyst question.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~29% YoY but down sequentially due to Andhra Pradesh expansion shutdown (700 to 950 CBM/day). Management targets 15%+ EBITDA margin without a date.

segments.name: Particle board
segments.commentary: Revenue +155.7% YoY and +29% QoQ on higher utilisation; margins still early-stage. Management expects ~15% margins next year.

segments.name: Logistics (Khidderpore Docks / CFS)
segments.commentary: Operations stabilised and EBITDA-positive; 9,000+ containers handled in July. Management is evaluating a possible strategic partner at valuation accretive to the company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance on revenue, volume or margins; management cites volatility from geopolitical developments.
MDF: aim for 15%+ EBITDA margin as soon as possible; growth trajectory to be maintained for FY27.
Particle board: margins to rise quarter-on-quarter with utilisation; ~15% margin targeted next year.
Long-term: ROCE target of 20% for MDF and particle board; long-term debt to be within 1x EBITDA.
Revenue aspiration: INR12,000 crore, implying ~INR4,000 crore incremental revenue; indicative incremental capex ~INR2,500 crore at 1.5-2x asset turnover.
capex_capacity: Hoshiarpur greenfield plywood plant (60,000 CBM per annum) expected to commence in Q3 FY27.
Chennai brownfield plywood capacity: 8,000 CBM/month in Q1, 10,000 in Q2, 12,500 from Q3 FY27.
Andhra Pradesh MDF expanded from 700 to 950 CBM/day during Q1.

Uttar Pradesh plywood plant (~INR200 crore capex) targeted for April 2028 if land is secured by year-end; UP MDF to follow with a lag, timing not finalised. Odisha project still at land-selection stage.

No large capex planned in the near term; third laminate press capex ~INR25 crore; no large MDF or particle board capex planned. Particle board capacity expansion beyond ~240,000 CBM via efficiencies only, not 20%+.
demand_pricing: Industry growing ~5-7%; company estimates its share at 9.5-10% of the industry at end-FY26, targeting 15% in five years (implies 12-15% annual growth).

Price hike: ~7% in plywood (April), ~15% in MDF (part since rolled back as raw material prices moved), ~10% in domestic laminate and slightly lower in exports. Price increases remain above pre-war levels across most segments.
Channel inventory at June-end described as okay; July was a high sales month to date.
Brand spend ~4-4.5% of revenue including schemes. Total Cover assurance programme (10-year, covers furniture-related costs) launched; management states claim ratio of 0.06%.
Management declined to give volume guidance or premium/standard split.

qa_highlights.question: Is plywood growth from industry growth or share gain, and where is market share heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says share was 9.5-10% last year and the goal is 15% in five years. Growth was driven by the 7% price hike, dealer stocking and a strong June. Quarterly share is not tracked.

qa_highlights.question: When will balance sheet and gearing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose on working capital for ~33% growth in a 60-day debt industry. Cash flows go to debt repayment, with no large capex planned. Target is long-term debt within 1x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is it possible to give MDF FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance has been stopped due to volatility. The objective is 15%+ MDF margins and a good growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Will particle board capacity increase by minor capex to ~3 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The line was pre-designed in two parts. Efficiency gains are possible but a 20%+ increase is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for UP and Odisha greenfield projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP land is not yet secured; target is to acquire by year-end, with the plywood plant by April 2028. Odisha is still in government talks with no land selected. UP MDF timing is not finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable ROCE for MDF and particle board, given particle board capex and realisation differences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the analyst's numbers do not match its capacity basis. The target for both segments is 20% ROCE, which it believes is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the logistics business and its structure?

segments.commentary: Operational RE capacity 12 GW; 4.2 GW added in FY26 and target of 7-8 GW in FY27 subject to transmission. NGEL generation about 15 BU vs 7 BU a year earlier. RE target 60 GW by FY32 and 136 GW by FY37.

segments.name: Coal and thermal
segments.commentary: Group coal capacity 66 GW at March 2026, planned to reach 77 GW, with 17 GW in pipeline (total 91 GW). Under-construction thermal around 16 GW. Sinnar 1,350 MW acquired with Mahagenco, first unit targeted this calendar year.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Target 30 GW by FY47 and about 6 GW by FY37. ASHVINI (NPCIL JV) building 2,800 MW at Mahi Banswara (PHWR); nuclear island EPC NIT floated 15 July 2026. Close to 34 sites under study.

segments.name: Storage and pumped storage
segments.commentary: Group BESS portfolio 38.9 GWh, with 6.62 GWh under execution (including 5 GWh co-located at thermal plants under regulated returns). Pumped storage: 1 GW Tehri operational, 13.2 GW allocated, 3-5 GW targeted by FY33.

segments.name: Mining (NTPC Mining Ltd)
segments.commentary: Production 47.8 million tonnes in Q1 (+8.5%), FY26 48.66 MT. Captive share of coal needs 18% now, targeted at 25% by FY30. Nine mines with 92 MTPA peak capacity.

segments.name: Green hydrogen and emerging
segments.commentary: Pudimadaka green hydrogen hub on 1,200 acres with about INR 1 lakh crore envisaged. Coal gasification (SNG) opportunity referenced in a INR 37,000 crore government scheme; NTPC says it is a serious contender.

guidance_outlook: Capacity target 150 GW by FY32 and 250 GW by FY37; fossil share of capacity to fall from 82% to 56% by FY32 and 39% by FY37.
Group capex about INR 1.08 lakh crore in FY26-27 (INR 56,000 crore spent in FY26), INR 5.97 lakh crore for FY28-32, and about INR 9.63 lakh crore for FY33-37; total about INR 17 lakh crore.
FY27 RE addition target of 7-8 GW, subject to transmission; management said 7 GW with storage is equivalent to roughly 8 GW of pure RE.
Dividend payout ratio to hover around 36-40%; management intends dividend to keep growing.
Generation share: RE to rise from 4% to about 33% of generation by FY37; total generation about 943 BU by FY37.
Sinnar unit commissioning targeted in calendar 2026; Pipalkoti pumped storage targeted for FY28 year-end, with a likely few-month slip.
capex_capacity: Group capacity about 127 GW, of which about 91 GW operational and 36 GW under construction; FY26 addition 9.6 GW, of which about 60% was RE. FY27 to date addition 1.9 GW.
Coal capacity 66 GW (March 2026), targeted 77 GW, with 17 GW in pipeline to reach 91 GW; beyond FY32 additions will depend on RE and demand.
Forced outage reduced to about 3.75% in FY26 from 3.9% the prior year and 4.1% earlier.
Pipeline: about 37 GW under construction and about 12 GW under tendering (per CMD). Group under-construction 35.7 GW (Investor presentation).
Coal gasification and BESS co-location at thermal plants are being developed; CO2 battery pilot expected to be commissioned by October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: Peak demand crossed 270 GW (record 271 GW in May 2026), with a projected 450+ GW by FY36 per CMD.
Management said year-to-date all-India energy met rose 9.28%, and NTPC generation about 8% YTD; NTPC rail-fed stations up 18% YTD.
PLF about 77% after backing down; management says this is despite must-run RE.
Curtailment and technical minimum (55% for coal units) are pressuring thermal units; the regulator now allows units below 55% to shut down and restart after about a day.

Regulated return: post-commissioning around 15.5% pre-tax equivalent to 12-13% returns, per CMD. Management prefers cost-plus brownfield over competitive bidding, citing equity scarcity and sustainability of returns.
Management cited a cost of debt of 5.89% (per analyst), a figure management did not dispute.

qa_highlights.question: Can NTPC accelerate RE additions, given FY26 missed target and FY27 target of 7 GW vs about 0.6 GW delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said RE should not be measured in MW alone; storage is needed, and 7 GW with storage is equivalent to about 8 GW. Transmission delays are a key constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How does NTPC plan to handle thermal units falling below technical minimum during peak solar hours?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a regulatory change allowing shutdown below 55% with capacity charges still recovered, co-located BESS of 5 GWh at thermal plants, and advocacy for uniform technical minimum. Smaller flexible units are being designed for cycling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for coal capacity and FY32-37 RE additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal capacity to reach 77 GW by FY32 and 91 GW with pipeline; beyond that, additions depend on RE and demand. Nuclear to reach about 6 GW by FY37.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend payout policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Director (Finance) said payout will hover around 36-40%, with dividend trend maintained through FY37.

qa_highlights.question: Why are states preferring tendered coal capacity over regulated cost-plus projects, and why is NTPC not bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said NTPC focuses on brownfield cost-plus projects with PPAs for healthy and transparent returns. Director (Finance) cited limited equity capacity and stated that competitive bids would compress margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will NTPC add coal gasification and nuclear capacity, and is there a plan for smaller flexible thermal units?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal gasification (SNG) is a significant opportunity; NTPC considers itself a serious contender for the INR 37,000 crore scheme. Smaller flexible units could amount to tens of GW, to be located at load centres and designed for fast start and stop, pending regulatory approval.

risks_watch: RE execution lag: 4.2 GW added in FY26 and only 1.9 GW in FY27 to date against a 7-8 GW target, constrained by transmission availability.
Curtailment and technical minimum: rising backing down of coal units could raise costs and pressure returns, which management says it will protect through policy advocacy.
Capex envelope of about INR 17 lakh crore to FY37 needs sustained funding; equity availability is a stated constraint on competitive bids.
Nuclear execution: first EPC package NIT floated July 2026; sites and JV partners still being finalised.
Hydrogen commercial viability is far off per management; coal gasification and CO2 battery timelines (Oct-Nov 2026) need monitoring.
Pipalkoti pumped storage may slip a few months past FY28 year-end.
532555|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, long-term capex and financial strength, but defensive on RE delivery and curtailment; management answered several questions by redirecting to storage and policy advocacy. Evasive on specific tender participation and on the reasons for not bidding in competitive auctions.
key_quotes: Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days from 31 days.
So, if it is about an one hour or two hours, it is better to curtail the renewable rather than stopping the thermal plant because in the evening you will be left without power.
And one per megawatt hour is roughly about INR1 crore plus on that side.
There is no plant which we are undertaking which is without PPA.

532555|2026-09.headline: NTPC standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR 45,752 crore and PAT 14% to INR 5,320 crore; NGEL revenue up 53%.
532555|2026-09.overview: NTPC posted strong Q2 FY27 standalone growth, with revenue from operations up 17% YoY to INR 45,752 crore and PAT up 14% to INR 5,320 crore, helped by O&M gains and lower fixed-cost disincentives. Group PAT for H1 rose 26% to INR 14,247 crore. NGEL's revenue and EBITDA grew about 53-57% in Q2, but renewable capacity addition is behind plan due to transmission delays, with FY27 group target cut from about 9.5 GW to about 8 GW. Management flagged coal supply tightness (5.2 MMT stock, about 7 days) and is sourcing 13 MMT from alternative sources for H2. A first interim dividend of INR 3 per share was recommended.

segments.name: NTPC standalone (conventional)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 45,752 crore and PAT INR 5,320 crore; other income fell INR 432 crore on lower dividends from subsidiaries/JVs (down INR 481 crore) and LPS down 28%. Coal fixed-cost disincentive fell to INR 332 crore from INR 625 crore a year ago.

segments.name: NTPC Group generation and coal
segments.commentary: H1 group generation 236 BU vs 214 BU (+10.4%); NTPC coal stations PLF 75.11% vs rest-of-India 68.35%. Captive coal dispatch 26.13 MMT vs 21.63 MMT (+21%).

segments.name: NTPC Green Energy (NGEL)
segments.commentary: H1 generation 10.88 BU vs 6.76 BU (+60%); Q2 revenue INR 938.16 crore and EBITDA INR 829.69 crore (about 88% margin). Curtailment from transmission constraints is ongoing.

segments.name: NVVN (trading)
segments.commentary: H1 power traded 31 BU vs 24.8 BU (+25%); commissioned 250 MW / 500 MWh BESS as an implementing agency.

segments.name: THDC and BRBCL
segments.commentary: THDC profit up on 500 MW PSP and 660 MW Khurja (full-year effect this year); INR 221 crore uplift cited. BRBCL Q2 profit up INR 64 crore on lower finance cost after refinancing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group capacity addition revised to about 8 GW from earlier 9.5 GW, all renewable; NGEL on-ground capacity expected about 6.35 GW by year-end, with a 1.5 GW shortfall attributed to transmission.
FY28 target about 9.6 GW for the group (thermal 1,460 MW, hydro 444 MW, renewable 7,735 MW); FY29 target about 10.9 GW (thermal 3,070 MW, renewable 7,807 MW).
Transmission constraints for NGEL expected to be resolved by mid-July 2027.
Group capacity under construction: 37 GW, including 17.32 GW coal, about 3.6 GW hydro and about 16 GW renewables.
Plan to tender about 4.8 GW of new thermal in Q1-Q2 FY28 with estimated capex INR 67,000 crore; pithead and non-pithead split equally.
Sinnar turnaround targeted by December 2026 or January 2027.
Battery storage: about 1,350 MW of NGEL BESS expected by mid-FY27; full-scale BESS largely in FY29; contractor issues being addressed, with BESS targeted by April.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 group capex INR 23,932 crore (vs INR 23,115 crore); standalone capex INR 14,398 crore (vs INR 14,149 crore).
Group gross PP&E INR 4,85,444 crore at 30 Sep 2026, up 11% YoY. Installed group capacity 91,506 MW; H1 additions 2,398 MW (NGEL 1,136 MW).
Lara Stage 3 (1,600 MW) awarded and limited notice to proceed issued pending environmental clearance.
Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 approved 30 Sep 2026: outlay INR 1,86,405 crore, central support INR 54,082 crore, targeted for FY32-33.
Storage plan: about 47 GWh overall, of which 5 GWh at thermal co-location; NGEL targeting about 41-42 GWh, with 40 GWh tender via ICB for direct Chinese procurement.
Pumped storage: first DPR (Maharashtra) due December, Amba DPR by March; award after DPR and TEC.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 15% and generation about 11% in H1 FY27; October demand up 21%. Peak demand met 271 GW.
Coal PLF across India rose to 70.37% in H1 FY27 from 66.02%; CIL and SCCL supply constrained, stocks critical.
Ratnagiri gas plant running on imported LNG at $16-32/MMBtu, average below $28-29; fuel cost about INR 26/kWh.
Ratnagiri profit growth driven by generation in a demand-led market, sold via market operations as PPA issues persist.
Regulatory deferral: INR 862 crore reversal of excess depreciation for Bongaigaon, nil PAT impact.
Curtailment: NGEL losses partly shifted via PPA extensions; T-GNA revenue covers O&M and interest but not depreciation. Revenue loss not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is government pushing for more thermal capacity, and what new thermal is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to tender about 4.8 GW of thermal in Q1-Q2 FY28 (Jhabua 2, Talcher 4, Talcher Kaniha 3, Bhilai, BRBCL 2), with 3-4 GW more under feasibility study.

qa_highlights.question: Is NGEL's curtailment easing and how much revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Connectivity constraints expected to clear by mid-July 2027; revenue loss not quantified, with lost generation shifted into extended PPA terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the RE addition target be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Original NGEL estimate was about 8 GW; now expected about 6.5 GW built, with about 1.5 GW held up by transmission and carried into next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated PAT grow faster than regulated equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited O&M gains and operational efficiency; expects profit growth to keep significantly exceeding regulated equity growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the C&I strategy and is thermal included?
qa_highlights.answer: An EOI for C&I partners covering power and heat closes end-November 2026, open to renewable, hydro or thermal supply.

qa_highlights.question: Why does BESS take 12-18 months and is there a merchant plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Utility-scale batteries and DC/AC integration need the time; management is replacing underperforming contractors and targets BESS commissioning by April 2027. No merchant BESS was confirmed.

risks_watch: Transmission delays in Khavda and other RE corridors continue to hold back NGEL CODs; connectivity expected by mid-July 2027.
Coal supply: 5.2 MMT stock (about 7 days); 13 MMT tender for H2 FY27 and 4 MMT additional domestic coal award pending.
Renewable target slippage: FY27 group target cut from about 9.5 GW to about 8 GW.
Other income under pressure from lower dividends from subsidiaries and JVs (down INR 481 crore) and lower LPS.
BESS execution depends on contractor performance and the upcoming 40 GWh ICB tender.
Pumped storage: DPRs due December 2026 and March 2027 before awards.
532555|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, operating performance and profit growth, but cautious and somewhat hedged on renewable capacity and transmission timelines, with several answers deferred to later data.
key_quotes: Rising demand during both peak and non-peak hours creates growth opportunities.
So, more specific to NGEL, our transmission constraint or the connectivity issue which we are facing will all be surmounted by next year, mid-July.
Profit is a different thing than a dividend payout. So, profitability has come out of better efficiency.

rows.why: Awarded with limited notice to proceed pending environmental clearance, adding 1,600 MW to the pipeline.

rows.label: Pumped storage DPRs and awards
rows.why: First DPR (Maharashtra) due December and Amba DPR by March, with awards only after DPR and TEC, so timing is conditional.

532612|2026-03.headline: Indoco Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 25.8% YoY to INR 4,291 mn and EBITDA margin hit 14.7%, with international formulations up 94.6%.
532612|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first positive quarter in about six quarters, driven by international formulations in regulated and emerging markets, while India was muted by a weak season in anti-infectives and respiratory. Standalone EBITDA rose to INR 630 mn (14.7%) from INR 35 mn a year earlier. Trade receivables rose sharply, mainly on long-credit emerging-market collections, and supplier/MSME payables were stretched. Consolidated debt is about INR 960 crore, with management guiding to roughly INR 140 crore of annual repayments and a tight capex freeze. Management also announced the hive-off of its India and Africa ophthalmic business to Sunway.

segments.name: Regulated markets
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,401 mn, +78.3% YoY. US INR 546 mn (+77.5%), Europe INR 786 mn (+68.7%), South Africa/Australia/NZ INR 692 mn (from INR 122 mn on a small base).

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 746 mn, +134% YoY (from INR 318 mn). Management cited longer receivable periods in this segment.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 315 mn, down 23% YoY (from INR 409 mn). Warren Remedies API capex is not yet generating sales as products await validation and approvals.

segments.name: Services (AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 895 mn, +65.3% YoY (from INR 467 mn).

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,739 mn vs INR 1,851 mn a year ago. Anti-infectives and respiratory were hit; management said stockist and primary sales fell while prescriptions grew. Stomatology primary sales were down 20% against IQVIA down 8%.

segments.name: Franchise/OTC (Warren Remedies)
segments.commentary: FY26 OTC revenue about INR 120 crore; Q4 OTC revenue INR 27.4 crore. Warren is loss-making, with Q4 consolidated FPP plus Warren net worth negative.

guidance_outlook: Debt repayments of about INR 140 crore a year for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with a target to prepay slightly more.
Average cost of borrowing about 8.5-9%; management implied interest savings of roughly INR 120 crore from the repayment schedule.
No major capex planned over the next two years; capex is under tight control and opex reduction is underway.
Europe margins expected to improve in the coming year as contract manufacturing moves to plants that have completed MMP scale-ups.
Management expects Warren Remedies API turnaround in a couple of quarters, with a regulated-market approval for the API site taking about one more year.
Management expects India business to grow in line with IPM and expects FPP product-mix COGS hits to reduce.
capex_capacity: Warren Remedies toothpaste block: only 1 of 4 planned lines installed; the second line (mouthwash) is deferred. First toothpaste export to South Africa started at about INR 37 lakh.
Patalganga API site: validations in progress; management is trying to speed USFDA approval by shifting a product's site from Patalganga to another site.
Sterile US supply is constrained at the existing plant pending FDA approvals; second sites now bill some sterile sales.
Liquid orals ANDA approvals received in the US for Brivaracetam and Lacosamide; launches planned in the US and Europe in FY27.
demand_pricing: Prescriptions (Rx) are growing across almost all main brands, but primary sales fell in Q4 as field staff missed annual targets; the company expects primary to correct as IQVIA follows Rx.
Cital (urinary alkalizer) was down 10% YoY and 1% QoQ in Q4 on a weak summer, though IQVIA is growing and channel stock is under 30 days.

Management said Rexidin-M Forte gel became the most prescribed stomatological brand (January and March on a max basis). Indoco overtook Pfizer to become the 20th most prescribed company by prescriptions.
Europe and UK pricing is volatile; the company is holding back on small molecules where margins are inadequate, including some Clarity Pharma products.
Emerging-market focus is Eastern Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia) and about 8 French West African countries.
The FPP Q4 COGS spike came from low-margin trading products, expired-product write-offs of about INR 4 crore, and shelf-stock adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables (up 45% vs revenue up about 9%) and rising debt and MSME payables.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the receivables rise to long-credit emerging-market collections, with regulated-market exports up about 28-29%. Debt is about INR 960 crore, flat vs last year. Some supplier payments were late due to cash-flow strain, and management expects to settle within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Why Rx growth has not translated into sales, and whether the India business will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 primary shortfall reflects weak field motivation and seasonality, with stockists holding low inventory. It expects IQVIA and primary sales to follow Rx and said India should grow in line with IPM.

qa_highlights.question: Why FPP's net worth turned more negative in Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the swing to low-margin trading sales, a COGS spike, and expired-product write-offs of about INR 4 crore. Management noted that the net worth figure includes Warren Remedies, which is also loss-making.

qa_highlights.question: Exchange loss and the interest cost increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exchange loss on the EUR 10 mn ECB loan at Oral Remedies was about INR 24 mn, roughly half of the quarter's finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: The INR 23 crore held-for-sale asset and the provision for doubtful debts.
qa_highlights.answer: The held-for-sale asset is a land parcel carried at book value, which management expects to sell above book. The roughly INR 10 crore provision includes a bankrupt customer and a policy-based provision on old disputed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment schedule and interest-cost savings.
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments are about INR 140 crore a year for FY27-FY29. Management cited an average borrowing cost of about 8.5-9%, implying roughly INR 120 crore of lower interest cost.

qa_highlights.question: Europe and US growth drivers and FDA-related constraints.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe margins should improve as MMP scale-ups complete, with only a small paracetamol residual left. US growth is driven by solid orals, while sterile supply awaits FDA approvals.

risks_watch: Receivables days and emerging-market collections, given rising trade receivables and MSME payable stretch.
Debt: about INR 960 crore consolidated, with about INR 344 crore short-term; delivery on the INR 140 crore repayment schedule.
US sterile approvals at the existing plant, and the timing of FDA approval for Warren/API sites.
Ophthalmic business hive-off to Sunway (India and Africa): deal completion and revenue impact.
Warren Remedies losses and advertising spend (about 3 years' support committed); API site validations.
Seasonality in India: Cital and anti-infective recovery, and stockist restocking.
Rivaroxaban US share (only one strength approved) and apixaban launch timing.
Currency exposure from the EUR ECB loan and the impact of the war on the exchange rate.

key_quotes: It gives me great joy to announce that after almost six quarters, we are in positive in this quarter for performance.
So, what is that is the primary reason of receivables, which are number of days of receivables, which are going up.
Yes, there has been some, where we have not paid suppliers on time given some of the cash flow situation we had.
So, next financial year which is '26-'27 we have a commitment to repay 140.

532612|2026-09.headline: Indoco Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7.4% to Rs 5,069 mn, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.2% from 12.4% on freight and material costs.
532612|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue crossed Rs 500 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 7.4% YoY to Rs 5,069 mn, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 464 mn at 9.2% margin. Standalone revenue grew only 2% to Rs 4,381 mn, with standalone EBITDA margin down to 9.2% from 12.4%. Management attributed the margin pressure to roughly Rs 13 crore of extra freight and higher material, solvent and handling costs linked to the geopolitical conflict. Domestic formulations declined to Rs 2,128 mn from Rs 2,261 mn as seasonal acute brands (Febrex Plus, Oxipod, ATL) degrew sharply, while the regulated international markets grew 21.1%.

532626|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR 932 crores and FY26 PAT rose 113% to INR 139 crores, with copper cathode capex of about INR 200 crores funded from internal accruals.
532626|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 production, sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with FY26 revenue of INR 2,939 crores (+45%) and EBITDA of INR 218 crores (7.4% margin). Q4 EBITDA was INR 61 crores and PAT INR 38 crores, with Q4 blended gross margin of 6.4% pulled down by a copper mix of about 40% and copper margins of about 3.5-4%. Operating cash flow was negative in FY26, which management attributed to about INR 265 crores of trade receivables, mainly an export shipment delayed by vessel movement that pushed INR 120-130 crores of collections into early April. Management also disclosed a 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant (Phase 1 of 18,000 tpa targeted for December 2026) and some trading volumes in Q4, which it said were opportunistic.

FY27 copper volume of about 12,000 MT including cathode; FY28 copper volume of at least 24,000 MT on a conservative basis, with up to about 36,000 MT by end FY28 mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Constant-currency growth, DSO increase, tax provision and FX hedging?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the e-Mudhra matter and RailTel arbitration?

qa_highlights.question: Which industries are targeted, and how is differentiation achieved?

532630|2026-03.headline: Gokaldas Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to about 12% (16% ex-tariff impact per management), with FY27 guided to a couple of points of margin improvement.
532630|2026-03.overview: FY26 was disrupted by US reciprocal tariffs that stayed near 50% for much of the year, with AGOA lapse hitting Africa, yet total income rose 4% to INR4,065 crores and the EBITDA margin was held at the prior-year level. Q4 standalone margins improved on volume-driven operating leverage and the post-February normalisation of the penal tariff, with no tariff refunds booked. Management guides to a Y-o-Y margin improvement of a couple of percentage points in FY27 and Africa revenue of about $115-120 million, while BTPL is being merged in and is expected to turn EBITDA positive in H2 FY27. Net debt rose by INR395 crores on capex, BTPL investment and working capital, and management targets a INR75-100 crore working capital reduction in Gokaldas and Atraco.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about $80 million; FY27 target $115-120 million, with H1 run-rate about $24-25 million per quarter. Q4 volume 5.63 million pieces at INR405; FY26 16.27 million pieces at INR420. Management expects H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10%.

segments.commentary: Had minor setbacks in Q4 as customers shifted business to other regions during the 50% tariff period; management expects reversal in FY27.

capex_capacity: Africa capacity expansion completed in FY26; one factory running 2 shifts on 20-25% of its capacity, with a second-shift opportunity without major capex.

Two further planned factories (about INR300 crores steady-state revenue) with capex of INR80-100 crores over two years; decision expected in the next quarter or so, with revenue mainly FY28.
Total capacity to reach 104 million pieces including 12 million added (India about 7.5 million, Africa about 4.5 million); India 52 million and Africa 40 million pieces currently, per management.
BTPL: 70 lakh meters/month capacity, expandable to 100 lakh with INR50-60 crores capex; captive fabric consumption by Gokaldas about 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Reciprocal tariff of about 50% (including penal 25%) on India until mid-February 2026; penal tariff withdrawn, then a 10% tariff applied until July 24, 2026. Section 301 tariffs may reset to about 20% for rest of world from late July; Africa not under Section 301 probe (Kenya stays at 10%).
Tariff rebates given during the penal regime were up to about 15% of order value, partly clawed back from the supply chain; sharper pricing of about 3% continues in H1 FY27 and is removed in H2.
AGOA extended to December 2026; US administration reportedly moving to country-by-country deals; Kenya FTA not expected by end-2026.
US retail sales grew 8% and UK 6% in CY25; US retailers pared imports from H2 CY25. Spring 27 orders being booked; customers ordering conservatively.

Input cost inflation from Middle East war (polyester, packaging, fuel, trims, cotton); pass-through being attempted in H2 orders, with partial recovery expected given customer resistance and competitor under-utilisation in SE Asia and China.
Hedging: about 80% of revenue hedged for the next two quarters at INR87-91/USD; 50% for the following two. Rupee depreciation benefit not yet in numbers, expected in H2.
Labour cost inflation in India: Haryana announced 35% wage increase from April 1 and UP 25%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a reduction of INR75-100 crores in Gokaldas and Atraco, with BTPL's working capital to be added on merger; the INR200 crore increase reflected inventory build for Q1 orders (Chinese holidays) and year-end receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Were tariff refunds booked in Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff reversals were factored in; the Q4 gain came from volume-driven operating leverage and no tariff discounts after mid-February.

qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state FY28 India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Are the acquired entities meeting internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not in FY26 due to tariff disruption; management expects them to perform to plan in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth: management said 15%-plus growth is 'straightforward' and it should do better; mid-to-high-teens was floated by the analyst, with management not confirming a number. Q2 FY27 revenue expected to resemble Q1; Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked.
Africa FY27 revenue visibility of USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, with a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.
Africa EBITDA margin expected back to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
ETR guided at 20-22% for FY27 as international operations contribute.
Wage, fuel and logistics cost pressure expected to partly ease in H2 if conditions improve; uncertainty remains. Pass-through pricing being applied to new orders.

Capex: about INR 80 crore mentioned in presentation; Jharkhand and Karnataka greenfield units total about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27), with steady-state revenue of about INR 350 crore from FY29. Bhopal second unit yields revenue from H2 FY27.
Potential 2,000-3,000 extra machines (about INR 200 crore revenue per 1,000 machines) to be decided within 3 months; larger spend in FY28.
capex_capacity: Bhopal second unit ramping up, expected to reach near full utilisation by Q4 FY27; adds about 3.5 million pieces and about INR 175-200 crore steady-state revenue.

Karnataka and Ranchi existing-factory machine additions (about 500-700 machines) are being commissioned in FY27; total of commissioned Bhopal Phase 2, Karnataka and Ranchi adds about INR 275 crore revenue potential.

New Jharkhand and Karnataka facilities: total investment about INR 100 crore, about 3.5 million pieces each, steady-state revenue about INR 350 crore combined; expected on stream H2 FY28, full potential FY29.
Africa: capacity already in place to deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue; second shift used for swing capacity; no significant Africa capex planned until existing options are exhausted.
BTPL capacity about 50 lakh meters per month, expected to grow about 30%; new customer onboarding with operations starting in Q2.
demand_pricing: US and UK end-consumer demand grew strongly through the first six months of CY26, though US growth slowed in June; EU and UK apparel imports declined through the first five months of FY27 per management.
US Section 301 tariff places India on par with competing sourcing countries, while China and Vietnam face 12.5%. India-UK FTA brings parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam in the UK.
Management says European buyers and US buyers are increasing inquiries and business towards India, extending beyond fashion and outerwear into shirts and bottoms; denim inquiries also rising.
Pricing: fabric cost pass-through is standard; some items (poly bags, cartons, fuel) were not priced into Q1 orders set in January and will be priced going forward.
Product mix: ASPs range from about USD 40-50 for high-value products to lower-value items; average realisation in India about INR 613 per piece for Gurgaon units.
UK is about 4-4.5% of total revenue; focus on larger UK players such as Marks & Spencer. Fibre mix about 65% cotton and up to 30% man-made (annual).

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth was only 3.4%, so where does India volume go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is a misleading metric because Q1 and Q2 are high-value outerwear with 150-250 minutes of content per garment, versus about 22-25 minutes for a shirt; it added there is no YoY volume drop and growth is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Does the strong order book mean the mid-teens growth guide holds, or can growth be mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Spring '27 orders execute in Q3 FY27 and revenue traction for that period and beyond looks similar to Q1; 15%-plus growth was called 'straightforward' and it should do better.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa EBITDA margin recover to double digits from about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with H2 the differentiator; it cited AGOA expiring December with a 2-year extension passed by the Senate and awaiting the House and presidential assent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility on shipping delays, and could they delay orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the worst shipping environment; outbound FOB shipments can wait about 2 weeks for a vessel, and it expects easing over the next two quarters as the war and typhoon issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: How do India incentive cuts (RoSCTL) and the BTPL merger affect margins, and is the Africa margin base higher?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% and management's worst case is a halving to about 1.75%, which it expects to offset; BTPL should reach mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA after merger in Q3. Management said the EBITDA margin would be a bit higher than the analyst's base, and it sees the rupee weakness as a cushion (about 70% of dollars hedged at about INR 89).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 visibility, particularly for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 are booked; Q2 revenue should look like Q1. Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked now and the projection looks good despite US inflation concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Is India gaining share from China and Vietnam after the tariff change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2.5% advantage is not remarkable by itself, but European and US buyers are increasing inquiries for India across shirts, bottoms and denim, not just fashion and outerwear.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 35% minimum wage hike a larger hit, and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana minimum wage rose 35% from April 2026 but overall wages for the Gurgaon/Manesar units rose only 14-15%; India wage cost increase in Q1 was about INR 20 crore, absorbed in the system. Karnataka increase was about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase and the ETR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore on utilities, gas, fuel and chemicals plus inbound and outbound logistics, partly expected to ease in H2; FY27 ETR is guided at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL Q1 performance and the break-even timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BTPL had about INR 170 crore fabric turnover in Q1 with operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%; management targets EBITDA break-even in H1 (Q2), EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan, including Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bhopal?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand and Karnataka together need about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27) for about INR 350 crore steady-state revenue, coming on stream H2 FY28; Bhopal Phase 2 adds about 3.5 million pieces and INR 175-200 crore revenue. Management also said it may add 2,000-3,000 machines with a decision within 3 months and larger spend in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Africa plan require more capex, and what is the Africa capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant Africa capex is planned until second-shift options are exhausted; capacity in place can deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue. FY27 visibility is USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indian business share, utilisation and product-wise breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Central India plants run about 85% utilisation and South India plants are full; Africa is at 80-85%. Management gave the old Gurgaon units at 1.53 million pieces at INR 613 ASP, while Matrix alone was about 1.5 million pieces at INR 613.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric mix and UK exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton is about 65% or a little higher and man-made fibres up to 30%, on an annual basis per management. UK is about 4-4.5% of revenue, with focus on larger players such as Marks & Spencer.

risks_watch: Africa EBITDA margin (about 8% in Q1) must recover to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28; AGOA expires December 2026 and the extension is still awaiting House and presidential approval.
Shipping and logistics: container shortages, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, and typhoon-related sailing delays; FOB outbound goods can sit about 2 weeks before boarding.
Wage and cost inflation: Haryana minimum wage up 35%, RoSCTL at about 3.5% with a possible halving to 1.75%, plus fuel, chemicals and poly bag/carton costs not priced into Q1 orders.
BTPL execution: operational EBITDA about -7.5% to -8% in Q1; break-even in Q2, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.
India volume metric disputed (3.4% per analyst), with growth attributed to mix; Q2 revenue expected to be similar to Q1, and Q3/Q4 orders still being booked.
Demand: US import growth slowed in June, EU and UK apparel imports declined, and US inflation could affect retail demand.
key_quotes: The quarter was a strong one, and importantly, the strength was broad based.
So we can't put an estimate to it.
Our business booking for beyond December seems to be robust.
So when we say we see a strong growth possibility, we are looking at Spring '27 for now.
I think the worst is being experienced now. My sense is in the next 2 quarters, it should ease.

532630|2026-09.headline: Gokaldas Q2 FY27: consolidated income up 13% YoY and EBITDA up 48% YoY, with India revenue up 10% in a seasonally weak quarter.
532630|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 India revenue growth of 10% YoY against industry apparel exports growth of 1.2%, Africa growth of 32% YoY, and consolidated income growth of 13% YoY with EBITDA up 48% YoY. Net debt fell to INR429 crores at September 2026 from INR553 crores at March 2026. Management said Q2 is the trough for Africa and expects growth from Q3, with margin support from INR-USD hedge rates and removal of customer discounts. The BTPL merger is expected to complete in Q3, and year-end net debt is guided at INR650-700 crores including BTPL.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 FY27; Q1 was about 44% per analyst
Q2 FY27, aided by lower base and product mix

financial_highlights.value: 72 days in Q2; target about 75 days average
financial_highlights.change: Atraco carries about 20 days of incremental working capital

financial_highlights.value: about INR170 crores; EBITDA slightly negative
financial_highlights.change: Q3 guided at INR220-225 crores, Q4 about INR250 crores

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY in a seasonally weak quarter; management targets double-digit volume growth from FY28 and India EBITDA margin of 13% at optimal utilisation.

segments.name: Africa (Atraco)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 32% YoY but margin dipped sequentially on seasonal fixed-cost absorption; management expects about 10% EBITDA margin within six months and at least 28% growth in FY28. Utilisation is about 80-85% per management's Q3 guidance.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR170 crores with slightly negative EBITDA; Q3 EBITDA breakeven targeted; about one-third of output consumed captively, aiming for 50% by FY29.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 onwards: stronger revenue and margin growth expected, supported by about 1.3-1.4% EBITDA margin from hedge rates (about INR93 in Q3 and about INR94 in Q4 versus about INR91 in Q2) and about 0.5% from ending customer discounts.
Africa: about $60m revenue visibility in H2 FY27 but management may slow one customer (20-25% of Africa revenue) to about $50-55m in H2; at least 28% growth in FY28.
Double-digit India volume growth expected from FY28; India FY27 capex about INR150 crores, possibly INR175 crores, and at least INR200 crores per year thereafter.
Effective tax rate to stay very low, near zero, after BTPL's accumulated losses (above INR600 crores) become available to the parent.
BTPL merger completion expected in Q3 FY27, pending NCLT final judgment expected within about 10 days; year-end net debt guided at INR650-700 crores.

Revenue capacity in FY28 (management view): India INR4,000 crores, Africa about INR1,250 crores, BTPL about INR1,200 crores (about 35% netted off as intra-group). Management aims for a billion-dollar consolidated revenue in about four to five years.
capex_capacity: India capacity about 59 million pieces by end FY27; Africa about 45 million pieces.
Ranchi 2,000-machine factory (1,000 machines, two shifts) to start ramp-up around mid-Q3 FY28, contributing about INR400 crores revenue largely from FY29.
Bhopal phase two fully ramped up by FY27 year-end, about 3.5 million pieces and about INR200 crores revenue.
At least two more 1,000-machine factories being evaluated, about INR400 crores revenue; debottlenecking expected to yield 4-5% extra revenue.
India utilisation about 92-93% in Q3; Africa about 80-85%.
demand_pricing: US Section 301 tariffs effective July 21, 2026 put India on par with Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Sri Lanka, with China and Vietnam at about 12.5%.
AGOA extended through December 2028 including third-country fabric provision; India-UK CETA in force since July 15, 2026 giving duty parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam.
US apparel imports fell in the year-to-date period to August 2026, with imports turning positive in August; management said Gokaldas is seeing growth despite aggregate declines.
European business about 15% of revenue, aimed at about 25% over 4-5 years; Europe margins a notch lower than US until Bangladesh duty-free access changes.
Realisations higher in Q1 and Q2 due to outerwear mix; management says YoY realisation growth is sustainable.
Two new Africa customers (one American, one European) to start from April 2026 (FY28).

qa_highlights.question: When will India deliver double-digit volume growth and is realisation growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit volume growth from FY28, with some growth from Q3; higher realisations are tied to outerwear and autumn-winter mix and are expected to be maintained or improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will Atraco reach about 10% EBITDA margin and what explains the Q2 dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is seasonally weak with fixed-cost absorption pressure; management is confident of about 10% EBITDA margin within six months, with pricing and order book aligned from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the African revenue trajectory versus the $110-120m annual guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility of about $60m in H2; management is slowing a weaker-credit customer (20-25% of Africa revenue) to about $50-55m, with no credit loss anticipated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the RoSCTL scheme changes affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% of export revenue; if halved, the 1.75% impact would be absorbed through pricing and productivity. Duty drawback of 1.5-2% is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL merger impact on debt and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR300 crores of BTPL debt will be inherited, with year-end net debt guided at INR650-700 crores including INR80-100 crores cash payout to BTPL shareholders; tax rate to stay near zero.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bangladesh unrest and EU FTA impact on orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a medium-term opportunity from Bangladesh wage unrest but does not expect large near-term shifts; EU FTA benefits are expected to flow only about six months after signing, starting around end-2027.

risks_watch: Aggregate US apparel import weakness and whether destocking persists into holiday season.
Possible loss of RoSCTL export incentive (about 3.5% of export revenue); government decision pending.
Credit risk at a large Africa customer; management is de-risking by slowing volumes.
Pending NCLT final approval for BTPL merger and an investigation media report involving Bombay Rayon and BTPL asset transfers; legal review ongoing.
Input cost inflation from oil prices and wage increases (wage costs up 8-9%, about 2-2.5% of revenue) with partial pass-through.

532633|2026-03.headline: Alldigi Tech FY26 revenue rose 9.6% to INR598.7 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR162 crore, with management guiding to mid-teens revenue growth in FY27.
532633|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR154.7 crore (+5.9% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR43.7 crore (+24.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin for FY26 at 27.1% versus 23.7% in FY25. Tech & Digital (T&D) was the growth engine at +22.3% YoY in Q4, while BPM was flat YoY at INR110.4 crore as management deliberately exited low-margin domestic FTE business. Management said about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin BPM business, and guided to mid-teens revenue growth and a 1-2% margin improvement for FY27. Q4 PAT rose 49.7% YoY to INR28.9 crore, and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore. This was the first call with new CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan, who joined about a month earlier.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR44.3 crore (+22.3% YoY, +14.5% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR156.2 crore (+16.5%). Q4 segment margin INR19.5 crore (44%); FY26 segment margin INR66.6 crore (+28.9%). Processed 49.9 lakh employee records in Q4 and 191.5 lakh in FY26; added INR40.1 crore new ACV.

segments.name: BPM (CXM)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR110.4 crore (+0.4% YoY, flat); FY26 revenue INR442.4 crore (+7.3%). Q4 segment margin INR15 crore (about 13.6%); FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore (+16.8%). International share of BPM revenue 78% in FY26 (73% prior year). Added INR54.1 crore new ACV; international BPM revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens, per the CEO, similar to the aspiration stated for FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-2% in FY27 (management said 1-1.5% annual margin growth is typical), but no absolute margin number was given.
BPM segment margin expected to hold around 13-14%; the Q4 QoQ dip was a one-off linked to a leave policy alignment with the holding company.
T&D growth expected to be slightly higher than BPM growth; international mix expected to keep rising.
Depreciation for FY27 expected to rise only modestly (management said a couple of crore from the new Chennai office), with a sub-10% increase implied on the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.
Management expects no significant negative currency impact on revenue; a weaker rupee is expected to add to margin.
FY27 existing-customer headcount expected to be flat, with no major positive growth in employee records anticipated.
capex_capacity: Office upgrade underway in Chennai (new office being built) and Noida, with about INR20 crore of investment for the Chennai facility.
Admin and facility capex typically runs INR20-25 crore a year.
Current depreciation run-rate is about INR58.6 crore; management expects only a small increase beyond the new office.
SP4 platform migration completed for India-based customers, targeted at about INR3 crore a year in efficiency gains for T&D.
HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) to be released in FY27; PulseHR.ai to automate inbound query handling and cut turnaround time.
demand_pricing: HRO international order book was about 48% of total order book as of March 31, 2026 (no comparable domestic figure given).
T&D ACV wins have consistently been more than 60% from international clients.
Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place, but timing is uncertain: client decisions were on hold due to macro conditions and the war, impacting healthcare clients.
RCM (revenue cycle management) entry: processing began about a quarter ago and has doubled in FTE; further expansion with the same client is in progress.
FY27 BPM focus verticals: healthcare and RCM, international insurance, and international collections.
Existing T&D customers have plateaued; about 90% of FY26 record growth came from new customers.
Deal closure: about 30% of deals closed at CHRO/CFO level; smaller deals (under 1,000 employees) close at HR level; CEO involvement is rare.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HRO revenue grow faster than payroll-process volumes, and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is not directly proportional to employee numbers because of one-time change requests, year-end tax work, new wage code implementation, and currency benefits from international business. Higher revenue than headcount growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 growth was constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and 6.3% from company efforts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BPM headcount decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit from low-margin business will continue through FY27; about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue CAGR below the mid-teens target, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the strategic exit from low-margin business and industry factors. It still sees mid-teens growth for FY27, which it said is slightly above industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a new large BPM client and how will margins change after the exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline, citing a large pipeline and deals delayed by macro conditions. It said the low-margin exit will have minimal impact because it is only about 10% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment margins (about INR129 crore) differ from reported EBITDA (INR162 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said segment margins are reported at PBT level after depreciation and finance costs, net of unallocable items, other income and expenses. He offered to reconcile offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company win deals and what is the sales structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price, scale, platform flexibility, operational accuracy and turnaround time. International sales are now run by geography-specific teams with rainmaker and technology partners.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and depreciation outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain guided to admin/facility capex of INR20-25 crore a year plus about INR20 crore for the Chennai office, with only a small rise in depreciation from the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.

risks_watch: BPM growth depends on landing one or two large clients; none was onboarded in the last about 12 months, and timing is not guided.
Continued headcount decline in BPM as low-margin exits proceed; about 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin.
Flat existing-customer headcount; no major positive growth in employee records expected for FY27, so growth relies on new clients and one-time revenue.
Currency tailwind contributed about 3.3% of FY26 growth; management declined to comment on future FX effects.
AI could cut client headcounts; management called this both a challenge and an opportunity.
Segment margin reconciliation to EBITDA was not clear on the call; Vaibhav Chechani's query was left for an offline discussion.
Q4 FY26 BPM margin dip was attributed to a one-off leave policy alignment with the holding company, which is yet to be quantified.

532633|2026-09.headline: Alldigi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR153.3 crore, while EBITDA grew about 29% to INR46.3 crore at a 30.2% margin.
532633|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR153.3 crore (+4% YoY, +2% QoQ), with H1 revenue at INR303.6 crore (+4.2%). Profitability grew much faster than revenue: Q2 EBITDA rose about 29% YoY to INR46.3 crore and PAT rose about 51% YoY to INR26.6 crore. Growth was held back by a deliberate reduction in low-margin domestic BPM, which fell 33% YoY in Q2, while international revenue rose 15.1% and now makes up about 70% of revenue. Management also announced a buyback of up to 4.8 lakh shares at INR1,000 per share (about INR48 crore), and new-business ACV for H1 more than doubled to INR82.6 crore.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR111.6 crore (+1% YoY, +1.8% QoQ); H1 INR221.3 crore (+1.4%). International BPM grew 12.6% YoY in Q2 and is about 83% of BPM revenue (75% a year ago), while domestic BPM fell 33% YoY.

segments.name: BPM segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR17.5 crore at 15.6% (11.6% a year ago, 11.9% in Q1); H1 INR30.6 crore at about 13.8%.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crore (+12.9% YoY, +2.7% QoQ); H1 INR82.3 crore (+12.4%). Employee records processed were 51.1 lakh in Q2 (+7.2% YoY) and 101.3 lakh in H1.

segments.name: T&D segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR18.3 crore at 43.9%; H1 INR35.7 crore at about 43.4%, helped by higher volumes and international mix.

BPM margin is expected to keep improving as domestic BPM is run down, but management gave no quantum; the domestic exit continues only where clients remain profitable.
Management declined to give revenue guidance for the next few quarters. BPM deals are expected to ramp in about 3-4 months; T&D ramp takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters.
T&D guided to early double-digit growth over the next three years.

capex_capacity: New BOT (build-operate-transfer) captive service started with one client: over 1,000 FTEs now, with the client targeting 2-3x growth; a separate BOT deal is valued at about INR16.8 crore on a contract of about 2 quarters, with potential to reach 3,000-4,000 FTEs.
Manila operations were significantly optimised; management called Manila a high-cost location.
Office was replaced with a new one on a longer lease commitment, raising ROU assets from roughly INR50-60 crore to about INR140-150 crore.

Products launched: Buzzily 2.0 (May 2026); Alldigi 360 (HCM suite incl. payroll, SaaS or technology-only) and Alldigi 360 Analytics (AI analytics, standalone or on top of existing HRIS) in October 2026.

Workday Silver certification held; design batch to finish mid-November 2026. Management sees about 4 clients in the pipeline for Workday connector implementations.
TaxSpanner partnership live since last year; management expects a bigger push this year, with more than 10-12 lakh employee records in India as the addressable base, but gave no revenue guidance.
Sales organisation rebuilt: new CBO for BPM, BPM-background leaders for US sales, SMB and enterprise sales teams in T&D, and a Southeast Asia BPM sales effort that has produced early Q2 ACV wins.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about INR5 crore (about 7%) QoQ while headcount fell less?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower replacement costs from tighter hiring rates, Manila optimisation (a high-cost location), and a retiral-benefit true-up. The full headcount reduction, which began mid-Q2, will show in Q3, and the employee cost-to-revenue ratio should keep falling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic BPM rationalisation complete?
qa_highlights.answer: It is ongoing. Management decided to exit some large client relationships and will not add new domestic clients, but will keep profitable existing ones, so the domestic book shrinks continuously rather than being fully exited.

qa_highlights.question: How far can payroll price erosion go, and how much revenue per employee can be extracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price points fall as efficiencies are shared with clients through gain-share, but premium services hold price. The focus is on selling additional HCM, SaaS and analytics services rather than defending transaction prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and timing prospects for the new ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly revenue. BPM ramp-up is about 3-4 months from go-live, while T&D takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters, depending on client implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR69 crore to about INR80 crore while DSO fell from 77 to 74 days?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said receivables are billed plus unbilled, and the rise reflects unbilled balances being converted into bills after project milestones, along with business acceleration. DSO is expected to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: How does the segment profit total of INR35.8 crore reconcile with reported EBITDA of about INR46 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said segment profit is measured before finance costs, depreciation and unallocated costs, so it is not comparable with EBITDA and no clean bridge was given.

532636|2026-03.headline: IIFL Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated PAT of INR623 crore (up 24% QoQ) and loan AUM of INR1,08,180 crore (up 38% YoY), with gold AUM up 150% YoY to INR52,581 crore.
532636|2026-03.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT before minority interest of INR623 crore, up 24% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit of INR1,173 crore, up 80% YoY and 9% QoQ. Loan AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, growing 10% QoQ, with gold the primary growth engine at 62 tonnes of tonnage. Asset quality improved, with GNPA about 1.5% and NNPA 0.7%, while the housing finance arm stayed flat and weak on profitability. Management guided to FY27 AUM growth of 20-25% for gold, 18-20% for housing, a credit cost fall to 1.5-1.7%, and a 100-120 bp cost-of-funds reduction on a rating upgrade. The income tax special audit outcome remained pending, with management expecting orders within days and saying it would appeal any demand.

segments.commentary: AUM INR52,581 crore, up 150% YoY and 11% QoQ on 62 tonnes tonnage; management guides 20-25% AUM growth in FY27 if gold prices stay at current levels, and says the new RBI gold rules are fully complied with.

segments.name: Housing finance (IIFL Home Finance)
segments.commentary: AUM was flat QoQ with subdued profitability, partly due to stress in the legacy micro-LAP book (since exited); FY27 guidance is 18-20% AUM/book growth and 25-27% disbursement growth, with yield at about 12%+ on new affordable business versus about 10.55% blended.

segments.name: Microfinance (Samasta)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency is recovering and asset quality is stabilising; management is growing cautiously, targeting about 20% growth with average microfinance ticket of about INR68,000 and micro-LAP ticket of about INR4.8 lakh, and aims to return to AUM levels of March 2024.

segments.commentary: Off-book share is 34-36% of AUM, with a target of 40-45%; co-lending book is INR14,384 crore, targeted to grow about 20%.

A credit rating upgrade from AA (stable) to AA+ could lower cost of funds by 100-120 bp.

Housing finance: about 315 branches (94 emerging, 221 affordable), with about 100 new branches planned this year in phases.
Leverage: net gearing about 3.8x at consolidated level; management says up to 4.5x is comfortable, with the regulatory maximum at about 6-7x depending on capital adequacy.
Liquidity: INR28,165 crore raised during the year plus INR7,046 crore via direct assignments; cash and equivalents including committed lines INR6,638 crore.
demand_pricing: Gold: management said loan demand is independent of gold prices, so tonnage can move sequentially even with AUM growth; Q3 tonnage growth was stronger than Q4.

Housing: prime segment exited on margin grounds; focus on affordable and emerging, where management says 7-8 large players operate and about 80 smaller players have small books. Management said PMAY 2 subsidy with a 5-year lock-in should cut borrower attrition.
Housing competition: management cited Bajaj Housing and PNB Housing entering affordable and near-prime ticket sizes of INR15-25 lakh and said IIFL does not see a challenge to growing its book.
Interest rates: management said money-market rates spiked in March and early April on war-related liquidity tightness, and are now normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax special audit and the likely impact (rumoured INR300-400 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on speculative reports. The special audit (mainly gold loans) is complete and the assessment order is expected within days or about a week; the company will appeal any demand and does not expect a material adverse outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an option to demerge into three entities (for ADIA's exit from home finance), but this is a Board decision with no timeline and no active process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 credit cost and ROA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is guided to 1.5-1.7% (against 2.7-3% in FY26) and ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%. Credit cost applies only to the on-balance-sheet book (about 10-20% of AUM), not to assigned loans.

qa_highlights.question: How will IIFL adapt to new gold-loan rules (cash-flow assessment for loans above INR2.5 lakh) and branch expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Detailed credit assessment is in place for all loans above INR2.5 lakh and the branch model already does cash-flow assessment. Gold AUM growth is guided at 20-25%, with more branches in underserved areas.

qa_highlights.question: What are the leverage and capital plans, and is equity needed for 20%+ growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow without equity if co-lending and DA reach 40-45%; it is comfortable with leverage up to 4.5x and will raise debt periodically and equity when the time is right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was housing AUM muted in FY26, and why are home finance ROE and ROA weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the exit of micro-LAP (overlapping with MFI borrowers) and reduced leverage after an equity raise 2-3 years ago. Growth is expected to lift ROE back toward double digits, and LAP is being focused on at about 18% of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rating upgrade roadmap and its impact on cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, GNPA is 1.5%, and profitability is improving; the remaining gap is capital adequacy, which needs more off-book growth or equity. A move to AA+ could cut funding cost by 100-120 bp, but management would not quantify the rating-upgrade impact.

532636|2026-06.headline: IIFL Finance Q1 FY27 PAT before NCI rose 14% QoQ to INR713 crore, with AUM up 38% YoY to INR1,15,523 crore and ROE at 19.5%.
532636|2026-06.overview: Consolidated PAT before non-controlling interest was INR713 crore, up 14% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit was about INR1,252 crore, up 50% YoY and 7% QoQ. Consolidated AUM grew 38% YoY and 7% QoQ to about INR1,15,523 crore, with gold loans at about INR58,406 crore. Gross NPA was 1.6% and net NPA 0.8%, both up about 9 bps QoQ, and management guided FY27 credit cost of 1.5% to 1.7%. The main open issue is parent-company capital adequacy, which management is addressing through an enabling resolution for fresh equity, co-lending, perpetual and subordinated debt, and possible subsidiary stake sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit cost 1.5-1.7% when microfinance is improving?

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan asset quality and LGD

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold loan growth look like 21% QoQ?
