532648|2026-03.headline: YES Bank Q4 FY26 net profit rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore, with ROA of 1.0% and GNPA at a record-low 1.3%.
532648|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered 44.7% YoY net profit growth to INR 1,068 crore and a 1.0% ROA, in line with guidance. NIM rose 10 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, helped by RIDF and mandated-deposit rundown and CASA outperformance. Asset quality improved sharply, with GNPA at 1.3% and NNPA at 0.2%, while INR 341 crore of one-time standard-asset provisioning was taken in Q4. Advances grew 11.1% YoY to INR 2.73 lakh crore, with management signalling faster momentum and FY27 growth targeted at 13-15%.

segments.commentary: Corporate book growing ~20% and Commercial Banking ~18%, per management. Commercial Banking is described as a preferred growth area.

Target ROA of 1% exit rate maintained; internal aim to add 25-50 bps of core ROA improvement over 2-3 years, excluding JC Flowers ARC write-backs.
Structural NIM target of 3.25-3.5% over 2-3 years; no near-term NIM guidance given.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 CA and SA each grew ~4% QoQ on average balances; CASA ~11% YoY on average. FY27 growth is guided at 13-15%, with sequential momentum accelerating from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift between Retail, Wholesale and Commercial after the SMBC induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail disbursements are above 20% YoY and normalising at 20-25%; Retail book growth expected at 10-11% in FY27. Corporate is growing ~20%, and mix is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How did the bond yield spike affect treasury and AFS reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: The trading book is small. AFS reserve is about negative INR 100 crore at March 31, with a swing of ~INR 200 crore. Most of the SLR book sits in HTM, and CET-1 absorbed ~10 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 340 crore one-time standard-asset provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 341 crore of provisioning was taken in Q4 under evolving and prudent policies, not linked to any credit issue. It was funded by SR recoveries of ~INR 450 crore and a INR 288 crore write-back from one corporate account.

qa_highlights.question: What is the next ROA milestone, and how sustainable is 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank exited FY26 at 1% ROA. Internal aim is 25-50 bps core ROA improvement, with some JC Flowers ARC write-backs still to come in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were credit card and personal loan slippages in INR crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card slippage was about INR 133-140 crore and personal loan slippage about INR 160-180 crore; the figures were corrected during the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion and branch share of disbursals change?
qa_highlights.answer: The plan is about 80 branches a year, aligned to deposit growth, credit growth and credit quality in each pin code. Branches supply ~60% of the ~50% of disbursals sourced internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff profile beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 and FY29 will see equal reductions, similar to FY27, with thinner runoff in FY29-FY30 as maturities taper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT1 case status?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is sub judice, with Supreme Court hearings complete and judgment reserved. Management declined to comment on the likely outcome.

532648|2026-06.headline: YES Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore, with NII up 17.5% and cost-to-income down to 62.8%.
532648|2026-06.overview: Net profit grew 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore and operating profit rose 25.5% to INR 1,704 crore, even with lower Security Receipts gains (INR 86 crore vs INR 338 crore) and lower treasury income. Reported gross slippages fell to 1.4% from 1.6% QoQ and 2.4% YoY, with retail slippages at a 10-quarter low. Advances grew 18.3% YoY to INR 2.85 lakh crore, with management stating underlying average-balance growth of 15-16%. Management reiterated its aim of a full-year ROA around 1% and a NIM above 3% over the next two years, and a board enabling resolution for capital raising was flagged.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Grew strongly in advances; management said part of the growth is transitional and shorter-tenure in nature.

segments.name: Commercial Banking (largely MSME)
segments.commentary: Advances grew 17% YoY; management said the portfolio quality remains high with controlled Q1 slippages.

segments.name: Retail Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew only 6.9% YoY, but retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY; retail slippages were at a 10-quarter low.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 ROA: aspiration around 1%; management expects core ROA to expand 15-20 bps in FY27, with the reported 1% ROA dependent on resolutions and bond/trading gains.
NIM: near-term aim of 3%+ over the next 2 years; management later said north of 3% is achievable in FY28, with expansion described as a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.
Advances growth targeted at 15-17%, a little above industry; underlying average-balance loan growth of 15-16%.
SR recoveries: guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore for FY27 maintained, dependent on J.C. Flower's execution.
Capital: 14% CET-1 seen as sufficient for about the next 4 quarters of growth; enabling approval for capital raise remains in place until the AGM. Future raise would be targeted in the 13% handle.
Retail: management expects double-digit retail book growth in about 3-4 quarters; mid-teens loan growth is the stated goal.

financial_highlights.value: INR 564 crore incl. INR 86 crore from SR portfolio

qa_highlights.question: What net advances target do you have for the year, and is the board capital-raise resolution a signal of need?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances growth is targeted at about 15-17%, a little above industry. Capital resolution is an enabler to stay ready; 3-4 quarters of growth cushion is available for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the FCNR(B) deposit and leverage product progressing and what constrains it?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is strong and leverage limits are being filled, capped at 9x for now. Pace is slowed by higher overseas borrowing spreads and uneven global liquidity; limits are being set up with international banks including SMBC.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins improve and what is the FY28 view?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are runoff of low-yield RIDF and priority-sector deposits, deposit repricing and CASA mix. Management said north of 3% NIM is achievable in FY28, with a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SR recoveries fall QoQ and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 SR redemption was INR 86 crore versus about INR 450 crore in Q4. SR face value outstanding is INR 1,500 crore with NAV above INR 2,000 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore is maintained but depends on J.C. Flower execution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raise timeline and does the AT1 court case link to it?
qa_highlights.answer: The approval is an annual enabling resolution, valid till the AGM and not tied to the court case. CET-1 of 14% is seen as enough for about 4 quarters; any raise would target the 13% handle. No provision has been made for the court case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail growth plan and how will disbursements translate into book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail book is flat to 7% growth due to run-off; disbursements grow 25-30% and book growth should follow in about 3-4 quarters. Secured mix of about 75% is the guardrail, with LAP, personal loans and franchise products.

qa_highlights.question: Did MSME slippages rise and is there West Asia war exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Commercial Banking slippages were controlled in Q1, with limited impact from the West Asia conflict and portfolio quality remaining high.

capex_capacity: No capex or capacity-expansion plans discussed; this is a bank, so the capital discussion is the relevant equivalent.

Capital: CET-1 at 14%, which management said is sufficient for about the next 4 quarters of growth (CFO also cited at least one year). Board enabling resolution for capital raise is an enabler kept in place until the AGM; future raise to be targeted in the 13% handle, versus prior raise at about 11-11.5% CET-1.

DTA benefit cited: bank can grow at 12-13% RWA without consuming capital; ROE of about 8-8.5% accretes to capital. Growth of 15-16% would consume more capital but management said it is still manageable.

ECL transition: no public estimate yet; management expects gross ECL impact not to be very material and, with new credit RWA norms from 1 April, not material to core equity. Numbers to be firmed up during the year.

Liquidity and funding: LCR 138.2%; FCNR(B) leverage limits filled, with leverage capped at 9x for now; limits being set up with international banks including SMBC, with spreads and global liquidity slowing pace.
demand_pricing: Advances up 18.3% YoY to INR 2.85 lakh crore; management said underlying average-balance growth is 15-16% and the target is 15-17%, a little above industry.
Corporate and Institutional Banking grew strongly, with part of the growth transitional and shorter-tenure; Commercial Banking (largely MSME) grew 17% YoY; Retail advances grew 6.9% YoY.
Retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY; management said fresh retail momentum is 25-30% and double-digit book growth is expected in about 3-4 quarters; mid-teens loan growth is the stated goal.
Deposits up 14.3% YoY to INR 3.15 lakh crore; CASA up 14.3% YoY (15% on average balance). Retail and branch-led deposits are close to 60% of total. Average-balance CD ratio unchanged QoQ.
NIM 2.7%, up 20 bps YoY and stable QoQ; cost of deposits down since April 2025 without attrition; management said NIM north of 3% is achievable in FY28, with a steady climb rather than linear.
Core fees up 18.7% YoY across cards, third-party products, forex and transaction banking. Cost-to-income 62.8% vs 67.1% a year ago.
Competition: deposit competition described as intense with the rate cut cycle now on par. FCNR(B) demand strong, with a stated leverage cap of 9x.
risks_watch: SR recoveries are lumpy and depend on J.C. Flower execution; Q1 recoveries of INR 86 crore fall well short of the INR 800-1,000 crore FY27 run-rate needed.
Margin path: NIM is 2.7%, with deposit competition intense and the rate-cut cycle now on par; management cautioned that expansion will be a steady climb.
Growth mix: much of the 18.3% advances growth is transitional, shorter-tenure corporate lending, while retail book growth is only 6.9%.
Dilution: capital raise enabler in place; any raise would be targeted in the 13% CET-1 handle, and the quantum and timing are unspecified.
ECL transition impact and the new credit RWA norms from 1 April are not yet quantified; management said it will update during the year.
FCNR(B) leverage growth depends on overseas bank limits; the 9x cap and pace of limit setup are unresolved.
key_quotes: Our Net Profit grew 33.7% that is year-on-year to INR 1,071 crores.
I would caution that, with the rate cut cycle now on par and Deposit competition intense, margin expansion will be a steady structural climb rather than a straight-line quarter-to-quarter.
So it is not a trigger of any particular event or court case.
We will raise it, let's say, in the 13% handle.

532648|2026-09.headline: Yes Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 65% YoY to INR 1,080 crore, but a Supreme Court ruling reinstating INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds cuts pro forma CET-1 to about 11.4%.
532648|2026-09.overview: Net profit was INR 1,080 crore (up 65% YoY) with operating profit up 29.4% to INR 1,678 crore and NII up 22.7% to INR 2,822 crore. The quarter was dominated by the Supreme Court's 15 October 2026 judgment upholding the Bombay High Court's setting aside of the March 2020 AT-1 write-down of INR 8,415 crore. Management said the indicative pro forma impact is about 240 bps on CET-1 (including profits), taking CET-1 to about 11.4% and overall Tier 1 to about 13.7%. NIM fell 12-14 bps QoQ to 2.6%, attributed mainly to FCNR(B) mobilisation that was not yet deployed, and management guided to a stable Q3 and a positive bias in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: vs 0.6% in Q2 FY26 and 0.9% in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail asset disbursements grew 35% YoY and the retail book grew nearly 9%. Retail and branch-led deposits grew 20.9% YoY and make up 58.8% of total deposits.

segments.name: Commercial Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew 20.2% YoY.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew 31.4% YoY. An analyst noted CIB was flat QoQ, and management said FCNR-linked funds would be deployed mainly in Q3 with some spill into Q4.

segments.name: Payments (PSP)
segments.commentary: Market share is about 58.7% in payee PSP and 36.4% in payer PSP (value vs volume not confirmed on the call). Management declined to size the incremental MDR income.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 NIM expected in a similar range to Q2, with a marginal negative bias from the full-quarter FCNR effect, offset by tailwinds.
Q4 FY27 NIM expected to show a positive bias. A 25 bps repo hike (October) is expected to add a high single-digit bps margin benefit in Q4, subject to market forces.
RIDF balances to fall by about INR 8,000 crore in H2 FY27: about INR 4,500 crore in Q3 and INR 3,500 crore in Q4.

FY27 ROA target of 1% for the full year is reiterated but relies partly on non-core items (Security Receipts). Management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core income, to be firmed up at FY27 end.
ECL transition: opening-balance-sheet CET-1 impact of about 50-60 bps, which management expects to be largely offset by the new credit risk circular, so not a material hit.

Growth can be sustained without a capital raise: management said ROE accretion and the DTA benefit allow about 11% growth without consuming capital, and 15% RWA growth would consume about 30-40 bps of CET-1. Capital actions are under evaluation, with no timing given.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet milestones: total assets crossed INR 5 lakh crore, deposits crossed INR 3.5 lakh crore and advances exceeded INR 3 lakh crore.
Mobilised INR 18,575 crore of FCNR(B) deposits and extended INR 15,215 crore of foreign currency term loans through the GIFT City IBU.

Security Receipts: face value about INR 1,500 crore (transcript says 15 billion), NAV about INR 2,000 crore, zero carrying value. Management cited this as a potential capital lever, without committing to action.
Recognised P&L gains of INR 395 crore from the Security Receipts portfolio in Q2.
demand_pricing: Reported advances grew 23.7% YoY; excluding FCTL linked to FCNR mobilisation, growth was 17.6%.
Deposits grew 19.5% YoY (end-period) and 22.1% (average). CASA average balances grew 15.5% YoY: current accounts +21.8%, savings +11.6%.
Certificates of deposit rose from about INR 6,000 crore to about INR 11,000 crore. Management called this tactical, citing the long-term rating upgrade above AA and LCR/NSFR considerations.

Floating-rate book is about 65% (linked to repo or T-bill), with the rest fixed. Management said a 25 bps repo move could lift margins by a high single-digit bps, subject to competition and liquidity.
Non-interest income grew 14.4% YoY and 4.7% QoQ. Operating expenses included INR 51 crore of FCNR-linked commissions, INR 20 crore of Asian Games marketing and INR 31 crore from wage code changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT-1 accounting and cash impact if the write-down is reversed, and is the coupon payable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reinstatement is in substance a balance sheet reclassification from reserves to Tier 1 borrowings, with no cash outflow on principal. The timing and manner of reinstatement and any coupon payment are still under assessment, and coupons will follow the information memoranda.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM sensitivity to repo changes, and how should Q3 and Q4 margins be framed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of the book is floating (repo or T-bill). A 25 bps repo increase could lift margins by a high single-digit bps, subject to market forces. Q3 should be similar to Q2, and Q4 should see a positive bias from repricing, RIDF runoff and FCNR deployment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff plan, and is there quantitative NIM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 RIDF reduction is about INR 8,000 crore: INR 4,500 crore in Q3 and INR 3,500 crore in Q4. Management asked that the benefit be baked into the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 ROA exceed 1%, and how much capital can growth absorb without a raise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core items, and said 11% growth is possible without consuming capital given DTA and ROE accretion. Growth at 15% would burn about 30-40 bps of CET-1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank raise capital, and what is the rating agency view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a pro forma CET-1 of 11.4% leaves headroom, but 11-11.5% is not ideal, so capital actions will be assessed. Agencies have called it a credit-neutral event, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CD issuance rise, and what is the ECL impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CD issuance was tactical, driven by the rating upgrade to above AA (long term), with LCR and NSFR considerations. ECL transition is expected at 50-60 bps of opening CET-1, largely offset by the new credit risk circular.

risks_watch: Supreme Court judgment on the INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds: legal review options, reinstatement timing, and CET-1 at about 11.4% pro forma (about 240 bps hit).
Future AT-1 coupon decisions, which are linked to dividend capacity and could affect capital-raise sentiment and bond valuations. Management declined to pre-announce.
Capital raise: timing and quantum are undecided, and management said 11-11.5% CET-1 is not ideal.
NIM path: Q3 may be flat to slightly negative, and Q4 recovery depends on repricing, FCNR deployment and RIDF runoff against competitive deposit pricing.
Corporate and Institutional Banking flat QoQ per an analyst, and FCNR deployment pace (Q3-Q4) is key to lifting yields.
ECL transition impact (50-60 bps) and the offsetting new credit risk circular, with details still being firmed up.
532648|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and growth, but cautious and often non-committal on the AT-1 judgment, coupons, capital actions and legal options, repeatedly deferring detail until the assessment is complete. Quantitative guidance was given on RIDF, NIM direction and ROA.
key_quotes: We respect the judgment and are examining it carefully, including the options available to the Bank.

Based on our current assessment, which is indicative, and as of 30th September 2026, the reinstatement of the AT-1 principal amount is expected to have a pro forma impact of approximately 240 basis points on our Common Equity Tier 1 ratio, including Profits.
There is no gun to our head to solve for capital.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 2.6% (down 12-14 bps QoQ) with Q3 guided flat, and Q4 guided to a positive bias from a 25 bps repo hike (high single-digit bps benefit), RIDF runoff of about INR 8,000 crore, and FCNR deployment, with about 65% of the book floating.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 23.7% YoY (17.6% ex-FCTL), deposits 19.5% YoY and retail disbursements 35% YoY, with management saying about 11% growth is possible without consuming capital and 15% RWA growth costs 30-40 bps of CET-1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pro forma CET-1 falls to about 11.4% after a roughly 240 bps AT-1 hit, and management called 11-11.5% not ideal, so capital actions are under evaluation with no timing; this is a capital raise rather than capex, and the brief gives no plant or branch numbers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA of 1% is reiterated with H1 at 90 bps, and management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core income, to be firmed up at FY27 end.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 NIM may be flat to slightly negative from the full-quarter FCNR effect, and FY27 ROA of 1% partly relies on Security Receipts non-core gains (INR 395 crore recognised in Q2).

rows.label: AT-1 bond reinstatement and possible capital raise
rows.why: The Supreme Court upheld reinstatement of INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds, cutting pro forma CET-1 about 240 bps to 11.4%, and management is assessing capital actions with no timing given; the timing of reinstatement and coupon payments is still under assessment.

rows.label: RIDF runoff of about INR 8,000 crore in H2 FY27
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (INR 4,500 crore) and Q4 FY27 (INR 3,500 crore)
rows.why: Management has given a firm schedule for the RIDF reduction, and it is expected to add to Q4 NIM as the benefit is baked into the following quarter.

rows.label: ECL transition CET-1 hit offset
rows.why: Opening-balance-sheet CET-1 impact of about 50-60 bps is expected to be largely offset by the new credit risk circular, though details are still being firmed up.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating metrics, growth, NIM direction and ROA, but cautious and non-committal on the AT-1 reinstatement, coupons, capital actions and legal options; analysts probed the CET-1 headroom and the Q3 NIM path.

532652|2026-03.headline: Karnataka Bank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% QoQ to INR408.19 crore; FY26 PAT record INR1,310.50 crore, GNPA down to 2.78%.
532652|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp sequential improvement: NIM rose to 3.07% from 2.92%, cost-to-income fell to 50.47% from 58.72%, and GNPA fell 54 bps QoQ to 2.78%. Business reached INR192,118 crore with gross advances up 8% QoQ to INR83,340 crore, and CASA rose to 33.61%. Management said FY26 guidance was met on most metrics, but advances (INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000–85,000 crore guidance) fell short. Much of the Q4 earnings lift came from lower employee cost, higher fee and technical write-off recovery income, and accelerated provisioning, which analysts questioned on sustainability.

financial_highlights.change: +40% QoQ from INR290.79 crore; +62% YoY vs INR252.37 crore (as stated for Q4 FY25)
+6% QoQ vs INR792 crore; +8% YoY vs INR781 crore
vs 2.92% in Q3 FY26 and 2.98% in Q4 FY25; FY26 NIM 2.88%
-54 bps QoQ from 3.32%; -30 bps YoY from 3.08%
vs 0.92% in Q3 FY26; FY26 ROA 1.05%
vs 31.53% in Dec '25; CASA INR36,560 crore, +11% QoQ
vs INR114.18 crore in Q3 FY26

segments.name: Retail, Agri and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM advances rose to INR51,197 crore from INR49,152 crore in Dec '25 (about +4% QoQ). Housing, agri, gold and vehicle loans added about INR1,547 crore to retail in Q4.

segments.name: Mid-corporate
segments.commentary: Mid-corporate advances grew about 13% QoQ in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: IBPC and food credit book
segments.commentary: Brought down to INR1,707 crore at 31 March 2026 from INR4,057 crore at 31 March 2025; about INR2,350 crore replaced in FY26 with higher-yielding loans.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Aggregate deposits INR108,779 crore (+4% QoQ). Retail term deposits INR67,648 crore (+2% QoQ, +5% YoY). Bulk deposits fell to 4.2% of total deposits from 4.8%.

guidance_outlook: Business growth around 15%; deposit growth 10% to 15%; advances growth 15% to 20% for FY27.
CASA to be maintained at 33% plus; CD ratio around 80%.
ROA to remain 1% plus, with management saying improvement is expected.
Cost-to-income to be 52% to 53% going forward, from 50.47% in Q4 and 56.34% in FY26.
PCR to rise about 1% every quarter; Q4 rise was larger than that.
Management said NIM margin floor has been reached ("I feel it has bottomed out"), with ongoing focus on 3% plus NIM; NIM had fallen to as low as 2.72% in earlier data.
Business growth phasing: H1 about 39% and H2 about 61% of annual growth; management also cited a monthly target path.
ECL transition impact estimated at 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over about 4 to 5 years (roughly 25 to 30 bps of credit cost per year).
Management targets recovering 50% of NPA and technical write-off books; called it ambitious and gave no figure.

FY27 product launches: tobacco agri input loans, programmable CBDC, NFC-based QR/Tap and Pay, surrogate-based housing lending, MSME dropline OD and LAP; major IT solutions due in FY27 include loan origination revamp, HRMS, treasury and BHIM 3.0.
capex_capacity: Around 31 branches opened in FY26; management said branch expansion plans may be revised in view of West Asia-related uncertainty.
Employee count fell in Q4 with about 350 to 400 retirements per month and no recruitment in Q4; some recruitment planned for IT and expansion.
Technical written-off portfolio about INR2,500 crore.
IT spending rising; major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27 include loan origination system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.
demand_pricing: Advances fell from about INR78,000 crore to about INR71,000 crore in FY25 before recovering to INR83,340 crore in FY26; management said retail and mid-corporate growth is the focus and bulk advances will be reduced.
About INR2,000 crore of sanctioned loans were pending disbursal as of March 2026; management said disbursement began post April.
Loan repayments were about INR26,000 crore in FY26; management estimated total disbursements at about INR31,000 to 32,000 crore.
Around 60% to 65% of the book is EBLR linked to T-bill rates (about 55% per management figures), 2.31% EBLR linked to G-sec, MCLR 5.59%, base rate 0.31% at March 2026.
Management said EBLR is at its lowest and any upward move in market rates would help interest income; ALCO will respond as required.

qa_highlights.question: Why did advances rise sharply in the quarter and how does it fit funding and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR was strong so it prioritised advances; funding came from available resources and some short-term borrowings, and funding was not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 across advances, ROA, credit cost, GNPA, NNPA and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Business growth around 15%, deposits 10% to 15%, advances 15% to 20%, CASA 33%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 52% to 53%. Credit cost was not given a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 employee cost fall while other opex rose, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any one-time shift. Employee cost cannot be cut but was held down through staff utilisation; attrition of about 350 to 400 a month and selective recruitment for IT and expansion. No FY27 employee cost figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income driven by core fees or treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income rose on fee income (processing charges, one-time ATM card fees, guarantee commission) and recovery from the technical write-off book; treasury gain about INR13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield pressure from growth squeeze margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBLR is at its lowest and margins have bottomed; upward rate moves would help; ALCO will manage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were gross slippages so low in Q4 and what is the interest reversal impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited SMA and CMA stress controls and recovery efforts; slippage was 0.20% in Q4 vs 0.47% in Q3. It did not quantify interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Will PCR keep rising, and what are the FY27 provisioning and technical write-off recovery expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is to rise about 1% a quarter; Q4 rose more. Recovery targets are ambitious (50% of NPA and technical write-off books) with no specific figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G-sec versus EBLR book mix and the gratuity impact on employee cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said both figures would be shared later by email; the call gave only the rate-linked mix (EBLR linked to T-bill about 55%, G-sec 2.31%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on net worth and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ECL impact is about 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over four to five years, with about 25 to 30 bps of credit cost each year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East deposit exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East and NRI deposits are a small share; the majority of deposits are domestic.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q4 earnings lift: PAT jump was helped by lower employee cost (management did not give a FY27 employee cost figure or gratuity impact), higher fee income and technical write-off recoveries, and accelerated provisioning; track whether these recur in Q1 FY27.

Advances shortfall vs guidance: gross advances INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000-85,000 crore guidance; FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-20% depends on converting INR2,000 crore pending disbursal and on shifting mix from bulk/IBPC to retail and mid-corporate.
Margin path: management said NIM has bottomed and ALCO will respond to rate moves, but ~55% of book is T-bill linked EBLR and rate direction is market-driven; watch NIM vs the 3% plus target.

Slippage and recovery sustainability: Q4 slippage of 0.20% vs 0.47% in Q3 is well below prior run rate; the 50% NPA and technical write-off recovery target (technical write-off book ~INR2,500 crore) was called highly ambitious with no figure given.

Macro and external risks: West Asia conflict, energy prices and supply-chain pressure; branch expansion plans may be revised; ECL transition impact of 1-1.5% of capital, spread over 4-5 years (about 25-30 bps credit cost per year), not yet quantified in FY27 guidance.

532663|2026-09.headline: Sasken Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.6% YoY to Rs.321 Cr with EBITDA margin up 330 bps QoQ to 12.9%, driven by software services.

Margins improved: gross margin 26.8%, EBITDA margin 12.9%, EBIT margin 8.9%, and PAT Rs.26 Cr (8% margin). TCV signed was $47 Mn, with $25 Mn new bookings, and management said the 60x4x3 target is delayed by about 12 months.

532667|2026-03.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.
532667|2026-03.overview: Suzlon reported record Q4 FY26 India deliveries of 830 MW and FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW (up 58%). Consolidated Q4 revenue was INR5,468 crore with EBITDA of INR964 crore (up 39% YoY) and reported PAT of INR1,114 crore, while FY26 PAT of INR3,153 crore includes a INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition. Management highlighted a shift toward EPC and development (DevCo) contracts, with EPC share of the order book rising to 28% from about 20% in Q2, and a 2.1 GW Andhra Pradesh development right extended by 24 months. Order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW at the start of the year, while commissioning reached 332 MW in Q4 and 744 MW for the year, with 971 MW erected but not yet commissioned.

financial_highlights.change: Record for any quarter in India; Q4 FY25 was 573 MW (about +45%)

financial_highlights.value: INR833 crore PBT; INR1,114 crore PAT
INR2,422 crore PBT; INR3,153 crore PAT

segments.name: WTG (wind turbine generators)

DevCo capital deployed is about INR300-350 crore against an earlier INR300 crore internal threshold; more working capital may be needed for connectivity and RE parks.

Foreign currency: some contracts carry pass-through clauses; steel is largely pass-through except some PSU contracts. Newer contracts will be priced at prevailing exchange rates.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said CERC moved wind DSM bands from plus or minus 15% to plus or minus 10%. Suzlon is testing a scheduling and forecasting model at plus or minus 10% and plans to offer it as a paid service, including to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any non-moving orders in the 5,892 MW backlog?

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, pointing to leading indicators and the FY24-26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) instead.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for price hikes to protect margins given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said WTG margins should not materially decline, citing pass-through clauses and cost management. Management said pricing on new contracts would reflect current exchange rates.

532667|2026-06.headline: Suzlon Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR3,819 crores and PAT was INR305 crores, with EBITDA flat at INR595 crores on upfront 2.0 costs and deferred deliveries.

Management attributed the flat margin to Middle East–linked logistics disruptions that deferred an estimated 10–20% of deliveries, higher fixed costs for Suzlon 2.0 (Puducherry facility, leadership, technology, marketing) and a mix shift toward lower-margin EPC/RE solutions versus AMS. Commissioning (COD) rose to 269 MW from 117 MW, with about 1,257 MW erected but awaiting commissioning. Order book stands at 6.1 GW, with about 1 GW booked in the first four months of FY27, of which 600-plus MW is DevCo-led.

532668|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, but Q4 missed plan on Middle East deal slippage and hyperscaler revenue timing; no FY27 growth number given.
532668|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 was below its own standards: revenue rose 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.02% and PAT margin at 15.02%, toward the lower end of guided ranges. The original plan was close to 30% growth, and Q4 fell short on Middle East license deal closures and project completions, a delayed hyperscaler data center project, and a one-time labour code charge. Management is stepping up expensed and capitalised investment in AI-native banking software, transit back-office software, payments and data centers, and expects higher working capital and balance-sheet pressure in FY27. It declined to give a numerical FY27 growth guide, saying only that it expects to grow ahead of industry rates.

segments.commentary: Management said Fenixys is growing strongly, has added clients, and is expanding into the Middle East, South Africa and the US. Recent European wins are smaller than Middle East deals, and management expects FY27 to be a good year for Europe.

Transit software stack work for MMRDA is described as a one-off, with later spend expected to be expensed.
Data center: investment in long-lead project execution ahead of revenue recognition, with some of the early work deferred into Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Middle East: banks halted late-stage buying processes in Q4. Management said some restarts of deal activity and POCs are now visible, but full buying has not resumed. Pre-war Saudi bank wins are in execution but have been slowed by inability to station teams on site.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 and FY28 margins and revenue growth return to 30%, or stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, citing Middle East and macro uncertainty. It said demand has not changed, Q4 was a management miss, and it expects to beat industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the capex increase is for TIG versus other areas, and where will intangibles stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is for TIG (transit and data center), the banking stack, AI stack, payments and cybersecurity. Management described a short-term spurt over the next couple of quarters, with products rebuilt as AI-native versions.

qa_highlights.answer: Management's best guess is INR 150-200 crore over the next four quarters, subject to productivity gains from AI-based code generation. The company has spent heavily on AI development over the last six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hyperscaler deal and when will its revenue be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 350 crore hyperscaler deal faced planning delays. Management said a fairly large chunk of revenue will be recognised within FY27, and the data center business is pure services.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital requirement in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 200-250 crore is the right number, with efforts to tighten contracting and payment terms. It does not expect debt to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,800 crore order book executable, and how might Middle East stress affect inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated 68%-72% of the order book is executable over 12 months, constrained by supply chain and Middle East issues. It said it is moving resources closer to Middle East customers and pushing Southeast Asia and Europe.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Advertising growth cut by about 7-8% from Jana Nayagan and Toxic shifting dates, and occupancy stuck at 26.2%, with macro risk from West Asia and fuel prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Smart screen pilots of 28-30 screens are targeted this financial year, with smart screen capex at least 30-40% below mainstream cinemas.

rows.label: Gross debt cut to about INR500 crores; net debt to zero possible
rows.why: Gross debt was about INR760 crores at 31 March 2026 and net debt is INR161 crores, with FY26 FCF at a record INR790 crores, but timing is not committed.

rows.label: Capital allocation (dividend or buyback) after net cash
rows.why: Board to decide only after the company turns net cash; buyback is on the list but no guidance was given, and management was evasive on it.

rows.label: Capital-light shift lowers capex and ROU additions
rows.why: 55% of FY26's 93 screen additions were capital-light, capex intensity fell 24% YoY, and ROU assets fell from about INR4,900 crores to INR4,600 crores as depreciation exceeded additions.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 138-screen pipeline and the balance sheet, but evasive on buyback/dividend timing, rent savings and the net-cash date; analysts pushed on capital-light economics and why own capex continues.

532689|2026-06.headline: PVR INOX Q1 FY27 PAT of INR71 crore vs loss of INR34 crore a year ago; net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026.
532689|2026-06.overview: Revenue on an Ind AS 116 adjusted basis rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore, with EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crore at a 14% margin. Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million, with ATP at INR273 (+8%) and SPH at INR161 (+9%). The company turned net cash of INR80 crore, and management said growth can now be funded from internal cash flows. No new screens opened in Q1 because completed sites were awaiting regulatory licences; openings are expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR34 crore in Q1 FY26
company describes it as debt-free; peak debt cited as INR1,450 crore
up from about 63-64%; convenience fee income +29% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Film hire cost and F&B COGS

segments.name: Exhibition (cinemas)
segments.commentary: Footfalls 36.6 million (+8%), ATP INR273 (+8%), SPH INR161 (+9%). Premium formats are 16% of the circuit (IMAX, 4DX, ICE, ScreenX, recliners, Insignia, Director's Cut, LUXE).

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management said ad revenue is still below its post-COVID peak and expects about a year to fully recover. Growth is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 with large titles; it did not give a figure.

segments.name: Alternate content and F&B
segments.commentary: Alternate content (live sports, concerts, events) ATP is about INR409; artist cost ranges from 35% to 65-70% of ticket. Food court JV with Devyani has 3 outlets open, with more in the pipeline. Web and app monetisation launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); Q1 had no openings and few closures are expected for the rest of the year.
FY27 capex now about INR350 crore, down from the earlier INR400 crore, including the food court JV and a higher renovation share.
Film hire cost guided at 45% to 45.5% of revenue for full-year FY27; F&B COGS expected to fall YoY.
Near-term target is a return to pre-COVID ROCE levels; no FCF target was given.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 expansion: about 300 cities identified, first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly, with asset-light and FOCO models; growth expected to accelerate from FY28.
Management expects margins of pre-COVID levels even at 27-28% occupancy.
capex_capacity: Screen count about 1,790 today, up from about 1,650 at the merger; about 120 net screens added over the last 4 years.
FY27 screen openings were held back by pending regulatory licences; openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.
Closed screens in Q1 were loss-making and more than 18-20 years old; bulk of FY27 closures done in Q1.
Around 600 screens are in South India; southern concentration is about 34%, according to an analyst's estimate.
Asset-light and FOCO models are the main route for new sites; the 15 million sq ft of leased space is being offered for sublease where it is not needed.
demand_pricing: India box office grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY27 across metros, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and across languages.
North America box office was up 14% YoY at $4.8 billion in H1 2026, per management.
Hollywood share of box office is about 60% overall, about 50% for big films, and up to 80-90% for mid and smaller films.
ATP growth was driven by dynamic pricing plus premium mix; discounts are offered on Tuesdays, morning shows and front seats.

Management sees no INR500 crore-plus film so far in the year, but says mid-scale films are performing; it views the upcoming slate (Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three) as strong.
Management said the occupancy trend is recovering as release windows return to 8 weeks, but did not disclose a current occupancy figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the screen closures and asset-light mix affecting the FY27 screen and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross screen additions are still 90-100 and net additions about 80. Capex is now about INR350 crore versus INR400 crore earlier, because FOCO and capital-light demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revisit asset-light models now that it is net cash, and is more real estate monetisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO will continue and will not limit growth of 100-120 screens a year. Capital will be deployed where needed without borrowing. Real estate monetisation is not planned at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why have footfalls stayed flat at 14-15 crore over rolling 12 months despite southern screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the southern skew reflects where opportunities are; 150 million admissions last year was the post-COVID high. It said occupancy is recovering and that margins at 27-28% occupancy can match pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 FCF target and what is the plan for surplus cash, including buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Sharma said there is no FCF target. The immediate goal is pre-COVID ROCE. Shareholder returns, including buyback, are being evaluated and will be disclosed when the Board decides.

qa_highlights.question: What are the unit economics of properties on the capital-light models?
qa_highlights.answer: Properties take 12-18 months to mature. FY24 and FY25 vintages are at margins above company level, and first-vintage performance will be shared by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did online penetration rise and what is the app/web monetisation revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Online penetration rose to about 69% on marketing and content mix. Growth will slow from here. The app/web ad product launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did film hire and COGS fall about 200 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Film hire fell because Dhurandhar was in its lower-rate third and fourth weeks, and there was no mega-blockbuster to trigger bonus payouts. F&B COGS have fallen YoY for two years.

risks_watch: Release calendar: no INR500 crore-plus film so far in FY27; the slate depends on Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic and Hollywood tentpoles.
Licence delays pushed Q1 openings into Q2 and Q3; the 90-100 gross screen target depends on this bunching.
Advertising has not yet recovered to post-COVID levels; management expects about another year.
Online penetration growth is slowing near 70%, so convenience fee growth will depend on ATP and admits.
Capital allocation is undecided: buyback or other shareholder returns may be announced, and the company says it is evaluating all options.
Occupancy is still below pre-COVID levels; management has not disclosed a figure.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 was a strong start to the year.
We can now fund our growth from our own cash inflows, continue on our capital-light path and do so without the weight of leverage on our balance sheet.
So we are evaluating all options, including growth as well as allocating this capital, which is best for the long-term shareholder value creation.
Yes, it would take another maybe a year before we get to the post-COVID and go ahead of that.
532689|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, the balance sheet and the content slate, and it said so repeatedly. It was cautious on timing and capital use: advertising is expected to take about a year to recover, occupancy was not quantified, and buyback and other shareholder returns were left open with "we are evaluating all options."

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA nearly doubled to INR230 crore at a 14% margin, film hire and F&B COGS each fell about 200 bps YoY, and film hire is guided at 45% to 45.5% for FY27; management expects pre-COVID margins even at 27-28% occupancy.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gross additions of 90-100 screens are guided for FY27 (about 80 net) against zero openings in Q1, so openings must bunch in Q2 and Q3; the brief flags pending regulatory licences as the risk to timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million in Q1 and India box office grew 20% YoY, but occupancy is undisclosed and no INR500 crore-plus film has landed so far, so growth depends on the upcoming slate.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex was cut to about INR350 crore from INR400 crore, the company is leaning on asset-light and FOCO models, and real estate monetisation is not planned, so a new capex programme is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on the content slate and demand, but gave no numeric guidance raise and occupancy was not quantified, so an upgrade depends on the Q3 and Q4 release calendar.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Screen openings depend on licences that already slipped Q1, advertising is about a year from post-COVID recovery, and no INR500 crore-plus film has yet come through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tier 2/3 first opening in Muzaffarpur is imminent, food court JV has 3 outlets with more in the pipeline, and the web/app ad product launched a month ago at INR2-3 crore annualised.

rows.label: Buyback or shareholder returns decision
rows.why: Company is net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026 and says shareholder returns including buyback are being evaluated, with disclosure only once the Board decides.

rows.label: Net cash position and self-funded growth
rows.why: Net cash of INR80 crore versus peak debt of INR1,450 crore, and management says growth can now be funded from internal cash flows.

rows.label: Upcoming film slate
rows.why: Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three are cited as strong, but no INR500 crore-plus film has yet been released in FY27 and the brief gives no box office estimate for them.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the balance sheet and the content slate, but cautious on advertising recovery (about a year), undisclosed occupancy, and capital use with buyback left open; analysts probed screen additions, asset-light economics, footfall stagnation and FCF targets.

532689|2026-09.headline: PVR INOX Q2 FY27 adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to INR 475 crores at a 22.3% margin, with PAT more than doubling to INR 273 crores.
532689|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was described as the best-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by a record industry box office of INR 4,433 crores (up 23% YoY) and footfalls up 4% to 46.3 million. Ind AS 116 adjusted total income grew 17% to INR 2,133 crores, with operating leverage lifting EBITDA margin about 420 bps. Management turned net cash (INR 141 crores at September-end), executed a maiden INR 300 crore buyback, and adopted a capital allocation policy targeting around 30% of annual surplus cash flow returned to shareholders. Screen growth is guided to accelerate, with 90-100 openings in FY27 and a new capital-light SMART Cinema format piloted in Muzaffarpur.

segments.name: Movie exhibition
segments.commentary: Footfalls 46.3 million (+4% YoY), occupancy 30.4%. Company says it under-indexed industry growth (18% vs 23%) because content was spread across single screens in Tier 2-4 towns.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: F&B spend per head INR 153 (+14% YoY). Popcorn and Pepsi make up about 60% of F&B sales; management says gross margin rose from about 74% to 77-78%. About 85% of footfalls buy F&B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films. Management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War; a pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

segments.name: Network and expansion
segments.commentary: Network at 1,797 screens across 114 cities (India and Sri Lanka). H1 added 24 screens across 6 cinemas and exited 25 mostly loss-making screens.

guidance_outlook: Open 90-100 new screens in FY27, mostly in H2 and mainly capital-light formats.
Next year (FY28) screen openings guided to about 150-175 per year, with about 60-70 possibly SMART screens; roughly 500 screens over three years was accepted by management.
Overall FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores (H1 spend INR 132 crores); FY28 capex likely above INR 350 crores, plus or minus.
Depreciation to fall by INR 35-40 crores a year after a useful-life change for projectors and IT equipment.
Capital allocation policy: keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x after distributions, invest for growth, and return about 30% of annual surplus cash flow via dividends or buybacks.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to benefit from a strong film slate; said it was 'very hopeful and optimistic' about H2 but did not give a Q3 footfall number.
Target payback of 3-4 years per unit; SMART Cinema capex 25-30% below normal screens and opex about 25% lower.
capex_capacity: Network 1,797 screens across 114 cities; 24 screens added and 25 exited in H1 FY27.

First SMART Cinema opened in Muzaffarpur, Bihar in September 2026 (capex 25-30% lower, opex about 25% lower, ATP about INR 190); two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur) and about 100 more signed for opening in the next 12-18 months.
300 cities identified for SMART Cinemas; expected two or three more SMART openings this fiscal.
Expansion mix is asset-light, FOCO and lease; for FOCO, only management fees are booked; for asset-light, full P&L is consolidated.
Around 35-40% of new screens in the last 2-3 years opened in South India.
demand_pricing: Industry box office INR 4,433 crores in Q2 (record, first quarter above INR 4,000 crores); H1 INR 7,618 crores (+22%).
English cinema INR 1,024 crores (+87%); Spider-Man: Brand New Day INR 608 crores; Odyssey INR 233 crores.
Hindi led by Hanuman Ansh (INR 351 crores) and Mirzapur: The Movie (INR 267 crores). Management argued Hindi growth is understated due to dubbed English films being reported under English.
Value offers: weekday morning shows at INR 99, Friday first shows at INR 149, front-row seats from INR 79.
South India average ticket price about 25% below the rest of India; management said higher occupancy more than offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How are SMART Cinemas priced, what is the capex, and what is the 2-year opening plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower than normal cinemas; ATP around INR 190 at the pilot. About 100 more are signed for 12-18 months. Management said growth will not be compromised while keeping paybacks within 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hindi incremental box office so small in H1 versus regional and English?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 had a high Hindi base; Hollywood was recovering. It added that dubbed English films (about INR 200 crores from Spider-Man) count as English, so Hindi growth is understated.

qa_highlights.question: Will screen additions accelerate after the cleanup of underperforming screens?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Past closures were of dilapidated mall screens. Management guided to 150-175 openings a year from next fiscal, with about 500 screens over three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are FOCO and asset-light revenues and costs accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light is fully consolidated. FOCO books only management fees, with operating costs at the franchisee. Lease screens are traditional leases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets and lease liabilities decline despite openings?
qa_highlights.answer: About 23-24 loss-making screens closed in H1, which offset new openings. ROU assets and liabilities also decline through depreciation and repayment under Ind AS 116.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion in F&B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a high-margin mix (popcorn and Pepsi are about 60% of sales), supplier renegotiation, a 4PL logistics migration that cuts wastage, and volume growth from weekend and weekday promotions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PVR's box office growth (18%) lag the industry (23%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to content mix: Hanuman Ansh, Mirzapur and regional films did well in Tier 2-4 towns where single screens dominate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the depreciation and capex numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year from the useful-life change. FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores; FY28 above INR 350 crores.

risks_watch: Ad revenue recovery depends on the Q3-Q4 tentpole slate (Ramayana, King, Avengers, Love & War) and the digital pay-per-eyeball platform, due in 8-10 months.
SMART format is a pilot with only about two months of data; the 150-175 screen FY28 target depends on the pipeline converting.
Lower rent-to-revenue in Q2 is tied to revenue-share terms on legacy screens (minimum guarantee or revenue share, whichever is higher); rent rose about 11% YoY in Q2.
Q2 other income includes INR 7 crores of one-off provision reversals.
Pending southern state ticket-price issues: management said no conversations are underway.
532689|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the film slate, with repeated emphasis on capital discipline and unit paybacks. Management was evasive on specifics for Q3 footfalls (no number given) and on the Hindi box office data, which it disputed.
key_quotes: This is also our best ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Unit level economics, even if you open 200 screens a year will not be compromised.
Hindi is not struggling. Hindi has been doing well since last year.
So we are trying to build on a digital platform.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose about 420 bps to 22.3% in Q2 on operating leverage, F&B gross margin moved from about 74% to 77-78%, and depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year; H2 tentpole films support it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 90-100 new screens guided for FY27 with the bulk in H2, from 24 added and 25 exited in H1, and about 100 SMART screens signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Footfalls rose 4% to 46.3 million in Q2 against industry box office up 23%, and management is 'very hopeful and optimistic' on H2 with Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, though no Q3 footfall number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 30.4% so capacity is not constrained, but FY28 capex is guided above INR 350 crores for 150-175 SMART screens a year and about 300 cities are identified, so a capex plan is likely to be formalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA rose 56% and H1 PAT rose 233%, and management is confident on the H2 film slate, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised numerically.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Screen additions (90-100) and capex (INR 300-330 crores) are held or cut, and the ad revenue risk depends on the Q3-Q4 slate and an 8-10 month digital platform.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SMART Cinema format is piloted in Muzaffarpur at about INR 190 ATP with two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur), and the pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

rows.label: SMART Cinema low-price format rollout
rows.why: SMART ATP is about INR 190 against INR 298 company-wide, with capex 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower, and about 100 more signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet and cash returns
rows.why: Net cash of INR 141 crores at end-September after H1 FREE cash flow of INR 604 crores, with a policy to return about 30% of surplus cash flow and keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x.

rows.label: Ad revenue recovery on tentpole films
rows.why: Advertising was weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films, and management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, but no ad figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, F&B gross margin, the SMART format's paybacks and H2 films, and stayed evasive on Q3 footfalls and disputed the Hindi box office data. Analysts pressed on the lag versus industry growth, the SMART pilot's short data history and the 150-175 screen FY28 target.

532698|2026-03.headline: Nitin Spinners Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR859.8 crore (+7.4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin rose to 15.17%, with management guiding to a 16-20% normalised margin in FY27.
532698|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR859.8 crore, up 7.4% QoQ and 2.2% YoY, driven by better demand and yarn prices. EBITDA rose 16.9% QoQ to INR130.4 crore, with margin up 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, and PAT reached INR57.4 crore. For full FY26, revenue fell 2.8% to INR3,213.9 crore and EBITDA fell 4% to INR452.8 crore, while PAT rose 1.2% to INR177.6 crore. Management said the capex programme (fabric and spinning expansion, renewable power) is on track for H2 FY27 commissioning.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Yarn was 74% of FY26 revenue; spinning capacity ran at over 98% utilisation in Q4 FY26, with management guiding 97-98% going forward. Average yarn spread (realisation over cotton cost, around 33-34 count) is about INR120-125/kg, up from about INR110/kg last quarter.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric was 21% of FY26 revenue (woven about 18%, knitted about 4%, per the Q&A corrections). Woven capacity ran at over 90% utilisation in Q4; woven realisation rose about 2-2.5% QoQ and knitted about 5% QoQ. Knitted utilisation is below normal, with a 65-70% normal level expected to return in 1-1.5 years.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Others contributed 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 63% of Q4 FY26 revenue (61.9% for FY26); domestic was 37% in Q4 (31.8% for FY26).

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin range of 16-20%, which management expects to reach in FY27.

Fabric capex adds 35 million metres, taking capacity to 75 million metres (errata to 70 million metres as stated), and spinning adds 22,000 tonnes to about 130,000 tonnes. Commissioning in H2 FY27: fabric from October-December 2026 and spinning from January-February 2027.

Capex of about INR1,000-1,100 crore is expected to add more than INR1,000 crore to top line. Normalisation of yarn prices may add 5-7% to existing turnover. Management expects 30-35% revenue growth on the existing base over time.

Renewable power: about 75 MW added including PPAs, reaching close to 100 MW installed. A 10 MW hybrid PPA is due by Q3 FY27. Expected savings of INR50 crore per year at full run-rate, with INR30-35 crore in the current year.
Total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crore after commissioning, including working capital. Average borrowing cost about 5.6%, working capital under 7%, blended about 6.5%.
Asset turn of about 1.2-1.3x at company level; new capex expected at about 1:1 excluding renewable capex.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion adds 35 million metres (to about 75 million metres, errata). Spinning adds 22,000 tonnes (to about 130,000 tonnes). Commissioning in H2 FY27.

Over INR300 crore spent so far, including about INR140 crore in capital advances, about INR55-60 crore capitalised from modernisation and balancing, and capital WIP of about INR100 crore. The balance is to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Additional energy capex of about INR230-240 crore, not planned before last year. Renewable power capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme incentives include capital subsidy (about 20-27% of eligible investment, paid over 10 years), interest subsidy (5% of term loan or 2.5% of eligible fixed investment, whichever is lower, for 5 years), plus electricity duty and mandi tax rebates. Management did not quantify the total.
demand_pricing: Demand improved in Q4 FY26 in both domestic and export markets, driven by US tariff removal, downstream restocking and longer transit times. Management said exports of about 100 million kg of yarn a year are steady, with a possible 5-10% increase.

Yarn spread (realisation over cotton) rose to about INR120-125/kg from about INR110/kg last quarter. Management called INR120-125 the median and said it should be sustainable, with a minimum of INR100/kg against an earlier floor of INR90/kg.
Polyester prices rose more than 20% after the West Asia conflict, but synthetic yarn spreads stayed flat. Blended yarn margins improved marginally.

Cotton: domestic prices were INR52,000-55,000 per candy in the lowest period, around 4 years low, and have been rising since recent weeks. Duty on imported cotton was removed Aug-Dec 2025; the industry is asking for a repeat removal.
Fabric prices lag yarn: the company has already raised fabric prices, and management expects further improvement. The India-UK and India-EU FTAs are expected to add European and UK orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised yarn spread and margin, excluding inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spread was about INR90/kg at the low end historically and about INR140-150/kg at the high end; a minimum of INR100/kg is now the floor, and INR120-125/kg is sustainable. Last year's margin at INR110 was about 11.5-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the freight and gas cost impacts from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sea freight is up 75-80% and other regions 15-20% versus February, but freight is normally passed on under FOB terms and has normalised since March. Gas-based yarn is a very small share, with under a day of disruption and gas costs up about 1.7x since February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the duty removal on cotton and the top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty removal is up to the government, with a possible permanent fix in 5-6 months. Top-line growth is expected from the INR1,000 crore+ capex, yarn normalisation (5-7%) and recovery, for 30-35% growth on the existing base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the fabric and knitted utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Knitted utilisation is expected to recover to the normal 65-70% within 1-1.5 years, as US tariffs were reduced from 50%. Some customers were lost to competing countries and are being regained.

risks_watch: Cotton import duty status and cotton availability. The industry wants duty removed; government has not committed to a timeline.
West Asia conflict: transit times up about 2 weeks, sea freight volatile, and polyester and gas costs rising. Management says these are passed on, but synthetic spreads have not widened.
Capex execution: commissioning slips from H2 FY27, and ramp-up of new fabric and yarn capacity. Management said it can increase the reach of fabric to European and UK buyers under the FTAs.
Knitted fabric utilisation is well below normal, at the 65-70% benchmark, and customers were lost in the US tariff period.
Future capex plans are not yet quantified. Management declined to give future capex or fabric margin targets.
532698|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the near-term outlook, with management pointing to a record quarter, a 124 bps margin gain and firm yarn spreads. Cautious where the questions turned to the war, cotton duty and timing of FTAs, and it declined to give timelines for government action or future capex.
key_quotes: This is our highest ever quarterly revenue, driven by improvement in demand and yarn prices.
As regards to the present ongoing capex, the plan is progressing very well. It is expected to commercialize in second half of FY '27.
So instead of per unit capex, we need to look at what is the total saving which we can generate out of this.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, yarn spread is INR120-125/kg vs about INR110/kg last quarter, and management guides a normalised 16-20% margin in FY27 with renewable savings of INR30-35 crore this year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spinning at 98%+ utilisation and woven fabric at 90%+; 35m metres fabric and 22,000 t spinning (to ~130,000 t, +20%) are under construction with commissioning dates set, though fabric and spinning start is the second half of the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Spinning capacity goes from about 110,000 t to about 130,000 t (+20%) and fabric to about 75 million metres (+35m) in H2 FY27, with exports steady at about 100 million kg of yarn a year and a possible 5-10% increase.

rows.label: New capex announcement

532699|2026-06.headline: Royal Orchid Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, but PAT fell to INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore.
532699|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, with EBITDA up 39% to about INR 33 crore and margin at roughly 30.7% versus 30%. Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR 12 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about INR 2.5 crore in the quarter
financial_highlights.change: company-wide, due to 5% output GST regime

segments.commentary: Occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 vs INR 5,488 a year earlier. These hotels account for the bulk of revenue; ICONIQA is the newest asset, opened November 2025.

segments.name: Managed and franchised portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

segments.name: ICONIQA (single hotel)
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 occupancy was hit by April-June travel disruption (April about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%) versus about 80% in Feb-March. Breakeven estimated at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; target INR 100 crore.

Lakshminarayan Palace in Vadodara opened, branded under an ICONIQA collection brand, positioned upper upscale.
demand_pricing: April-June demand hit by flight cancellations linked to the war; management said about 50% of India inbound travel runs through three Middle Eastern carriers, which went to zero.
Business hotels seasonally weakest in Q1 (April-June); management said Q3-Q4 are the strongest quarters.
Leisure destinations performed well while business and airport hotels were hit.
Rain in Mumbai in July and August has weighed on ICONIQA occupancy.
Nearby supply: Fairmont (50 keys), Hilton Garden Inn (170 keys) and Roswin (110 keys) opened around the same time as ICONIQA, adding about 1,000 keys within walking distance.
ICONIQA missed the corporate RFP season, so management is relying on online travel portals and repeat guests.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said April was about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%; Q4 about 80%. Q1 is seasonally weak and the war hit inbound travel. August occupancy was hit by heavy Mumbai rains.

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said no date is committed for INR 150 crore; fees grew about 14% last year, and the company aims to double fees as quickly as possible.

Reported PAT trend: PAT fell to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore; non-Ind AS PAT was INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore; management said it was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS performance and cited high tax cost.

Amit Jaiswal: So Surbhi, let me tell you, if you take the whole year round, see the revenues are scattered from first quarter to fourth quarter, but the wage remains fixed, more or less.

532699|2026-09.headline: Royal Orchid Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 34% to INR 116 crore and EBITDA 53% to INR 31.66 crore, helped by a Tanzania disinvestment gain.
532699|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income was INR 116 crore against INR 86.77 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA rose to INR 31.66 crore from INR 20.79 crore. Reported PAT of INR 14.73 crore was inflated by an exceptional gain on disinvesting the Tanzania subsidiary Multi Hotels Limited, while PBT before exceptional items rose to INR 5.57 crore from INR 4.43 crore. Sequentially, EBITDA fell about 3.8% on revenue up 2.7%, which management attributed to monsoon seasonality and roughly INR 1 to 1.5 crore of pre-opening costs for a Vadodara hotel. ICONIQA Mumbai reached EBITDA positive in the quarter for the first time, but bottom-line inflection remains unproven.

vs INR 20.79 crore in Q2 FY26, up ~53%
vs INR 4.43 crore in Q2 FY26
Operating margin ~37-38% pre-tax; ~36% after eliminating 5% inter-company royalty
vs INR 3 crore revenue and INR 1.4 crore EBITDA loss in Q2 FY26

segments.commentary: Keys up ~7%, ARR up ~4.5% and occupancy up ~2% YoY in Q2; managed-hotel revenue up ~10-10.5%. Overall managed occupancy ~59% at ADR ~INR 4,000. PBT up ~11.5% YoY.

segments.name: ICONIQA Mumbai
segments.commentary: Opened end-September 2025 and was EBITDA positive in Q2 FY27 for the first time. Management targets INR 25 crore quarterly top line this fiscal; Q4 FY26 was INR 23 crore. Management estimates ~INR 2 crore per quarter GST input-credit disallowance hit.

ICONIQA targeted to reach INR 25 crore quarterly top line in FY27, with Q4 the strongest quarter.
Other expenses expected to stay around INR 33-35 crore per quarter for the rest of the year, with no major surprises expected.
Management sees a bottom-line improvement from the second year of ICONIQA's operations; long-term goal set for 2030.
Management hopes for GST input-credit relief from the government from January onward.
capex_capacity: Opened five hotels adding 426 rooms in the last quarter; portfolio now over 127 operating hotels (177 including signed hotels).
Development pipeline of over 50 upcoming properties expected to add more than 3,500 rooms.
Growth is asset-light through partner-owned and managed structures.
Ramping up the development team to support pipeline conversion.
demand_pricing: ICONIQA occupancy was 70% in Q2 and H1 FY27, versus 81% in FY26; management cited the war-driven drop in Bombay inbound traffic in Q1 (April start) and seasonal monsoon weakness in Q1/Q2.
Marginally higher ICONIQA occupancy seen for the current quarter, with a clean run of holidays through 20 December.
Management says the market-comp annualised level is around 75% occupancy for ICONIQA, which it expects to approach.
Premiumisation strategy under way: Royal Orchid Resort Bangalore EBITDA reportedly rose from INR 80 lakh to INR 2 crore after investment.
Most managed hotels are mid-market with ADR below INR 7,500; GST input-credit disallowance on rent-linked costs is a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Managed-hotel growth trajectory and Q2 PBT margin versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said growth will be above the 10-15% range from next year, and faster than 10-12% this year, given ~30 hotels and ~1,800 keys opening over 12 months. Amit Jaiswal said managed-hotel PBT rose ~11.5% YoY with operating margin ~37-38% pre-tax, or ~36% after eliminating the 5% royalty.

qa_highlights.question: What top line gets ICONIQA to breakeven and when will it reach INR 25 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Baljee said the target is INR 25 crore quarterly top line this financial year; Q4 is strongest and last Q4 was INR 23 crore. He noted Q2 was the first EBITDA-positive quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When will the bottom line inflect, given upfront costs and asset-light ROCE goals?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the 2030 long-term goal remains, ICONIQA's second year should show bottom-line improvement, and GST disallowance is costing about INR 2 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA fall sequentially and what margin to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal attributed it to monsoon seasonality and ~INR 1-1.5 crore pre-opening cost for the Vadodara hotel, and expects a better EBITDA going forward; no margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: ICONIQA occupancy trend and ADR?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Baljee said FY26 occupancy was 81%, Q1 and Q2 FY27 were 70%, and Q2 ADR rose from ~INR 7,800 to ~INR 8,000. He argued like-for-like comparison is more relevant, and management did not give a stable ARR figure.

qa_highlights.question: Governance: qualified audit opinions, SEBI order, and promoter resolutions defeated by institutions?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the SEBI issue is partly resolved in the company's favour, one accounting issue is pending with a final hearing held and an order expected soon, and the audit matters are being defended with no financial impact expected. Arjun Baljee cited premiumisation as the path to better ARR.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and timeline of the Ksheer Sagar NCLT matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the NCLT matter is with the partner, creates no financial implication even on outcome, and is a control issue with no defined timeline given.
