532700|2026-03.headline: ENIL FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3.9% to INR565 crore; digital grew 84% to INR112.4 crore while Q4 non-FCT weakened on war-related event disruptions.
532700|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was INR565 crore (+3.9% YoY), with domestic revenue up 4% to INR548 crore led by digital. EBITDA excluding digital was INR76 crore (18% margin) and PAT excluding digital was INR22 crore, which includes a INR17.2 crore one-time gain from reversing deferred tax liability under the Finance Act 2026. Radio faced subdued demand and the Middle East conflict hurt international operations, while non-FCT grew strongly in the first nine months but was hit in Q4 by cancelled international artist concerts. Management reiterated that Gaana should reach breakeven in FY27 and recommended a dividend of INR2 per share.

financial_highlights.value: INR22 crore (includes INR17.2 crore one-time deferred tax reversal)

segments.name: Radio (FCT)
segments.commentary: Demand stayed subdued through FY26 amid macro uncertainty and the Middle East conflict; volume market share cited at 25.2% (25.6% in a later answer). International operations, especially the Middle East, were hit. Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore.

segments.name: Non-FCT (events and experiential)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR148 crore; grew strongly in the first nine months (described as double digit) but Q4 was hit by travel constraints and cancellation of some international artist concerts. Q4 non-FCT revenue was about INR38 crore.

segments.name: Digital (Gaana and pure digital)
segments.commentary: FY26 digital revenue INR112.4 crore (+84%), about 48% of radio revenue. Q4 pure digital revenue about INR29 crore (+61%) per one answer, while Gaana Q4 revenue about INR21 crore (+42%). Gaana revenue has been roughly flat at about INR20 crore in the last two quarters per the analyst; management cited 10-15% sequential growth from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gaana: management targets operating breakeven in FY27, with a possibility of achieving it within FY26 itself; quarterly losses have been reduced sequentially.
Gaana subscriber growth expected to continue at about 15% CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with focus on unit economics over subscriber count.
Gaana pricing: annual plan raised to INR799 from INR499; management sees headroom toward a steady-state price of about INR1,200 a year.
Dividend of INR2 per share recommended for FY26; management said the company will keep evaluating inorganic opportunities.
Radio and experiential business expected to recover; management called the Q4 shortfall momentary.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call.
Radio volume market share cited at 25.2% in prepared remarks and 25.6% in a later answer; management said it may have gained some basis points.
Radio inventory utilisation described as roughly flat quarter on quarter in Q4; effective rates (ERs) said to be at similar levels, not up since COVID.

Non-FCT events and experiential business is the capacity-linked segment; Q4 hit by event disruptions, execution delays and cancelled international artist concerts, with recovery expected from the H2-heavy event calendar.
Digital spend reduced 23% YoY in FY26; management said it would keep investing in digital and evaluating inorganic opportunities, with no specific capex amount given.
demand_pricing: Radio demand subdued through FY26 because of macro uncertainty and the West Asia conflict, which weighed on advertiser sentiment.
Gaana annual subscription raised to INR799 (from INR499); music label variable content cost cited at 60-70% of revenue.
Management said customer acquisition costs have risen across the subscription market; CAC and LTV figures were not disclosed.
Management estimates India's paid music subscribers at about 15 million (from about 8 million two years earlier, per EY-FICCI), against a 80-100 million paid-subscription pool across video/OTT.
Competition from free offerings such as YouTube and bundled products was cited; one competitor cut prices sharply in Q3 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business plan and subscriber trajectory for Gaana over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 15% subscriber CAGR to continue for 2-3 years, prioritises profitable growth over subscriber count, and sees FY27 as the year to reach breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Gaana Q4 and FY26 revenue split, and FCT/non-FCT split?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital revenue in Q4 was about INR21 crore (+42%) and INR81 crore for FY26 (+71%). Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore and non-FCT about INR38 crore. Volume growth was described as flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gaana revenue look flat over the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is seasonal Q3/Q4 churn, that prices were cut and then raised, and that revenue grew about 10-15% sequentially from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose CAC-to-LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share CAC or LTV metrics on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the income tax notice of INR111 crore about?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Ballabh said the notice relates to FY2023-24, with a demand of about INR113 crore after the department passed an order ignoring submissions; the company plans to appeal to the CIT and further authorities and is confident of the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line fall about INR15 crore in Q4 and how is radio doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said radio volume share is about 25.6% and possibly up slightly; the Q4 drop came mainly from non-FCT events after international concerts were cancelled. First nine months of non-FCT grew double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How many paid music subscribers are there and how long to reach the 100 million pool?
qa_highlights.answer: Music paid subscribers are about 15 million per the EY-FICCI report; management said timing depends on behaviour change and could not give a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash deployment or inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will pursue profitable growth rather than burn cash, is evaluating inorganic opportunities, and has kept dividends rising.

Q4 non-FCT weakness from geopolitical disruption and cancelled international artist concerts; watch recovery in events revenue.
Gaana Q4 sequential growth was modest, and CAC is rising; breakeven in FY27 depends on subscriber growth and pricing.
Middle East international radio operations remain disrupted.

532720|2026-09.headline: M&M Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 55% YoY to INR 882 crore, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% and credit cost at 1.6%.
532720|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as steady across growth, margin and risk, with disbursements up 22% YoY and AUM up 15% YoY. Asset quality improved, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% (near all-time lows) and inter-quarter volatility reduced; credit cost was 1.6% against a 1.3-1.7% guided range. ROA was about 2.2% in the quarter (H1 about 2.3%), dented by excess liquidity buffers and high trade advances, while cost of funds is expected to rise after one 25 bps repo hike with more hikes priced in. Management said it sees no change to its FY31 targets of 16-18% AUM growth, 1.3-1.7% credit cost and 2.2-2.5% ROA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-of-funds trajectory for FY27 given the rate hike and liquidity holdings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects cost of funds to rise after one 25 bps hike and more priced in; a 25 bps move resets about 10 bps of floating stock within a quarter. Refinancing is at higher rates. Some liquidity buffer flexibility exists but not large.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory after a flat H1 with no seasonality: could it drop below 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1.3-1.7%, citing existing stock keeping H2 GS3 stable and rural cash flows improving in Q3-Q4. The INR 852 crore overlay is adequate and no further buffer is planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trade advance increase in others (8.2% of AUM) driving growth visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, trade advances were deployed at a clear level above normal to support Q3 festive growth. Personal loans to existing customers are also building; prime housing started in August and will be disclosed separately later.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on tractor collections in drought-affected states such as Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call: tractor half-yearly instalments fall due at end of rabi/kharif and collections are not yet at that point. Teams are assessing stress case by case; management does not plan to change its tractor stance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the housing finance merger and mortgage push change returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is an early drag on ROA but seen as strategic; management noted the HFC-NBFC cost-of-funds arbitrage is narrowing and cited the merger rationale of simplifying duplicated functions.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM fall below 7% in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM expansion will be hard; loan income should recover as trade advances and excess liquidity convert, and fee income has some headroom. Half-year loan income reflects the run-rate better than Q2 alone.

532725|2026-03.headline: Solar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR3,053 crore (+41% YoY) with EBITDA INR870 crore at ~28.5% margin; FY27 revenue target INR14,000 crore.
532725|2026-03.overview: Solar Industries reported record quarterly and annual sales of INR3,053 crore and INR9,838 crore, with Q4 EBITDA up 59% YoY to INR870 crore and PAT up 61% to INR556 crore. Defence revenue nearly doubled, reaching INR1,008 crore in Q4 (+134% YoY) and INR2,634 crore for FY26 (+94%). Management guided to INR14,000 crore revenue in FY27 while maintaining current EBITDA margins, backed by a INR21,300 crore order book. Working capital days rose above the 90-100 day range in Q4 on deliberate inventory build, which management expects to normalise over about two quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on Africa, with South Africa as hub and facilities in Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe; Nigeria base with Ghana started; Sierra Leone expected this year. Turkey and Kazakhstan are also active, with Southeast Asia and Australia smaller.

qa_highlights.answer: Bhargavastra final-stage development; all trials expected in calendar 2026. 155 mm complete-round supply expected after the coupling facility is done in a couple of quarters plus 3-4 months.

532725|2026-06.headline: Solar Industries to acquire Omnia Holdings (South Africa) on an all-cash, 100% basis, funded by debt; ~$1.35bn deal value cited, FY28 leverage target below 2x EBITDA.
532725|2026-06.overview: This was a business update call on the proposed acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings Limited by Solar SA Investments (wholly owned step-down subsidiary), held as a transaction-only call, with no questions on core Solar operations taken. Management framed the deal as creating an integrated global explosives and blasting platform, adding mining (BME brand) and agriculture/agritech businesses, with benefits expected to be visible from FY28. Funding will be all-cash, through debt at Omnia level plus Solar-group debt and internal accruals, with no equity issuance planned. Management guided to combined FY28 revenue of about INR30,000-32,000 crore and EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore, and said net debt/EBITDA will stay below 2x. Many figures are management estimates pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, and structuring is not finalised.

532726|2026-09.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.

EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. Coal block allotment in Singrauli and a medium-term greenfield growth plan (to be presented in Q4 FY27) were the main strategic updates.

segments.name: Kutch (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Rolling mill utilisation 68% in Q2 vs 66% in Q1, a 2 percentage point rise. Management expects further structural improvement in Q3 and Q4.

Singrauli coal block allotted August 2026; due diligence under way with a one-month decision window. Operations would take about 2-3 years after a decision; Gorakhpur intended to move fully to this coal, replacing imported South African coal.

demand_pricing: Management says India finished steel consumption grew 7.5% to about 85 million tons in H1; construction steel demand up about 7% per management. India remained a net importer of finished steel.

532734|2026-03.headline: GPIL FY26 consolidated EBITDA flat at INR 1,253 crore, but Q4 EBITDA rose 91% QoQ to INR 439 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%.
532734|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and PAT were broadly stable, with consolidated PAT at INR 802 crore and EBITDA margin at 23%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 41% QoQ and PAT reached INR 280 crore, driven by higher pellet volumes, a one-time carry-over pellet inventory gain (about INR 20 crore) and March mining uplift after environmental clearance for Ari Dongri. Consolidated PAT was below standalone because Ardent Steel was de-recognised as an associate after the stake sale. Management guided FY27 revenue above INR 6,000 crore and EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels, while flagging price softness of about 10% in late April and early May.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: FY26 pellet output reached 95% of target. Pellet capacity rose from 2.7 to 4.7 million tons after the 2 million ton gas-based grate-kiln plant commissioned in December 2025; FY27 pellet guidance is 4 million tons, with about 3 million tons for merchant sales.

segments.name: Sponge iron
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26. Capacity is being expanded from 0.59 to 0.65 million tons under a CTO received from CECB.

segments.name: Structural rolled products / RR Ispat
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26 and rose sharply from Q4 after mill modifications finished at end-Q3; order book is about six months. Total FY27 rolled output is guided at about 3.7-3.75 lakh tons.

segments.name: Ferroalloys
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26; no further figures given on the call.

segments.commentary: Billets reached 96% of target in FY26; sales volumes for galvanised fabricated products increased over the year.

segments.commentary: Commissioning targeted March 2027, with long-term supply tie-ups with EVE Power (628 Ah LFP cells) and Shanghai Shenyi Roche. Phase-1 ramp is 5-6 GWh in FY28 (30-40%), about 12-14 GWh in FY29 and 17-18 GWh from FY30. Management guided a 7-8% margin, but said current margins are about 12-13%.

segments.name: CRM complex (0.7 million tons)
segments.commentary: Targeted commissioning March 2027; FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation, or 3-3.5 lakh tons. Management expects about 90% from FY29.

qa_highlights.answer: Carry-over pellet inventory of about 89,000 tons sold in Q4, the new pellet plant ramp to 70% and about 2-2.5 lakh extra tons of mining in March after EC approval.

qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised for an earlier estimation error. The increase reflects a coke oven plant (now needed after import curbs) and a value-added structural mill; EBITDA above 20% is expected at full capacity.

qa_highlights.answer: The first line is expected by end-Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation (3-3.5 lakh tons), with about 90% from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Milestones needed before the board revives the 1 mtpa integrated steel plant, and should it now be treated as optional growth?

qa_highlights.question: Will the mining production shortfall continue into Q2 and Q3, and when does merchant ore purchasing fall?

Mining ramps from Q3 and reaches full capacity by end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28. Merchant ore purchases stay at 25-30% in Q3, fall below 10% in Q4, and reach 100% captive in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the pellet plant shut, and is the gas issue expected to normalise after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas is fully supplied, but the PNGRB guideline has pushed gas purchase value up about 40-45%. Combined with market ore purchases, this made the plant commercially unviable, so one 2 mtpa plant was shut. No clarity on normalisation was given; GAIL has no guidelines, and August is expected to remain a shutdown month.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for iron ore and pellet prices, and what is the sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global iron ore is expected to hover at USD90-100/t, with management not expecting a fall below USD90 soon. Pellet prices were about INR10,000/t after a roughly 10% recovery from the early-July low of about INR8,700/t. Each INR100/t fall in pellet price cuts annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA benefit per tonne do beneficiation, EV fleet and mining cost cuts deliver from FY28?

532734|2026-09.headline: Godawari Power Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to ₹1,632 crore, but margins fell sharply on costlier purchased iron ore and coal; mining guidance cut to 2.5 Mt.
532734|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25% YoY to ₹1,632 crore in Q2 FY27 and 29% to ₹3,382 crore in H1, driven by volume and realisation. Profitability compressed because the company bought iron ore from the market at about ₹3,300-3,500/t while captive mining was constrained by overburden dumping space, and coal costs rose. Management cut FY27 iron ore mining guidance from 3.4 Mt to 2.5 Mt and pellet guidance from 4.4 Mt to 3.5 Mt, and expects margin recovery from Q4 FY27 once dumping land approval is received. The 20 GWh battery storage project is on track for commissioning around June-July 2027, and a new 3 GWh-scale BESS line was added.

segments.name: Iron ore mining and pellets
segments.commentary: Mining hit by overburden dumping space constraint; FY27 mining guidance cut to 2.5 Mt (from 3.4 Mt) and pellet guidance to 3.5 Mt (from 4.4 Mt). segments.name: Sponge iron, billets, steel (captive chain)
segments.commentary: Sponge iron capacity raised from 5.25 to 5.75 Mt, with near-100% captive use in billet making; management says non-pellet chain is performing, though DRI costs rose about ₹1,000/t.

segments.commentary: Captive power capacity expanding from 190 MW to 290 MW; 25 MW solar commissioned in late FY26, 100 MW solar delayed to December 2026. Lower captive power generation affected ferro alloys output in Q2.

segments.commentary: Project relocated from Chhattisgarh to Maharashtra (Marasa, 71.45 acres allotted). Commissioning now expected around December 2027, possibly stretching to March 2028; ₹100 crore container line approved, commissioning by March 2027.

₹100 crore EV capex for 50 vehicles at mines and plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing mine approval delays and the debt-funded capex, given margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the forest-land (dumping) permission could come any day; ₹500 crore of CRM capex is covered and about ₹900 crore free cash is available, with long-term loans also taken. No cash constraint is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop comes from purchased iron ore versus price movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Purchased iron ore at ~₹3,300-3,500/t, lost ~₹1,000/t premium on high-grade pellets and lower volumes; DRI cost up ~₹1,500/t and power cost up ₹25-30 crore per quarter. qa_highlights.answer: Q3 margins similar to Q2; Q4 improvement; normalised margins from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS plan and expected utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: A new subsidiary Davi Energy Solution was formed for tenders; 10-20% utilisation expected in year one for the 5 MWh container line, rising to 20-25% by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS project economics?
qa_highlights.answer: For the ₹1,400 crore BESS project at 80% utilisation, revenue about ₹1,300 crore and EBITDA about ₹600 crore per annum; payback about 3-3.5 years. Cell technology 6.28 MWh expected to save 4-5% operating cost.

qa_highlights.answer: Ad-Dongri reserve about 80 Mt, supporting full capacity for ~15 years; Pauri-Tipu about 75 Mt of low-grade ore, with only 25-30 Mt usable at 30-40% recovery; 4 Mt beneficiation planned.

532735|2026-03.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.
532735|2026-03.overview: Revenue grew 3.5% QoQ and 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore ($62.8 million), with Novigo consolidated for a full quarter and rupee depreciation supporting the numbers. Management said organic revenue was flat QoQ, citing fewer days and Q4 fixed-price true-ups, and that Novigo's restated revenue is about $21–22 million a year after accounting alignment versus the roughly $32 million quoted at acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 115.7 crore (20.1% margin), which management said is about 19% excluding the currency benefit. Utilisation was deliberately reduced to about 80.5% (from a peak of about 84%) to build AI and data bench and COE capacity. Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.

It views the frontier-lab services move as validation that AI is a people problem, and will assess competition as it develops.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q1 growth mainly from full-quarter Novigo consolidation, and is organic growth returning from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Novigo's accounting was aligned to R Systems policies, moving some licence revenue from gross to net and changing fixed-price accounting. Restated Novigo revenue is about $21–22 million a year versus about $32 million at acquisition. Organic growth was flat QoQ, attributed to fewer days and Q4 true-ups, and management said it sees no challenge to positive outlook for Q2.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the venture as early-stage and as validation of its playbooks; Blackstone portfolio access gives a faster path to some companies, but deals are still won on merit against competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A fall, and what is the normal run rate?

Full-year FY26 revenue was USD 6,385M (+0.6% cc) and operating margin expanded 290 bps to 12.6%. qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth rely on telecom mega deals, and how will the company diversify away from telecom?

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between fixed-price and T&M, and how will surplus margin be used?

532755|2026-06.headline: Tech Mahindra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.66bn with operating margin at 14.4%, and deal wins hit US$1.078bn.
532755|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 2.2% QoQ and 6.1% YoY in reported USD (6.6% YoY constant currency), with every vertical growing YoY. EBIT margin rose 60 bps QoQ and 330 bps YoY to 14.4%, led by volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partly offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix. Management said Q1 was stronger than expected, helped by early delivery on a European automotive programme that it expects to reverse in Q2. Management reiterated its FY27 ambition of growth above the peer average and an operating margin of 15%, with Q4 margin expected above 15%.

financial_highlights.change: +16.2% YoY in USD; PAT margin +80 bps YoY

segments.commentary: Grew 1.3% YoY; held back by Comviva Q1 seasonality and a cloud pass-through that a client pulled back after a takeover. Management expects the pass-through impact to fade in Q2, and one large deal has not yet ramped.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 8.1% YoY and 2.7% QoQ. Acquisition of Avant Techno Solutions (Canada, payments modernisation and wealth platforms) was announced in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew 17.2% YoY and 9% QoQ, helped by aerospace and early delivery on a large European automotive programme. Management called the auto delivery acceleration a timing benefit, not a one-off, with a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure expected next quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew 8.6% YoY; management described the macro as mixed.

Wage increases to take effect from Q2 in a phased manner.
Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing volatility; it said it expects to exceed peer-average growth, by an amount it did not quantify.

Management said it is investing in centres of excellence in Hyderabad (learning, engineering, retail CPG) and will calibrate investment to growth opportunities.
Investing in talent, IP and software licences; deals are screened to be margin-accretive over the long term.
Headcount in IT services fell 7% YoY because of AI-led productivity gains in fixed-price work. Management expects hiring to resume in the rest of FY27, mixing fresh and experienced talent.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,078 million, with the largest coming from manufacturing and HLS. Management said the pipeline looks strong but that large deals are binary and hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two.

Demand strengthening in ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and data and AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI). Weakness seen in manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM and legacy infrastructure admin.

Management walked away from deals with 70%-80% productivity benefits over 5-7 year contracts and from fixed price guarantees on infrastructure, citing memory and chip price inflation of about 20% YoY.
Auto sector: some customers are cutting costs with AI. Auto finance was resilient. Aerospace demand is rising, especially in IT and engineering.

BPS: AI operations made up most of the BPS deal TCV this quarter, including a large AI-led engagement with a high-tech client. Some clients are questioning in-house versus outsourcing decisions on multi-year deals, but management said it is not seeing outsized delays or cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth momentum carry into Q2 without the Comviva seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months, offset by a European auto slowdown; it expects to meet or exceed the peer-average growth for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion lever remains, and what is the exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an exit target, but said Q4 margin must be above 15%. Levers are gross margin from Project Fortius plus SG&A gains from portfolio company consolidation. Q1 had seasonal visa and travel costs and Comviva seasonality as negatives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO and free cash flow improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of Q1 was helped by accelerated customer payments and FX on receivables, which will normalise. Management said working capital remains a priority with a long-term improvement trend, though quarterly seasonality will persist.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Comms ramp impact is in Q1, and what is the full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: One of the two large Comms deals has not ramped at all yet, so impact comes in later quarters. Management said it would not give a specific full-year growth number, given the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Was the strong quarter a plan or a surprise, and is demand improving or is share being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarter was stronger than expected, helped by the European auto acceleration. It described a shift in demand toward modernisation and platform work, with the core stable and no 'SaaS eclipse' seen; it remains cautiously optimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Given the pricing comparisons with peers, can 15% margins go higher, and what competitor irrationality exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% is the target for FY27, with a path beyond FY27 to be set. Examples of irrational pricing included 70%-80% productivity assumptions in 5-7 year deals and holding infrastructure prices amid about 20% YoY inflation.

532762|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 15% QoQ to INR1,021 crore, but FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.33%; management plans 9-10% price hikes to offset 11-14% cost inflation.
532762|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the company's best ever revenue quarter, with total income of INR1,021 crore (up 15% QoQ, 5.58% YoY) and EBITDA of INR163.7 crore (16% margin). FY26 total income was flat at about INR3,395 crore, with EBITDA up about 4% to INR622 crore and PAT up 5.4% to INR425 crore. Other income was negative in Q4 on mark-to-market losses on surplus-cash investments, and March brought West Asia-driven steel and crude cost inflation. Management is taking staged price increases and has withheld annual guidance until the middle of Q2.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% to around INR251 crore in FY26, with margins at about 1%.

segments.commentary: Separately reported line of about INR76.55 crore; management said it is mainly miscellaneous exports, including some construction equipment, and no volume figure is available.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: management expects growth of 15-20% or slightly more, helped by a low base in Q1 FY26; no full-year guidance given until the middle of Q2.
Pricing: 1-1.5% hike in January, about 4% from 1 May, and a further 5% from 1 June (total 9-10%); management sees total cost inflation of 11-14% and may take another 3-4% later in Q2.
Margins: target EBITDA ex-other income of 15-16%; management said expanding margins beyond about 17-18% including other income would hurt market share.
Other income expected to recover to INR20-35 crore in Q1 FY27 if markets hold or improve, after partial April recovery of March mark-to-market losses.
Defense: execution of about INR200-220 crore in FY27 (5-6% of revenue vs about 3% last year); about INR575 crore order book; rough terrain forklift/telehandler execution to start next quarter.

Long-term: INR6,000-6,200 crore revenue target by FY29 (worst case FY30) implies adding about INR700-800 crore a year; exports plus defense targeted at 10-15% of the segment, with about 11-13% expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment is about 60%.

Tower crane capacity is about 950-1,000 units a year versus about 680-690 units produced in FY26 (FY25 comparison not given).
demand_pricing: Tower crane order books are full; demand is strong into the start of Q1, with slowdown usually beginning mid-to-late June during monsoon.

Hydra-type cranes (about 60% of the market) shrank in FY26 on emission-norm skepticism and are recovering since January-February; management expects higher volumes in backhoe loaders and construction equipment.
Price realisation per unit rose on a mix shift to higher tonnage cranes; emission-transition costs added an estimated 5-7% to blended cost per unit.
About INR40-50 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to Middle East-bound export shipments stuck in India and March delivery deferrals.

Competition: Chinese players are absent from pick-and-carry cranes (below 30-35 tonnes) and compete in slew/heavy cranes (40-50+ tonnes), offering 1-2 year credit terms; competitor segment margins are about 8-9% versus about 18-19% for ACE.
Anti-dumping duties of 25-52% on Chinese cranes were recommended by DGTR in September 2025 but not notified by the Finance Ministry; the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of LD implementation and Chinese competition in pick-and-carry cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese players do not make pick-and-carry cranes; they compete in heavy slew cranes (40-50+ tonnes). The anti-dumping order was not notified, and the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments large and what is their size?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash is invested in secured, listed bonds with 1-3 year tenures, classified as non-current under accounting rules but saleable; the amount is about INR700-750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR76.55 crore 'others' revenue and the impairment line?
qa_highlights.answer: 'Others' is miscellaneous exports, reported separately by the auditors. Impairment is a prudent expected-credit-loss provision on slightly delayed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on investments at March month-end; partly recovered in April. Management expects INR20-35 crore of other income in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes grow 10%+ in FY27 and what are price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 growth of 15-20% or more is possible on a low base; annual guidance is deferred to mid-Q2. Price hikes total 9-10% with another 3-4% possible, against 11-14% cost inflation (steel about 65% of cost, up 20-22% since January).

qa_highlights.question: What is the KATO JV revenue potential and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue of about INR300 crore in 3-4 years under current conditions, potentially INR700-800 crore if anti-dumping duties are imposed. Chinese imports are priced 25-30% below Indian-made costs, aided by credit terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and tower crane factory timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR200 crore; a INR400 crore tower crane factory is need-based, with a 12-18 month build.

532762|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose about 19% to INR836 crore and EBITDA rose 19.66% to INR170.58 crore at a 20.40% margin, with management guiding no margin expansion.

Segment revenue for Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling rose about 22% to INR738.37 crore, while Agri Equipment booked INR42.67 crore. Commodity inflation (steel up nearly 20%, plus rubber, tyres, plastics and freight) compressed gross margin by about 140 bps YoY, which management is offsetting with price hikes totalling about 10% so far. Management declined to give a full-year revenue growth number until end-September, citing demand unpredictability and price resistance.

demand_pricing: Demand was strong till May-June 2026, and softened in the monsoon. Management says it expects growth in Hydra crane volumes (price increases and technology change had suppressed them in FY26).

Price actions: about 1-1.5% in January, 3-4% in March, and 5-6% in June (still being implemented, due to complete in July). Cumulative about 9-10%, with another 2% possible.

Commodity inflation: steel up nearly 20%, plus tyres, belts, rubber and plastics. Management estimates Q1 raw-material inflation at about 5-6% (7-8% flowed through per Sorab Agarwal), with more to hit Q2.

Predictability is the main issue; management cites the Iran/West Asia war, US tariffs and erratic monsoon. A deficient monsoon could cut Tier 2 and rural demand by 5-10%, with the effect showing in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much did defence and export orders contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the visibility for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Export was about 3% and defence about 5% of Q1 revenue. For FY27, management expects exports 6-7% or more and defence 5-6%, so the combined share will be about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can you update on the KATO JV?

qa_highlights.question: Is the defence order target of about INR200 crore still on track?

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation did you see in Q1, and what is expected in Q2? Will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflation is expected at 11-12% in total, with about 10% booked. Management says there is no plan for margin expansion, only cost recovery. Price increases and inflation are expected to align by July-August.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin down about 140 bps YoY?

qa_highlights.answer: Tower crane expansion will be decided in September (start October or defer 6 months). Plant 9 is due by end-December, with turnover of about INR500 crore, and capex for the year is INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: No leads so far. Management believes the DGTR recommended the duty, but the Finance Ministry did not implement it, and says it is still hopeful.

Management says LAP demand is strong with a stable rejection rate; about one-third of LAP borrowers are arbitrage cases, a third seek better products and the rest need more exposure.
Gold prices are fairly stable at around INR 14,560 per gram (999 gold). Management names gold price decline as the main risk.
Management cites a bancassurance fee drop as the main earnings headwind, and said other levers will be needed to offset it.

qa_highlights.question: Is opex growth elevated, and will headcount reach 13,000 with 20 branches added this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was driven by people costs and normal cyber-security tech spend, with no one-offs. Headcount is 12,002 and is expected to reach about 12,800-12,900 by year-end; about 20 branches are planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline QoQ, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus liquidity from the FCNR(B) raise was carried for most of the quarter; lending yield fell 2 bps QoQ. Management expects NIM to improve in Q3 and Q4 as repo-linked loans reprice in November, and as credit costs stay low.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gold loan book growing faster than disbursements, and are gold slippages rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth includes inorganic DA and co-lending, while disbursement figures are organic only. Non-gold slippage rose to 1.55% from 1.52%. Management said some co-lending and DA partners collect before NPA, so the 1 DPD rule does not apply to many of them.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-FCNR(B), what was the lending yield and margin, and will the expansion continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an ex-FCNR NIM figure. It said lending yield fell 2 bps and that yield should rise with repo hikes, with a fairly decent NIM expansion expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL readiness and impact on PCR and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: A Big 4 firm has been appointed; the ECL model is expected to be live by March. Management said lead indicators are positive except SMA-1 and SMA-2, and sees credit-cost gains from SMA reduction after ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA/ROE guidance be revised, and how will bancassurance fee loss be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to set a new ROE target until capital comes in; it expects ROE above 13.5%. On bancassurance, it cited the prior loss of about INR 100 crore of treasury gains and said it will wait for final norms and build offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Is gold loan CIBIL screening relaxed, and what is the risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Low CIBIL is not a bar for gold loans; management uses it to profile customers. The main risk is a fall in gold prices, and auction recovery was under 10% during the MFI stress, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How are the drought and agri books, and what is the mortgage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor and KCC books are about 4% each and collections remain robust, with no state above 20% of exposure. Management expects mortgage share to rise as gold is capped at 25% and overall growth is 18-20%.

risks_watch: Non-gold slippage edged up to 1.55%, and SMA-1 and SMA-2 are elevated; ECL transition and the related model risk are to be tested by March.
Gold loan book, co-lending and DA partner collection practices and gold price exposure.
Bancassurance commission drop under draft norms; management has not quantified the offset, and analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.
Capital raise: terms and price are not yet disclosed; management said it will not raise below book value.
NIM recovery depends on repo pass-through and on deposit repricing lagging asset repricing.
532772|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and firm on asset quality, cost and profitability. Management was evasive on NIM ex-FCNR(B), product-wise repricing mix, and the size and price of the capital raise, citing ongoing negotiations.
key_quotes: So we got more than what we deserve in terms of foreclose -- what you call, prepayment penalty, etcetera, and lesser interest rate.
Below the book value, we will not raise capital. That much I can tell you.
So it's about -- it's from that perspective that you'd be looking at the CIBIL.
So, we are stockpiling liquidity post February '26 Israel-Iran war.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Management said it is near closure on three components with a firm commitment expected before the next investor call, the bank has not raised equity since 2017, and it will not raise below book value; size and price undisclosed.

532777|2026-03.headline: Info Edge Q4 FY26 standalone billings rose 7% to Rs.1,057 crore and revenue 17% to Rs.805 crore, with 99acres billings flat at 2%.
532777|2026-03.overview: Standalone operating profit rose 39% YoY to Rs.323 crore at a 40% margin, helped by a one-time Rs.20.5 crore 99acres warranty provision write-back that lifted revenue. Recruitment billings grew 10% standalone (9% including Zwayam and DoSelect) amid a subdued hiring market, with GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4. 99acres billings grew only 2% after a sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls, while traffic share rose to 49% web and 52% in April. Management guided to double-digit Naukri topline growth as the threshold for holding margins, and said 99acres should turn cash-generative in FY27 if execution holds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring sentiment across GCCs, IT and non-IT, and what is driving 99acres margins and share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitesh Oberoi called the market lukewarm; larger GCCs have shrunk headcount while smaller ones hire. Share gains credited to execution, with 13-14 points added to traffic share in recent months; new-home responses up 33% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-time reversal of over-provisioned warranty on cost-per-lead products, which did not affect billings. Provision will move from 20% to 5% of leads going forward; the write-back was not expected to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from AI tools, a self-serve shift away from telecalling and a counter-cyclical lift as hiring slowed. Management was surprised by 30% growth after one quarter and said it was unsure whether it would sustain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is similar to Apna and WorkIndia but more freemium. It is monetising in Delhi NCR and will expand to Mumbai and Bangalore; management targets about 100% YoY growth for several years.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Naukri margins hold at 10%+ topline growth; 99acres aim is 60% share, doubling billings in 3 years and reaching 25-30% EBITDA margin. Management said Q1 should recover but near-term markets may slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the adoption and willingness to pay for AI-Rex, and how does 99acres gain share in new homes?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex was made free to many recruiters after B2B sales friction; it has 30,000 mandates, with 1% take rate targeted. New-home share gains come from secondary-market traffic plus 99Shorts video content.

risks_watch: 99acres Q1 FY27 billings recovery after the 2% Q4 growth and the sales reorganisation; the one-time write-back will not repeat.

GCC and IT hiring softness, with larger GCCs shrinking headcount and GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4.

Matchmaking pricing pressure from competitors' discounting; Jeevansathi operating loss of Rs.4 crore in FY26.

532777|2026-06.headline: Info Edge Q1 FY27: standalone billings up over 14% and recruitment billings up 17%, with underlying recruitment billings growth at about 15%.

Naukri recruitment billings grew 17%, which management says is about 15% after adjusting for renewal timing, with revenue up 13% and a 58% operating PBT margin. 99acres billings grew 17% and its operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores, near break-even. Shiksha billings fell 23% on AI-driven search traffic loss, and matchmaking grew billings 20% and was near break-even.

segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled on a small base; about Rs.15 crores revenue last year, burn near Rs.50 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 13% revenue growth is from realisation versus customer count, and how much from AI products?

qa_highlights.question: Is the normalised 15% recruitment billings growth adjusted for the favourable Q1 FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said normalisation nets out early and deferred renewals each quarter, which captures the prior-year base effect. GCC billings grew 31% reported, with about 2.5% of one-off timing shift from Q4 FY26 deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying separately for AI-Rex, and is there cannibalisation?

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-Rex renewal cycle and how is value measured?

532777|2026-09.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
532777|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri)
segments.commentary: Q2 billings +13%, revenue +13%, operating profit +20% at 59% operating PBT margin; H1 billings +15%. Q2 IT/Tech/BPM billings +3%, GCCs +7%, other sectors +18%, consultants +7%. Naukri 360 billings +37%; Job Hai billings +86%; NaukriGulf +9% at about 36% margin.

532784|2026-03.headline: Sobha FY26 real estate sales hit a record INR8,136 crore (+~30%), with Q4 EBITDA of INR194 crore and FY27 sales growth guided at a similar ~30%.
532784|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: real estate sales of INR8,136 crore at an average realisation of INR14,675 per sq ft (up 9.4% from INR13,412), and 3,188 homes (5.4 million sq ft) delivered, up about 19%. Q4 revenue recognition improved after occupancy certificates delayed in Q3 were received, with Q4 total income of INR2,030 crore, EBITDA of INR194 crore and PAT of INR92 crore. Net operating cash flow was INR1,637 crore for FY26 (up 39.4%) and the company moved to a net cash position of about INR800 crore. Management expects margins to improve through FY27, with projects nearing completion guided at 24-26% margins against a 30%+ EBITDA margin on the overall unrecognised revenue of INR18,647 crore. Some FY26 launches slipped, and the Rivana (Greater Noida) launch and the Crescent (Gurgaon) launch in April were the main new-launch data points.

segments.commentary: Record annual sales of about INR4,500 crore, with both new launches and sustenance sales contributing.

segments.name: NCR (Gurgaon, Greater Noida)
segments.commentary: Record annual sales of about INR2,450 crore, helped by the Greater Noida expansion; Bangalore and NCR together made up about 85% of sales.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Steady at about INR800 crore of sales in FY26.

segments.name: Other regions
segments.commentary: About INR400 crore of sales in FY26.

segments.name: Non-real estate (manufacturing, contracting, retail)
segments.commentary: Management says these performed steadily; collections of INR732 crore in FY26 and INR183 crore in Q4, with an expectation of similar run rate and better profitability.

FY27 net operating cash flow target close to INR2,000 crore.
Launches of about 10 million sq ft planned in FY27 across Bangalore, Gurgaon, Hyderabad, Thrissur and Pune; a 20.67 million sq ft pipeline over the next 6-8 quarters.
Margins expected to improve through FY27, higher toward Q3 and Q4, as projects nearing completion are recognised at 24-26% margins versus 30%+ EBITDA margin on total unrecognised revenue.
FY27 sales mix guided at roughly 45-50% from sustenance and 50-55% from new launches.
Business development spend of about INR1,100-1,200 crore expected in FY27, with pending land payments cleared in H1; targets a pipeline of at least 10 million sq ft a year.
Projected marginal cash flow of INR9,560 crore from completed and ongoing projects, and INR8,699 crore from forthcoming projects.
capex_capacity: Hoskote (Bangalore) residential project: about 5.3 million sq ft, GDV about INR7,000 crore; Phase 1 expected to launch in Q1 FY27 after RERA; at least half of Phase 1 to be released initially, with ~INR3,500 crore potentially launching depending on demand.

Rivana (Greater Noida): about 2.5 million sq ft, 1,384 units; Phase 1 of 684 units launched in late March 2026, with about 25% sold; execution started. Crescent (Gurgaon) Phase 1 launched in April 2026, about 50% sold, about INR1,100 crore.
Q2 FY27 launches planned in Calicut and Thrissur (Kerala); a Bangalore row-house project was cancelled and is being relaunched as apartments toward year-end.
About 2 million to 2.5 million sq ft of rental/commercial space planned in the next few years on land in Hoskote and Gurgaon; Hoskote Phase 2 and 3 to include commercial.
Tentative Pune and Chennai launches toward year-end; Hyderabad second project awaiting approvals, targeted this year.
demand_pricing: Pricing described as stable for 3-4 quarters, with NCR and Bangalore both stabilising; management expects growth mainly from volume.
Management says leading indicators (inquiries, site visits) are stable and there is no big slowdown from AI concerns for the sub-INR3 crore ticket band, though demand is not at the 2021-23 peak.
Launch pricing for FY27 assumed at about INR15,000 per sq ft; FY27 GDV from the ~10 million sq ft launches estimated at about INR15,000 crore.

Management flagged commodity and material price increases from the geopolitical situation; the margin impact is not yet quantified and will be reviewed in 3-6 months. Escalation clauses have not yet been exceeded.
Labour shortage was temporary, caused by state elections in four states.
Kerala inquiries improved slightly, given that much of its demand comes from the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins and EBITDA still below historical guidance, and when will they expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise as ongoing projects complete at end of Q2 and Q3 FY27, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be far better, in line with the projected EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hoskote project size, GDV and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5.3 million sq ft of residential space with a GDV of about INR7,000 crore; RERA expected in Q1 FY27 and the launch is at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Row House project converted to apartments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a better use of the land, with higher ticket sizes, higher realisation and margins, and it will add to sales value.

qa_highlights.question: How are Rivana and Crescent performing and why was Rivana weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Rivana sold about 25% of its launched inventory (~INR500 crore) and Crescent about 50% (~INR1,100 crore). Management attributed the gap to the timing of the Rivana launch in late March amid uncertainty, rather than to demand, and said sustenance sales are good.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 sales split between sustenance and new launches, and what is the GDV of the FY27 launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustenance is expected at 45-50% and new launches at 50-55%. About 10 million sq ft of launches is roughly INR15,000 crore GDV, and with about INR1,200-1,300 crore of unreleased inventory the total is about INR27,000-28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost inflation is expected and can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost inflation is event-led and its duration is unknown; the impact will be assessed over 3-6 months, and price increases depend on demand-supply, so it is in a wait-and-watch mode.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rental and annuity income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees about 2-2.5 million sq ft of rental space on land already held in Hoskote and Gurgaon, with a decision on a separate rental vertical expected to be visible within a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Launch slippage: some FY26 launches were delayed, and FY27 relies on about 10 million sq ft of launches, including Hoskote (INR7,000 crore GDV) whose Phase 1 needs RERA in Q1.
Margin recovery depends on project completions in Q2-Q3 FY27 and on absorbing commodity and material cost increases from the geopolitical situation.
Rivana sustenance pace after its ~25% launch sell-through; Phase 2 timing depends on demand.
Bangalore FSI change remains unresolved in the courts; management has not given a timeline.
Business development: Hyderabad and Mumbai have few current land parcels, with only two small Mumbai deals (about INR2,000 crore GDV) targeted this year.
Demand sensitivity to AI-related IT/ITeS job concerns and the macro environment in Bangalore.

532784|2026-06.headline: Sobha Q1 FY27 record presales of INR3,656 crore (+76% YoY) and PAT of INR50.7 crore vs INR13.5 crore a year earlier.
532784|2026-06.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly real estate sales of INR3,656 crore on 2.34 million sq ft and 1,432 homes, at an average realisation of INR15,655 per sq ft. Total income rose about 48% YoY to INR1,330 crore and real estate revenue rose about 60% to INR1,107 crore. Net cash stood at INR659 crore, with operational cash inflow of INR1,924 crore, though collections lagged presales because new-sale cash came late in the quarter and milestone billing slipped on labour shortages in April and May. Management reiterated margin recovery from H2 FY27, with EBITDA guided to 17-20% by Q4 from 9.7% currently.

segments.name: NCR
segments.commentary: Record quarterly sales of about INR1,384 crore, mainly from SOBHA Crescent in Gurgaon, where about 60% was sold in Q1.

segments.name: Contractual, manufacturing and retail
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR171 crore; management expects FY27 other-business revenue similar to FY26. Commercial rental income about INR23 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales growth of at least 30% guided; could be slightly better if all launches happen on time.
FY27 completions targeted at 6-6.5 million sq ft vs 5.4 million sq ft in FY26 (about 20% higher).
Launch of 9 projects, about 8.2 million sq ft (about INR12,000 crore GDV at about INR15,000 crore per 1 million sq ft basis) in the remaining nine months; roughly 3 projects in Q2, rest in Q3 and Q4.
Net debt expected to be around zero for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What presales growth and launch GDV are expected for FY27, and which projects come next?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 30% presales growth guided; about 9 projects, 8.2 million sq ft, in the remaining nine months, with about 3 projects in Q2 and the rest in Q3-Q4. Roughly INR12,000 crore GDV from the 8.2 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Why were collections modest versus presales?
qa_highlights.answer: New-sale collections came late in the quarter, and milestone billing was lower because some milestones were missed due to labour shortages in April and May.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the forthcoming-project margin fall from about INR86 billion to INR68.3 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Greater mix of joint development projects, and Hoskote (own land, high margin) dropped from the forthcoming set.

qa_highlights.question: Land spend and business development plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 land spend about INR1,160 crore; FY27 about INR370 crore so far, with INR600-700 crore more identified (mostly Bangalore, rest NCR and Mumbai). Total could reach INR1,500-1,600 crore. Land typically about 15% of sales value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the demand recovery in the second half of the quarter, and what about Rivana?
qa_highlights.answer: Preparation time for launches drove the stronger response; demand described as steady. Rivana sales steady with no spike at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 similar to Q1; Q3 and Q4 sequentially better as high-margin projects complete. EBITDA to move from 9.7% to 17-20% by Q4.

NCD issue of INR1,000 crore approved, to be drawn in at least 2 tranches tied to land deals.

532796|2026-09.headline: Lumax Auto Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% y-o-y to INR 1,556 crore, with PAT up 50% to INR 117 crore; FY27 growth guided to 20-25%.
532796|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 35% y-o-y and 14% q-o-q, with EBITDA of INR 228 crore (14.7% margin, broadly flat y-o-y). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR 2,919 crore (+34%), EBITDA INR 434 crore (+42%, margin 14.9%, up 90 bps) and PAT INR 215 crore (+64%). Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to 20-25% growth (near INR 6,000 crore), with H2 growth of 15-20%, and said the order book rose to INR 1,879 crore. Margin dilution in Q2 was attributed to input-cost pass-through lag of about one quarter.

segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% y-o-y to INR 1,655 crore from INR 1,138 crore; IAC is about 60% of the division. Order book INR 834 crore. Contributes 44% of total order book.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 45% y-o-y to INR 177 crore from INR 122 crore; order book INR 512 crore. Management says margins are in line with the overall company. Contributes 27% of order book.

segments.name: Structures & Control Systems
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 24% y-o-y to INR 476 crore from INR 380 crore; order book about INR 150 crore. Contributes 8% of order book.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 9% y-o-y to INR 234 crore from INR 216 crore; Q2 growth was 11%. Non-lighting category weakened as input-cost increases were passed on.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 30% y-o-y to INR 220 crore from INR 170 crore; order book INR 379 crore. Contributes 20% of order book. Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 for M&M.

segments.name: Lumax Industries (LIL) wiring business
segments.commentary: Reported H1 revenue flat y-o-y because one product line moved to in-house supply by LIL; management says like-for-like growth is about 25-30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided at 20-25% y-o-y, implying roughly INR 6,000 crore; H2 FY27 growth expected at 15-20% y-o-y due to higher FY26 base.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance unchanged; management expects current margins to be sustained for the rest of the year.
FY28 absolute EBITDA target of about INR 1,000 crore reaffirmed.

North Star: 20% revenue CAGR FY25-FY31, with EBITDA margin moving toward 20% over 5-7 years; FY31 revenue aspiration about INR 11,000 crore. Organic CAGR of about 20% now seen as achievable if industry momentum holds.
Margin ambition of a further 100-200 bps over the next few years, toward 17-18%.

Capex guidance for FY27 around INR 300 crore, including greenfield expansions in Mechatronics, Advanced Plastics and Alternate Fuels; SOP expected in H2 FY27. Effective tax rate about 25%; minority interest about 11% of PAT.
capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in H1 FY27 was INR 60 crore; full-year capex guided at about INR 300 crore.

Board approved (24 Oct 2026) a new Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, with capex of about INR 150 crore funded by debt and internal accruals; commissioning in two phases from Q3 FY28, peak turnover about INR 500 crore.

Greenfuel Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 (ferrule-less tubes, fittings, receptacles) for M&M; Maruti Suzuki firm orders also won. Capacity expected to be significantly utilised by M&M and Maruti over about 2 years.
IAC Chakan Plant IV is in SOP phase; product launches expected around December 2026 to January 2027. Efficiency gains from centre-of-competence concept to be quantified after launch.
demand_pricing: Management cites industry Q2 FY27 production growth (SIAM): overall +19% y-o-y to 106 lakh units; PV +25% to about 17 lakh; 2W +17% to 81 lakh; 3W +25% to about 4.5 lakh; CV +34% to 3.5 lakh. Growth expected to moderate in H2.

Inflation: input costs (crude-linked polymers, electronic parts, freight, rupee) are rising. Most cost increases are passed to OEMs with about a one-quarter lag; management says pass-through is complete, with a 30-40 bps EBITDA margin dilution in Q2.
Order book of INR 1,879 crore: about 14% to execute in FY27, 59% in FY28, 27% in FY29; about 85% is new business. EV and CNG together are 29% (CNG 20%, pure EV about 9%); future technologies 22%.

Content per vehicle: about INR 70,000-75,000 per PV and INR 20,000-22,000 per 2W; about 50% of PV content is in IAC; Greenfuel about INR 5,000-8,000 per vehicle. Mechatronics is about 20% of PV content; expected to rise about 10% in 2-3 years.
Aftermarket growth target of 15-20% over a 3-5 year horizon, despite weak H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance being raised after 34% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% y-o-y (about INR 6,000 crore), versus the earlier implied 12-14%. H2 growth is expected at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins face pressure in Q3, and is the FY28 EBITDA target of INR 1,000 crore on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through lags about one quarter, so margins dilute by a few bps. It remains confident of the FY28 INR 1,000 crore EBITDA target and of sustaining current margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% North Star revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31) still realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is now more confident of about 20% organic CAGR if industry growth holds. Inorganic growth could push it higher. The base year is FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Who develops the Body Control Module (BCM), and is it reported in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: BCM is a build-to-print standalone revenue stream since SOP in July 2026, with a INR 250 crore order book. Technology comes from a large Japanese electronics component maker, not a JV; it is reported under Mechatronics across standalone and subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV component strategy and the Aftermarket outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV focus is narrowed to 3-5 products, with active SOPs targeted for 2028-2030 and possible inorganic routes. Aftermarket grew 11% in Q2 and 9% in H1; the 15-20% target is over 3-5 years.

risks_watch: Input-cost inflation (crude-linked polymers, electronics, freight, rupee) and the one-quarter pass-through lag, which dilutes margin by 30-40 bps in Q2.
Festive-season demand sustainability and H2 moderation, with H2 growth guided at 15-20%.
Aftermarket weakness in non-lighting products, with H1 growth at 9%.
Mechatronics BCM ramp faces global competition and is in build-to-print phase; the Manesar plant is due Q3 FY28.
Dependence on JV partners for technology and IP (Mechatronics: about 75% of IP via JVs). One JV (with JOPP of Germany) was dissolved amicably in Q2.
Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and energy price volatility, flagged by management as key uncertainties.

we are quite confident of delivering the absolute guidance of EBITDA for FY 28, which was always at about INR 1,000 crore EBITDA.

532799|2026-03.headline: Hubtown guides FY27 pre-sales of ~6,000 crore and collections of ~3,000 crore; 25 South/Downtown debt expected to fall at least 35% by end-FY27.
532799|2026-03.overview: Management hosted its Q4 and FY26 analyst meet, focusing on the promoter-entity mergers, project launches and debt reduction. In FY26 the company sold about 1 million sq ft, mainly in Mumbai, for roughly 4,400 crore of pre-sales and collected about 1,900 crore. About 11,300 crore of unrecognised revenue from booked sales sits in existing projects, with substantial recognition expected in FY27 on project completions. Two of the three promoter-entity mergers are NCLT-approved and the third awaits exchange approval. Refinancing of the roughly 15% legacy debt has slowed due to Middle East market conditions, and the proposed equity placement at 341 was cancelled in favour of a possible QIP.

financial_highlights.change: Management said both pre-sales and collections improved vs previous years; no exact percentage given

financial_highlights.value: approx. 1 million sq ft, primarily Mumbai

financial_highlights.metric: Unrecognised revenue from booked sales (existing projects)

financial_highlights.change: Construction finance for 25 West from ICICI at 12%

segments.name: 25 South / 25 Downtown (merging entities)
segments.commentary: 25 South is about 95% sold and expected to complete in FY27; 25 Downtown has sold almost 1.1 million sq ft of carpet area. Combined debt of these two is about 4,000 crore and management expects at least 35% reduction by end of this year.

segments.name: 25 West (Bandra)
segments.commentary: Fifth tower launched, selling about 1,40,000 sq ft; first tower completion expected next year. Construction finance from ICICI at about 12%.

segments.name: Rising City (Ghatkopar)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (about 6.5 lakh sq ft): 5 of 6 towers have received OC; 6th tower OC expected in calendar 2026. Phase 2 (commercial offices) to be partly launched this year.

segments.name: Hubtown Seasons (Chembur)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 launch of about 500,000 sq ft expected this year, including a strata commercial building, one luxury and two mid-luxury buildings; phase 1 revenue expected in FY27.

segments.name: Mulund-Thane (Sunstream City)
segments.commentary: About 150 acres on seafront at Thane and Mulund, about 2.5 crore sq ft, not yet launched; environmental clearances being obtained and expected within months.

segments.name: Commercial (Gujarat and Pune)
segments.commentary: Four ongoing commercial projects in Pune, Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Baroda; three Gujarat projects expected to recognise substantial revenue this year.

Surplus collections to be used first to repay high-cost debt; at least 35% of combined 25 South and 25 Downtown debt expected to reduce by end of FY27.

Management says returns to shareholders and stakeholders will start coming from FY27 onwards.
Mergers: 25 West and Ghatkopar holding entity merger expected this year; 25 South/Downtown awaiting exchange approval. Effective date of all mergers is 1 April 2025.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 350 acres and over 35 million sq ft; delivered 47+ projects, mainly in MMR.
Total ongoing and unlaunched pipeline stated as in excess of 1 lakh crore GDV; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore.

Rising City Phase 2 commercial offices expected to do well given strong office market.
Management said price growth cannot be expected to be sharp, but prime-location product should avoid a cycle hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pro forma financing cost look high relative to combined debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest payable to DLF on Downtown's balance sheet was unprovided for 3-4 years due to disputes; it is now provisionally booked after settlement. Some further outflow until full repayment; Shapurji's share was small.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 15% cost of borrowing be refinanced lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing efforts continue but have slowed due to the last six months' market conditions and the Iran-US/Middle East situation; not expected in the immediate future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end FY27 debt level for 25 South?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is combined across 25 South and 25 Downtown, not only 25 South; at least 35% of the total should go down by end of this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total GDV of the launch and pipeline projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Total including unlaunched and ongoing projects is over 1 lakh crore; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore; other launch projects about 50,000 to 60,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the equity placement at 341 per share?
qa_highlights.answer: It was cancelled because the market did not support the preference share issue; management is now looking at a QIP instead.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 6,000 crore asset-debt raise authorised last year been done?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not raised yet; the company is still trying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sunstream City plan and financing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 acres on the Thane/Mulund seafront; environmental clearances are the main hurdle and are expected within months; capital needs and financing will be planned after approvals.

qa_highlights.answer: Collections target of INR3,000 crore; linked to construction progress under RERA, with Q2 to Q4 inflows from 25 South, 25 West, Ghatkopar and Chembur OC-related receipts.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding after mergers and pledge status?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding expected around 68%; two promoter pledges continuing, with management aiming to release them in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to address low ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited refinancing at lower rates, rising realisations and deliveries as drivers of ROE improvement; no specific ROE target given.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness from completion-method accounting; reported earnings may stay weak until OCs and handovers in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Merger completion depends on NCLT sanction and third scheme approval; merging entities carry about INR3,956 crore of borrowings.
Pre-sales of INR6,000 crore guidance is heavily back-ended into Q3-Q4 and depends on launch timing (Downtown Tower 5, Thane, 25 Estates, Chembur).
Cost of debt of 14-20% and refinancing of about INR2,800 crore not yet secured.
Mid-segment walk-ins muted at Ghatkopar and Andheri; luxury exposure concentrates demand risk.
Promoter pledges still outstanding; promoter holding target stated inconsistently (68% vs 70%).
key_quotes: While the project completion method means reported earnings may not always reflect the underlying momentum of the business, but still, it shows the strong collections and strong sales.
We are looking at refinancing practically entire portfolio, which is at a higher cost as on today with us, including entities to be merged, which is in the range of around INR2,800 crores.
Cost of debt is in around -- it varies from 14% to 20%.
I would not back on averages, but it depends upon which site it is? Where it is? So, but as on today, it is from 14% to 20%.
Yes, we have enabling resolutions available with us on a preferential issue and/or on a QIP, including FCCB. But we are waiting for the right time to launch those.
532799|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the pipeline, pricing and Hubtown 2.0 merger, but noticeably cautious on near-term reported earnings, refinancing terms and fundraise timing, which management repeatedly deferred until markets or term sheets improve. Answers on promoter stake (68% vs 70%) and the cost of debt average were vague or inconsistent.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management cites refinancing of ~INR2,800 cr debt at 14-20% cost and rising realisations (25 South ~INR25,000/sq ft, further INR15,000-20,000 rise expected) as ROE drivers, but refinancing term sheets are not finalised and Q1 PBT was flat QoQ at INR32 cr.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ongoing development area ~7.13 mn sq ft rising to 34+ mn sq ft post-merger, with Chembur phase 2 (Q3-Q4 FY27), Downtown Tower 5 (Oct-Nov 2026) and 25 Estates (Q4 FY27) planned, but the bulk of the area expansion depends on NCLT sanction of mergers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 area sold was flat YoY and mid-segment walk-ins are muted, so volume growth hinges on the Q3-Q4 launch cluster (Downtown Tower 5, Chembur phase 2, 25 Estates, 25 Chalets) that drives the INR6,000 cr pre-sales guide.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Pre-sales guidance of ~INR6,000 cr is new and heavily back-ended to Q3-Q4 with launch timing dependent; Q1 pre-sales of INR535 cr and flat YoY area sold give no early evidence to lift it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue is lumpy on completion accounting with OCs and handovers concentrated in Q3-Q4 FY27, Q1 revenue fell 17% YoY to INR156 cr, and pre-sales depend on launches and on merger approvals.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Named launches are planned: Downtown Tower 5 and floors 51-85 from Oct-Nov 2026, Chembur phase 2 in Q3-Q4 FY27, 25 Estates in Q4 FY27 pending approvals, and 25 Chalets toward end FY27.

rows.label: Contracted pipeline INR11,583 cr yet to be recognised
rows.when: over 2-4 quarters as OCs and handovers occur
rows.why: Pipeline of INR11,583 cr sits behind INR3,252 cr already recognised out of INR14,835 cr ongoing pre-sales, but recognition is subject to statutory merger approvals and OC timing (25 South final tower by Mar 2027, Rising City and Premiere OCs in FY27).

rows.label: Refinancing of ~INR2,800 cr high-cost debt and FCCB/equity option
rows.why: Cost of debt is 14-20% and term sheets are not yet finalised; a USD150 mn (~INR1,400 cr) FCCB is discussed but timing awaits better markets, with a net debt-free target by FY2031.

rows.label: Price increases at Downtown higher floors and 25 South
rows.why: 25 South prices rose to ~INR25,000/sq ft within a year with a further INR15,000-20,000/sq ft expected, and higher floors carry a 30-40% premium over lower floors.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline, pricing and the Hubtown 2.0 merger but cautious on near-term reported earnings, refinancing terms and fundraise timing; analysts probed collections decline, cost of debt, promoter stake (68% vs 70%) and pledges, and answers on those were vague.
